questions.q: A payroll clerk accidentally enters 400 instead of 40 in the hours-worked field for an hourly employee. Which input control would most likely prevent this error from being processed?
choices: Limit check
Sequence check
Field check
Validity check
questions.exp: A limit check rejects values exceeding a predetermined maximum, such as 60 hours per week. A field check only verifies the data type (e.g., numeric), and 400 is still numeric.

questions.q: When a sales clerk enters a customer number, the system displays the customer's name and address so the clerk can confirm the correct account before proceeding. This control is best described as:
choices: Hash total
Closed-loop verification
Check digit verification
Completeness check
questions.exp: Closed-loop verification displays related data retrieved from the master file so the user can confirm the input is correct. A check digit would detect transposed digits arithmetically but would not show the user the matching record.

questions.q: A distributor's order entry system rejects any order whose product code does not exist in the inventory master file. This is an example of a:
choices: Sign check
Reasonableness check
Range check
Validity check
questions.exp: A validity check compares input with a master file or table of valid values. A range check tests whether a value falls between limits, which is not meaningful for product codes.

questions.q: A data entry clerk transposes two digits of a vendor account number, keying 4325 instead of 4235. Which control is specifically designed to detect this type of error in identification numbers?
choices: Check digit
Record count
Run-to-run total
Limit check
questions.exp: A check digit is calculated from the other digits of an identifier, so transpositions and transcription errors produce a mismatch. A record count would still show the same number of records and would not detect the error.

questions.q: A batch of 50 vendor invoices is submitted for processing. The clerk computes the sum of the vendor account numbers on the invoices and the system compares it to the sum of processed account numbers. This total is a:
choices: Cross-footing balance
Record count
Hash total
Financial total
questions.exp: A hash total sums a field that has no inherent meaning, such as account numbers, to detect lost, added or altered records. A financial total sums a meaningful amount, such as invoice dollars.

questions.q: An insurer's claims system rejects a claim for a pregnancy-related procedure if the policyholder is recorded as male. Which control is this?
choices: Limit check
Sequence check
Reasonableness (logic) check
Field check
questions.exp: A reasonableness or logic check tests whether data are consistent with related fields. A limit check compares a single field to a maximum and cannot detect an inconsistency between two fields.

questions.q: A company's system compares the total of records processed at each stage of a multi-step nightly batch with the total from the previous stage. This processing control is a:
choices: Validity check
Run-to-run control total
Key verification
Closed-loop verification
questions.exp: Run-to-run totals verify that data remain complete and unaltered as they move between processing steps. Closed-loop verification is an input control performed by the user at entry.

questions.q: An auditor wants to verify that the client's payroll program correctly calculates overtime. The auditor prepares fictitious transactions, including invalid ones, processes them through the client's program under the auditor's control, and compares results to expected outcomes. This technique is:
choices: Test data
Parallel simulation
Embedded audit module
Integrated test facility
questions.exp: Test data involves processing auditor-prepared transactions through the client's program, usually separate from live processing. Parallel simulation instead runs actual client data through an auditor-controlled program.

questions.q: An auditor processes the client's actual payroll data through an auditor-developed program that replicates the client's overtime logic, then compares the output to the client's results. This technique is:
choices: Test data
Integrated test facility
Parallel simulation
Tagging and tracing
questions.exp: Parallel simulation reprocesses real client data with an auditor-controlled program and compares results. Test data runs fictitious data through the client's program, the reverse arrangement.

questions.q: An auditor creates a fictitious division in the client's live accounts receivable system and processes test transactions against it alongside regular transactions. Which technique is this, and what is its main risk?
choices: Integrated test facility; fictitious transactions may contaminate live data if not removed
Parallel simulation; the auditor's program may differ from the client's
Test data; the program used may not be the production version
Embedded audit module; excessive alerts
questions.exp: An integrated test facility uses dummy entities within the live system, so the test transactions must be carefully reversed or excluded to avoid misstating real records. Test data, by contrast, is typically run separately from live processing.

questions.q: A company wants continuous monitoring of transactions exceeding $100,000, with qualifying transactions written to an audit file as they are processed. Which technique is most appropriate?
choices: Generalized audit software applied annually
Test data
Parallel simulation
Embedded audit module
questions.exp: Embedded audit modules are programmed into the application to capture transactions meeting criteria during live processing, enabling continuous monitoring. Annual use of generalized audit software is periodic, not continuous.

questions.q: A purchasing system automatically matches the purchase order, receiving report and vendor invoice and holds invoices for review when quantities or prices differ beyond a tolerance. The most significant risk this control mitigates is:
choices: Recording sales in the wrong period
Errors in depreciation calculations
Unauthorized changes to payroll rates
Paying for goods not ordered or not received, or at unauthorized prices
questions.exp: The automated three-way match ensures payment only for goods ordered and received at agreed prices. It does not address revenue cut-off or payroll, which are different transaction cycles.

questions.q: A cash disbursements system rejects any check request where the vendor and invoice number combination has already been paid. This control primarily addresses which assertion for accounts payable and cash?
choices: Valuation of inventory
Occurrence, by preventing duplicate payments
Presentation
Completeness of liabilities
questions.exp: Duplicate payment checks prevent recording and paying the same invoice twice, which addresses occurrence of disbursements. Completeness concerns omitted transactions, the opposite risk.

questions.q: A company's billing interface sends daily shipment data from the warehouse system to the billing system. Which control best ensures all shipments are billed?
choices: Encrypting the interface file
Requiring passwords for the billing system
Monthly review of the revenue budget
Reconciling the record count and total quantity sent by the warehouse system to those received and billed in the billing system
questions.exp: Interface reconciliations of counts and totals between sending and receiving systems ensure completeness of transferred data. Encryption protects confidentiality and integrity in transit but does not detect records that were never sent or loaded.

questions.q: Customer orders are prenumbered by the system, and a daily report lists gaps and duplicates in the numbering sequence. This control most directly addresses:
choices: Accuracy of prices
Valuation of receivables
Authorization of credit limits
Completeness of processing and detection of duplicates
questions.exp: Sequence checks identify missing or duplicate document numbers, supporting completeness and preventing double processing. Price accuracy would be addressed by validity checks against the price master file.

questions.q: Which control is most effective for preventing unauthorized changes to the vendor master file, such as a fraudulent change of a vendor's bank account number?
choices: Sequence checks on purchase orders
A limit check on invoice amounts
Run-to-run totals in the payment batch
Restricting master file update access and independently reviewing a report of all master file changes
questions.exp: Master data are used by every transaction, so restricting who can change them and reviewing change reports is key to preventing payment redirection fraud. Limit checks on invoice amounts would not detect a changed bank account.

questions.q: A data entry system requires a second operator to rekey the same source documents, and the system flags any differences between the two entries. This control is:
choices: Key verification
Hash total
Closed-loop verification
Check digit
questions.exp: Key verification (double keying) detects data entry errors by comparing two independent entries. Closed-loop verification shows related master data to the person entering, without a second keying.

questions.q: A web form for new customer accounts will not submit until the tax ID, address and credit limit fields are populated. This is a:
choices: Sign check
Completeness check
Validity check
Reasonableness check
questions.exp: A completeness check ensures all required fields contain data before processing. A validity check would compare entered values against acceptable values, which is a different test.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an IT-dependent manual control?
choices: An input edit that rejects alphabetic characters in a numeric field
A controller's review of a system-generated aged receivables report to identify accounts needing an allowance
A system configuration that prevents users from approving their own journal entries
An automated calculation of sales tax
questions.exp: An IT-dependent manual control is performed by a person but relies on system-generated information, so its effectiveness depends on the report's completeness and accuracy. The other choices are fully automated controls.

questions.q: Errors detected by edit checks in a batch are written to a suspense file. Which control is most important for this suspense file?
choices: Monitoring the file so errors are corrected and resubmitted timely and the file is aged and reviewed
Restricting the file to read-only for all users
Deleting the file at month end
Excluding the file from backups
questions.exp: Error correction and resubmission controls ensure rejected transactions are not lost, preserving completeness. Deleting the suspense file would permanently lose valid transactions that need correction.

questions.q: A loan system automatically calculates interest on each loan using the rate stored in the loan master record. Which test is most appropriate for an auditor to evaluate this automated control?
choices: Review the board minutes for rate approvals
Recalculate interest for one or a few loans of each relevant type and confirm the related ITGCs are effective
Recalculate interest for a statistical sample of 300 loans
Inquire of loan officers
questions.exp: Automated controls process consistently, so testing one or a few instances per relevant variation is generally sufficient when ITGCs are effective. Large samples are typical of manual controls, which can fail inconsistently.

questions.q: An order entry screen offers a drop-down menu of valid shipping methods rather than a free-text field. This preformatting control primarily:
choices: Corrects errors automatically
Prevents invalid data from being entered
Detects errors after processing
Encrypts input data
questions.exp: Drop-down menus and other preformatted fields limit entries to valid options, preventing errors at input. Detective controls identify errors after they occur, which is not how this control works.

questions.q: A general ledger application prevents a journal entry from posting unless total debits equal total credits. This control is best described as a:
choices: Check digit
Validity check
Zero-balance (balancing) check
Range check
questions.exp: A balancing check ensures debits equal credits so that the entry nets to zero before posting. A range check compares a value with an upper and lower bound and does not compare two totals.

questions.q: The ERP system is configured so that the same user cannot both create a vendor and approve payments to that vendor. Which kind of control is this?
choices: A physical control
A detective manual control
An automated preventive application control enforcing segregation of duties
A corrective ITGC
questions.exp: Role configuration that blocks incompatible functions is an automated, preventive application control. It does not depend on someone reviewing a report after the fact, so it is not detective.

questions.q: A payment file is generated by the ERP and uploaded to the bank's portal. Which control best mitigates the risk that the file is altered between generation and upload?
choices: Saving the file to a shared drive before upload
Allowing AP clerks to edit the file to fix errors
Printing the payment file for review
Using automated secure transmission (e.g., host-to-host with hashing) and reconciling totals confirmed by the bank to the ERP totals
questions.exp: Secure automated transmission with integrity checks and reconciliation of bank-confirmed totals to ERP totals reduces the risk of tampering. Saving to a shared drive or allowing clerks to edit the file creates an opportunity to alter payee or amount data.

questions.q: In processing payroll, the system verifies that net pay is not negative before writing checks. This is an example of a:
choices: Sequence check
Sign check
Hash total
Validity check
questions.exp: A sign check verifies whether a value has the appropriate sign, such as positive net pay. A validity check compares input to a list of acceptable values rather than evaluating sign.

questions.q: Before distributing monthly management reports, the reporting team reconciles report totals to the general ledger and restricts report distribution to authorized recipients. These are examples of:
choices: Change management controls
Processing controls
Input controls
Output controls
questions.exp: Output controls ensure that output is accurate and complete (e.g., reconciliation to source) and distributed only to authorized users. Processing controls operate during the transformation of data, not on finished reports.

questions.q: A retailer's point-of-sale system compares the total sales recorded by each register to the cash and card settlements at day end. Which objective does this control primarily achieve?
choices: Prevention of unauthorized logons
Authorization of price changes
Validation of item codes at entry
Detection of discrepancies between recorded sales and amounts collected
questions.exp: Reconciling recorded sales with settlements detects missing cash, unrecorded sales or processing errors. It does not control price changes or system access.

questions.q: Two users attempt to update the same inventory record simultaneously. Which control prevents one user's update from overwriting the other's?
choices: Closed-loop verification
Hash total
Concurrent update control, such as record locking
Check digit
questions.exp: Concurrent update controls lock a record while it is being updated so that simultaneous changes do not overwrite each other. Hash totals detect batch integrity issues after processing, not concurrency conflicts.

questions.q: A company's revenue system allows sales representatives to override system-calculated prices. Which control best addresses the risk of unauthorized discounts?
choices: Increasing sales commissions
Removing the price field from invoices
Using a check digit on product codes
Requiring override approval by an authorized manager and reviewing an exception report of all overrides
questions.exp: Requiring approval and independently reviewing overrides addresses the risk that overrides are used to grant unauthorized discounts. A check digit only ensures the product code is entered correctly.

questions.q: A company implements an automated control that blocks journal entries posted to closed periods. During testing, the auditor finds the period-close setting can be reopened by any accountant. What is the main concern?
choices: Journal entries cannot be posted at all
Any accountant could reopen the period and post entries, undermining the control
The control is not automated
The control should be a manual review only
questions.exp: A configurable control is only effective if the configuration is protected; broad ability to reopen periods allows the control to be bypassed. Automation is not the problem, and a manual review would be less reliable.

questions.q: When testing an application's edit checks, an auditor submits transactions with invalid customer numbers, negative quantities and alphabetic characters in numeric fields. The auditor is testing whether:
choices: Output reports are distributed correctly
Input controls reject invalid data as designed
Data are backed up nightly
The network is secure
questions.exp: Submitting invalid transactions tests whether input edits reject them as designed. Backup and network security are ITGCs or infrastructure controls unrelated to input edit testing.

questions.q: An auditor uses generalized audit software to extract all purchase orders and identify those without a matching receiving report. Which audit procedure does this represent?
choices: An integrated test facility
A computer-assisted audit technique used for data analysis and substantive testing
Parallel simulation of the client's matching program
An embedded audit module
questions.exp: Generalized audit software (a CAAT) is used to extract and analyze client data, such as identifying exceptions across an entire population. Parallel simulation would reproduce a client program's processing logic rather than search data for exceptions.

questions.q: A bank requires customers to enter the amount twice when submitting wire transfers online, and the system rejects the request if the two entries differ. Which risk does this primarily mitigate?
choices: Accidental data entry errors in the amount
Unauthorized access to accounts
Duplicate payments to the same beneficiary
Loss of data in transmission
questions.exp: Double entry of the same field detects keying errors, similar to key verification. It does not authenticate the user, so it does not address unauthorized access.

questions.q: An application uses a range check on the discount percentage field that accepts values from 0% to 15%. A clerk enters 12% when the authorized discount was 2%. Which statement is correct?
choices: A sign check would have rejected the entry
The range check will accept the entry because it falls within the allowed range, so another control such as approval is needed
A field check would detect the error
The range check will reject the entry
questions.exp: Range checks only reject values outside the defined bounds, so a valid-looking but incorrect value passes. Field checks verify data type only, so 12 would also pass.

questions.q: Which application control is most effective in ensuring that only authorized employees are paid in a payroll run?
choices: Printing paychecks on secured stock
Validating each employee ID in the time file against the active employee master file maintained by HR
Calculating gross pay using a limit check
Comparing net pay to the prior period
questions.exp: Matching time records against an independently maintained active employee master file prevents payments to nonexistent or terminated employees. A limit check addresses the amount of pay, not whether the payee is authorized.

questions.q: Which characteristic most distinguishes automated application controls from manual controls for audit testing purposes?
choices: Manual controls are always more reliable than automated controls
Automated controls never need testing
Automated controls can only be tested by inquiry
Automated controls perform consistently when ITGCs are effective, so they can be tested with a small number of instances
questions.exp: Because automated controls execute the same logic every time, auditors can test a few instances and rely on ITGCs for consistency. They still require testing, and inquiry alone is never sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness.

questions.q: A company's sales application automatically calculates each invoice amount by multiplying quantity shipped by the price in the price master file. An auditor finds that sales staff can edit the price master file without approval. What is the most significant effect on the invoicing control?
choices: Customer credit limits will be bypassed
The calculation may be accurate arithmetically but produce invoices at unauthorized prices
The invoice calculation will produce arithmetic errors
Quantities shipped will be overstated
questions.exp: An automated calculation is only as reliable as the master data it uses, so uncontrolled price changes lead to correctly computed but unauthorized amounts. The arithmetic itself is unaffected, which is why the arithmetic-error choice is a trap.

questions.q: During a critical outage, a developer applies an emergency fix directly to production at 2 a.m. without prior approval. Which control is most appropriate for emergency changes like this?
choices: Allow the developer to approve the change personally after the fact
Prohibit all emergency changes, even if the outage continues
Require documentation, testing evidence and retroactive approval by the change authority within a defined period, followed by review of the change
Treat emergency changes as standard changes that never require approval
questions.exp: Emergency change procedures allow expedited implementation but require after-the-fact documentation, review and approval by an appropriate authority. Self-approval by the developer lacks independence and defeats the purpose of the control.

questions.q: Under ITIL, routine, low-risk changes such as adding a standard user workstation that follow a documented procedure are typically classified as:
choices: Standard (pre-authorized) changes
Unauthorized changes
Normal changes requiring full CAB review
Emergency changes
questions.exp: Standard changes are pre-authorized, low-risk, well-understood changes performed following an established procedure. Normal changes need assessment and authorization each time, and emergency changes are those needed urgently.

questions.q: Which environment setup best supports change management controls?
choices: Separate development, test and production environments, with production access restricted to authorized release personnel
Separate test and production but with developers holding production update rights
A single shared environment for development, testing and production
Developers code and test directly in production to save time
questions.exp: Separating environments and restricting production access prevents untested or unauthorized code from reaching live systems. Giving developers production rights undermines the separation even if environments exist.

questions.q: A change advisory board (CAB) reviews proposed changes. Which is its primary function?
choices: Assessing risk and impact of proposed changes and advising on authorization and scheduling
Performing user acceptance testing
Writing the code for approved changes
Migrating code to production
questions.exp: The CAB evaluates proposed changes, considering risk, impact, resources and scheduling, and advises the change authority. Writing code and migrating it are performed by developers and release personnel, respectively.

questions.q: An auditor wants assurance that the program currently running in production for payroll calculations is the authorized version. Which procedure is most effective?
choices: Inspect the CAB meeting minutes
Interview the payroll manager
Compare the production executable or code to the authorized version in the controlled source library
Review the change management policy
questions.exp: Comparing production code to the authorized version (code comparison) directly detects unauthorized modifications. Policies and minutes show intended processes but not what is actually running.

questions.q: A company's change ticket shows approval by the business owner, but the approval date is two days after the change was moved to production. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: No issue exists if the change worked
The issue relates only to documentation, not to control effectiveness
The change was not authorized before implementation, which is a control exception unless it qualified as an emergency change
The change was properly authorized because approval was obtained
questions.exp: Normal changes require approval before implementation; after-the-fact approval is an exception unless the emergency change process applied. A change functioning properly does not cure the authorization failure.

questions.q: Before implementing a major upgrade to the order management system, the release plan includes steps to restore the previous version if critical issues arise. This element is a:
choices: Change freeze
Back-out (rollback) plan
Configuration baseline
Regression test
questions.exp: A back-out plan describes how to reverse a change and restore the prior state if implementation fails. Regression testing is done before release to verify existing functions still work.

questions.q: After modifying the sales tax calculation module, the QA team reruns tests on unchanged functions such as invoicing and credit memos to ensure they still work correctly. This is:
choices: Regression testing
Unit testing of the new code only
Stress testing
Penetration testing
questions.exp: Regression testing verifies that changes did not break existing functionality. Unit testing focuses on the individual changed component, not on other functions that may be affected.

questions.q: Under NIST SP 800-53, the control family that includes baseline configurations, configuration change control and security impact analysis is:
choices: Configuration Management (CM)
Contingency Planning (CP)
System and Services Acquisition (SA)
Access Control (AC)
questions.exp: The CM family includes CM-2 Baseline Configuration, CM-3 Configuration Change Control and CM-4 Impact Analyses. SA addresses acquisition and development, including developer configuration management, but not operational change control generally.

questions.q: A company's file integrity monitoring tool alerts the security team whenever critical system files or configurations on production servers change. Which type of change management control is this?
choices: Corrective
Preventive
Detective
Directive
questions.exp: File integrity monitoring detects changes after they occur so they can be investigated against authorized change records. It does not by itself prevent changes.

questions.q: A SaaS ERP vendor pushes quarterly releases automatically to all customers. Which control is most appropriate for the customer?
choices: Block all vendor updates permanently
Assume vendor releases never affect controls
Review release notes, assess the impact on configured controls and reports, and perform regression testing in a sandbox before the release reaches production
Rely on the vendor's marketing announcements
questions.exp: Even when the vendor controls code changes, customers should assess and test releases' effects on their configurations, automated controls and reports. Blocking all updates is usually impossible in SaaS and would forgo security fixes.

questions.q: In a DevOps environment with continuous deployment, which control best replaces a manual CAB approval for each change while preserving segregation of duties?
choices: Allowing any developer to deploy directly to production
Disabling automated testing to speed deployment
Reviewing a sample of changes once a year
Branch protection rules requiring an independent peer review and passing automated tests before code can merge and deploy
questions.exp: Pipeline-enforced peer review and automated tests provide preventive, independent approval for every change. Annual sampling is too infrequent to prevent unauthorized changes.

questions.q: Which statement about a configuration management database (CMDB) is most accurate?
choices: It stores customer transaction data
It is used only for financial asset depreciation
It replaces the need for change approvals
It records configuration items and their relationships, supporting impact analysis of proposed changes
questions.exp: A CMDB tracks configuration items and their relationships, helping assess which systems a change might affect. It supports, rather than replaces, change authorization.

questions.q: An analyst uses a database tool to directly correct erroneous customer balances in the production database, bypassing the application. Which control is most important?
choices: Restricting such access to developers only
Requiring data changes to be requested, approved by the data owner, performed by authorized personnel, logged and reviewed
Performing corrections only at night
Allowing such corrections without documentation because they fix errors
questions.exp: Direct data fixes bypass application controls, so they need the same discipline as program changes: authorization, restricted execution, logging and review. Restricting the access to developers would worsen segregation of duties.

questions.q: A company implements a change freeze during the last two weeks of its fiscal year. What is the primary purpose?
choices: To reduce IT staffing costs
To reduce the risk that changes disrupt critical year-end processing and reporting
To force all changes to be emergency changes
To allow developers to take vacation
questions.exp: Change freezes limit the risk of disruption during critical business periods, such as financial close. They do not convert all changes into emergency changes; only genuinely urgent changes should be processed through the emergency process.

questions.q: An auditor selects a sample of changes from the change ticketing system and finds all were approved and tested. Why might this test be insufficient?
choices: Approval is not a relevant attribute
Testing evidence is never required
Changes made outside the ticketing system would not be in the population, so completeness of the population was not tested
The sample size is irrelevant for change testing
questions.exp: If changes can bypass the ticketing system, sampling from it cannot detect unauthorized changes; the auditor should test completeness, for example from system change logs. Approval and testing remain relevant attributes.

questions.q: Developers check out source code from a version control system, and every modification is recorded with the developer's identity and a description. Which risk is primarily mitigated?
choices: Excessive storage costs
Weak passwords
Network denial-of-service attacks
Untracked or conflicting code modifications and loss of the ability to identify who changed what
questions.exp: Version control maintains history, accountability and integrity of source code changes. It does not address network attacks or authentication strength.

questions.q: A security impact analysis is performed before approving a change to the firewall ruleset. What is the main goal?
choices: Training users on the new rules
Ensuring the change is completed within the budget
Determining whether the change could introduce vulnerabilities or weaken existing security controls
Measuring network throughput
questions.exp: Security impact analysis (SP 800-53 CM-4) evaluates how a change could affect security before it is implemented. Budget and throughput are operational concerns, not security impact.

questions.q: Which situation represents the most serious change management deficiency?
choices: Change tickets use inconsistent formatting
The CAB meets weekly instead of daily
The same developer can write, test, approve and deploy changes to the financial application
Some low-risk changes are classified as standard changes
questions.exp: A single individual controlling the whole change lifecycle can introduce unauthorized changes undetected, a fundamental segregation of duties failure. Formatting and meeting frequency are minor process issues.

questions.q: A company uses infrastructure as code (IaC) templates to provision cloud servers. Which control most effectively governs changes to infrastructure?
choices: Storing IaC templates in version control with peer review and automated policy checks before deployment
Allowing engineers to change cloud consoles manually
Reviewing cloud invoices monthly
Disabling cloud audit logs
questions.exp: Treating infrastructure definitions as code allows standard change controls such as version control, peer review and automated checks. Manual console changes bypass those controls and cause configuration drift.

questions.q: After a change is implemented, the business owner confirms that the change achieved its intended results and that no unexpected issues occurred. This is called:
choices: Impact analysis
Post-implementation review
Change freeze
Unit testing
questions.exp: A post-implementation review evaluates whether the change met objectives and identifies lessons learned. Impact analysis happens before approval, not after implementation.

questions.q: Which control most directly ensures that changes are tested by someone other than the developer who made them?
choices: Version control check-in
Independent quality assurance or user acceptance testing with documented sign-off
Automated backups
File integrity monitoring
questions.exp: Independent QA or UAT sign-off provides objective evidence that changes work as intended and meet requirements. Version control tracks changes but does not test them.

questions.q: A company's ERP allows finance users to change configuration settings, such as approval thresholds, directly in production. Which statement is correct?
choices: Configuration changes are always low risk
Configuration changes that affect controls should be subject to authorization, testing where appropriate, and logging and review
Only IT can create risks through configuration
Configuration changes are exempt from change management because no code is changed
questions.exp: Configuration settings can alter how automated controls function, so changes should follow change management principles even though no code is modified. Treating them as exempt is a common trap.

questions.q: Operating system patches for production servers are deployed monthly. Which practice best balances security and stability?
choices: Delaying all patches until the annual maintenance window
Applying patches only when users complain
Deploying all patches immediately to production without testing
Risk-based prioritization, testing in a non-production environment, approval and scheduled deployment, with an expedited path for critical vulnerabilities
questions.exp: A risk-based patch process tests patches before production while allowing expedited handling of critical, actively exploited vulnerabilities. Waiting until an annual window leaves known vulnerabilities exposed for too long.

questions.q: COBIT 2019 addresses change management primarily through which management objective?
choices: BAI06 Managed I&T changes
DSS02 Managed service requests and incidents
APO12 Managed risk
MEA01 Managed performance and conformance monitoring
questions.exp: BAI06 Managed I&T changes covers managing all changes in a controlled manner, including standard and emergency changes. DSS02 handles incidents and service requests, which may trigger changes but do not govern them.

questions.q: An organization maintains approved baseline configurations for servers and periodically scans servers to identify deviations. What is the primary benefit?
choices: Elimination of the need for patching
Detection of unauthorized or undocumented changes (configuration drift)
Faster user logons
Reduced software licensing costs
questions.exp: Comparing systems against approved baselines (SP 800-53 CM-2) detects drift caused by unauthorized or undocumented changes. Baselines do not replace patching, which updates the baseline itself.

questions.q: Which evidence best demonstrates that a program change was tested before implementation?
choices: Documented test cases and results with sign-off by the tester dated before the production deployment date
The change request form showing the requester's name
A developer's verbal statement that testing occurred
The production deployment log
questions.exp: Dated test documentation and sign-off before deployment provide objective evidence of testing. Verbal statements and deployment logs do not show that testing occurred or was successful.

questions.q: A company outsources development of a custom module to a vendor. Which change control is most important when the vendor delivers code updates?
choices: Disabling logging during vendor deployments
The company's own testing and approval of vendor-delivered code before migration to production by the company's authorized personnel
Allowing the vendor to deploy directly to production
Accepting the vendor's assurance that the code was tested
questions.exp: Vendor-delivered changes should go through the company's own testing, approval and controlled migration. Relying solely on the vendor's assurance or giving it direct production access removes the company's control over its environment.

questions.q: A financial institution requires that changes to critical systems be scheduled outside business hours and communicated to affected users in advance. Which risk is primarily mitigated?
choices: Insider fraud
Business disruption and unexpected impacts on users during implementation
Weak encryption
Unauthorized code changes
questions.exp: Scheduling and communication reduce operational disruption from change implementation. They do not address whether the change itself was authorized.

questions.q: Under COBIT 2019, which management objective covers formally accepting and transitioning new or changed solutions into operation, including acceptance testing and post-implementation review?
choices: DSS01 Managed operations
BAI07 Managed I&T change acceptance and transitioning
APO11 Managed quality
BAI03 Managed solutions identification and build
questions.exp: BAI07 covers acceptance testing, promotion to production and post-implementation review. BAI03 addresses designing and building solutions, which comes before acceptance and transition.

questions.q: A help desk technician can modify user roles in production when users call with urgent requests, without a ticket. What is the primary risk?
choices: Help desk performance metrics will decline
Users will receive training late
Unauthorized access changes could be made without approval or an audit trail
System performance will degrade
questions.exp: Access changes without tickets lack authorization and traceability, creating risk of inappropriate access. The issue is control over changes to security settings, not performance or training.

questions.q: Which control best detects unauthorized changes to programs in production after they occur?
choices: Approved change requests
Requiring CAB approval for all changes
Periodic comparison of production program versions to authorized versions and review of change logs against approved tickets
Restricting developer access to production
questions.exp: Comparisons and reconciliations of actual changes to approved changes detect changes that bypassed the process. CAB approval and access restrictions are preventive controls.

questions.q: In a well-designed change process, who should normally migrate approved and tested code into production?
choices: The end user who requested the change
A release manager or operations function independent of development, or an automated pipeline that enforces approvals
The developer who wrote the code
Any member of the IT department
questions.exp: Independent migration, by a separate function or an automated, controlled pipeline, ensures only approved code reaches production. Developer migration reintroduces the segregation of duties risk.

questions.q: A company's change policy requires risk categorization of each change. Which change is most appropriately categorized as high risk?
choices: Modifying the revenue recognition logic in the ERP
Adding a printer to a department
Changing the color scheme of an internal dashboard
Updating the company logo on the intranet
questions.exp: Changes to logic that affects financial reporting have significant potential impact and warrant rigorous testing and approval. Cosmetic and peripheral changes are low risk.

questions.q: An organization requires documentation of each change to be updated (e.g., system manuals, run books, configuration records) as part of closing the change ticket. What is the main benefit?
choices: Shortening approval cycles
Eliminating the need for testing
Reducing the number of changes
Keeping documentation accurate for operations, support, troubleshooting and future changes
questions.exp: Current documentation supports reliable operations and accurate impact analysis for future changes. It does not replace testing or reduce the number of changes.

questions.q: A change to the payroll system was approved and tested, but the version actually deployed differed from the tested version due to a packaging error. Which control would most likely have prevented this?
choices: Building deployment packages from the controlled repository with integrity checks (e.g., hashes) verifying that the tested build is the one deployed
Testing changes in production only
Requiring users to approve changes twice
Increasing the number of CAB members
questions.exp: Promoting the same build artifact, verified by hash, from test to production ensures what was tested is what is deployed. More approvals do not prevent a mismatch between tested and deployed code.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between incident management and change management?
choices: Change management replaces incident management
Resolving an incident may require a change, which should be handled through the change management process, emergency or normal
Incident tickets automatically authorize any change
Incidents never require changes
questions.exp: Incident resolution often needs a change, and that change must still be controlled through the appropriate change process. An incident ticket does not by itself authorize arbitrary changes.

questions.q: While testing program changes for an ICFR audit, an auditor finds one production change to the billing application with no change ticket, approval or test evidence. What is the most appropriate next step?
choices: Ask the developer to create a ticket now so the file is complete
Determine the nature and effect of the change, whether it affected relevant controls or data, and whether other unauthorized changes may exist, and evaluate the deficiency
Ignore the change because it is a single exception
Conclude immediately that the financial statements are materially misstated
questions.exp: An unauthorized change is a control exception that requires understanding its cause and effect and evaluating whether the change process can be relied on. Creating a ticket after the fact hides the deficiency rather than addressing it.

questions.q: A customer database is valued at $500,000. A successful breach is expected to destroy 40% of its value, and such a breach is expected to occur once every four years. What is the annualized loss expectancy (ALE)?
questions.exp: Single loss expectancy = asset value x exposure factor = $500,000 x 40% = $200,000; ALE = SLE x annualized rate of occurrence = $200,000 x 0.25 = $50,000. The $200,000 figure is the SLE, which ignores how often the event occurs.

questions.q: A company's current ALE for ransomware is $120,000. A proposed endpoint detection and response tool would reduce the ALE to $30,000 and costs $50,000 per year. What is the annual net benefit of the control, and should it be implemented on a cost-benefit basis?
questions.exp: Net benefit = (ALE before - ALE after) - annual control cost = ($120,000 - $30,000) - $50,000 = $40,000, so the control is cost-justified. The $90,000 figure is the gross risk reduction before subtracting the control's cost.

questions.q: A successful attack on a company's e-commerce site would cause a loss of $75,000 and is expected to occur once every five years. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
questions.exp: The annualized rate of occurrence is 1/5 = 0.2, so ALE = $75,000 x 0.2 = $15,000. Multiplying by five instead of dividing produces the $375,000 trap.

questions.q: A data breach would cause a single loss of $200,000. A proposed control would reduce the annualized rate of occurrence from 0.5 to 0.1. What is the maximum annual cost the company could justify spending on this control?
questions.exp: ALE falls from $200,000 x 0.5 = $100,000 to $200,000 x 0.1 = $20,000, a reduction of $80,000, which is the most the control can cost annually and still break even. $100,000 is the original ALE and assumes the control eliminates all risk.

questions.q: A server with an asset value of $2,000,000 suffers an outage that causes a $300,000 loss. What exposure factor does this represent?
questions.exp: Exposure factor = loss / asset value = $300,000 / $2,000,000 = 15%. Dividing the asset value by the loss (about 6.7 times) inverts the formula.

questions.q: A retailer purchases a cyber insurance policy that covers breach notification costs, forensic investigations, and regulatory fines where insurable. Which risk response does this represent?
choices: Risk acceptance
Risk mitigation
Risk avoidance
Risk transfer (sharing)
questions.exp: Insurance shifts part of the financial impact to a third party, which is risk transfer or sharing. It does not reduce the likelihood of a breach, so it is not mitigation.

questions.q: After evaluating the cost of securing stored payment card data, a specialty retailer decides to stop storing card numbers altogether and to stop offering in-store credit accounts. Which risk response has the retailer chosen?
choices: Risk mitigation
Risk acceptance
Risk transfer
Risk avoidance
questions.exp: Eliminating the activity that gives rise to the risk is avoidance. Mitigation would keep the activity but add controls to reduce likelihood or impact.

questions.q: After management implemented controls over a payroll application, the risk team estimated the remaining risk exposure. What should management compare this residual risk with to decide whether further action is needed?
choices: The organization's risk appetite and tolerance
The inherent risk before controls
The industry average number of breaches
The cost of the existing controls
questions.exp: Residual risk is evaluated against risk appetite and tolerance: if it exceeds tolerance, further response is needed. Comparing residual with inherent risk shows how effective the controls are, but not whether the remaining risk is acceptable.

questions.q: A risk assessment notes that an internet-facing server is running software with a known, unpatched flaw, and that a criminal group is actively targeting that flaw. In risk terminology, the unpatched flaw and the criminal group are, respectively:
choices: An impact and a likelihood
A control and a risk
A vulnerability and a threat
A threat and a vulnerability
questions.exp: A vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited, and a threat is a source or event with the potential to cause harm by exploiting it. Risk arises from the combination of the two together with impact.

questions.q: An accounts payable clerk receives an email that appears to come from the CFO, urgently requesting that a vendor payment be sent to a new bank account before the end of the day. Which control would best prevent a loss from this business email compromise attempt?
choices: Encrypting all email messages sent by executives
Requiring out-of-band verification of payment changes by calling the requester at a known, independently obtained phone number
Requiring the CFO to send such requests only during business hours
Increasing the spam filter's sensitivity
questions.exp: Callback verification through an independent channel defeats spoofed or compromised email because the attacker does not control the known phone number. Encrypting email protects confidentiality but does not verify the authenticity of an instruction from a compromised or spoofed account.

questions.q: Attackers obtained usernames and passwords from a breach of an unrelated social media site and used automated tools to log in to a company's customer portal, succeeding wherever customers had reused passwords. Which control would most effectively prevent this attack?
choices: Encrypting the portal database
Annual penetration testing of the portal
Requiring passwords to be changed every 30 days
Multifactor authentication for portal logins
questions.exp: Credential stuffing relies on valid reused passwords; MFA requires a second factor the attacker does not have. Periodic password changes do not stop an attacker who already has the current, reused password.

questions.q: A penetration test shows that an attacker can enter ' OR '1'='1 into a web application's login field and retrieve all customer records. Which control best remediates this vulnerability?
choices: Requiring stronger user passwords
Adding a CAPTCHA to the login page
Encrypting the customer records at rest
Using parameterized queries and server-side input validation
questions.exp: This is SQL injection, which is prevented by parameterized (prepared) statements that treat user input as data rather than executable code, supported by input validation. Encryption at rest does not help because the application decrypts data when the injected query runs.

questions.q: Security researchers disclose a zero-day vulnerability in a company's internet-facing file transfer software; no vendor patch is yet available. Which action is most appropriate in the meantime?
choices: Immediately replace the software with a competing product
Wait for the vendor patch before taking any action
Apply compensating controls such as restricting access, adding web application firewall rules, and heightening monitoring of the affected system
Accept the risk because zero-day vulnerabilities cannot be addressed
questions.exp: When no patch exists, compensating controls (virtual patching, network restrictions, enhanced monitoring, or temporarily disabling the service) reduce exposure. Simply waiting or accepting the risk ignores practical mitigations available now.

questions.q: A vulnerability scan identifies two findings: a CVSS 9.8 vulnerability on an isolated test server with no sensitive data, and a CVSS 7.5 vulnerability that is listed as actively exploited on the internet-facing payment server. Which should be remediated first?
choices: The payment server, because active exploitation and asset criticality make its risk higher
Both simultaneously, because all vulnerabilities above 7.0 have equal priority
The test server, because it has the higher CVSS score
Neither, until the next quarterly patch cycle
questions.exp: CVSS measures technical severity, but risk-based prioritization also considers exploitability in the wild (such as CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog), exposure, and asset criticality. Ranking solely by CVSS score is the common trap.

questions.q: Management wants to know not only which weaknesses exist in its network but whether an attacker could actually chain them together to reach the general ledger database. Which activity best provides this information?
choices: A review of the firewall rule set
A security awareness survey
An automated vulnerability scan
A penetration test
questions.exp: A penetration test attempts to exploit weaknesses as an attacker would, demonstrating actual paths to sensitive assets. A vulnerability scan identifies potential weaknesses but does not prove they can be exploited.

questions.q: Before an outside firm begins a penetration test of a company's production systems, which step is most important?
choices: Notifying all employees of the exact test dates
Disabling the intrusion detection system for the test period
Providing the testers with all administrator passwords
Obtaining written authorization from management that defines scope, timing, and rules of engagement
questions.exp: Written authorization and rules of engagement define what may be tested and how, protecting both parties and preventing unintended disruption. Disabling detection controls would prevent the organization from learning whether its monitoring works.

questions.q: A company wants a network security device that not only alerts on malicious traffic but automatically drops it before it reaches internal servers. Which device should it deploy?
choices: A security information and event management system
An inline intrusion prevention system
A network-based intrusion detection system deployed on a mirror port
A honeypot
questions.exp: An IPS sits inline and can block malicious traffic in real time, which is preventive. An IDS monitoring a copy of traffic can only detect and alert.

questions.q: Once remote employees connect through the company VPN, they can reach nearly every internal system. The CISO wants each access request evaluated based on user identity, device health, and context, regardless of network location. Which security model is the CISO describing?
choices: Security through obscurity
Discretionary access control
Perimeter-based security
Zero trust architecture
questions.exp: Zero trust (NIST SP 800-207) removes implicit trust based on network location and continuously verifies identity, device, and context for each resource. The current VPN design is the perimeter model that zero trust replaces.

questions.q: System administrators at a company share a single domain administrator account whose password has not changed in two years. Which control best addresses this risk?
choices: Requiring administrators to sign a confidentiality agreement
Changing the shared password once per year
A privileged access management solution with individual accounts, password vaulting and rotation, just-in-time elevation, and session logging
Reviewing the administrators' job descriptions
questions.exp: PAM establishes individual accountability, limits standing privilege, rotates credentials, and records privileged sessions. Annual password changes keep the shared account, so actions still cannot be traced to an individual.

questions.q: Ransomware that infected one workstation in the shipping department spread within hours to servers in finance, HR, and manufacturing. Which control would most directly have limited the spread?
choices: Daily vulnerability scans of the shipping department
Moving the company website to a cloud host
Network segmentation that restricts traffic between business units and to critical servers
Longer password requirements
questions.exp: Segmentation limits lateral movement so a compromise in one zone cannot freely reach others. Password length does little against malware that spreads through network services and harvested credentials.

questions.q: A company's security strategy places firewalls at the perimeter, endpoint protection on devices, multifactor authentication for applications, encryption of sensitive data, and continuous monitoring. Which principle does this design reflect?
choices: Security through obscurity
Defense in depth
Single point of control
Separation of duties
questions.exp: Defense in depth layers multiple independent controls so the failure of one does not expose the asset. Separation of duties divides incompatible tasks among people rather than layering technical safeguards.

questions.q: A publicly traded company determines on Monday that a cybersecurity incident discovered two weeks earlier is material. Under SEC rules, when must it file a Form 8-K (Item 1.05) disclosing the incident, absent a national security delay?
choices: In its next quarterly Form 10-Q
Within 30 calendar days after determining materiality
Within four business days after determining that the incident is material
Within four business days after discovering the incident
questions.exp: Item 1.05 requires disclosure within four business days of the materiality determination, which must be made without unreasonable delay after discovery. Counting from discovery is the common trap.

questions.q: Under SEC Regulation S-K Item 106, what must a public company describe annually in its Form 10-K regarding cybersecurity?
choices: Its processes for assessing, identifying, and managing material cybersecurity risks, and the board's oversight and management's role in managing those risks
Every cybersecurity incident that occurred during the year, regardless of materiality
The names of all vendors that provide security software
The technical specifications of its firewalls and encryption
questions.exp: Item 106 requires annual disclosure of risk management processes, strategy, and governance, including board oversight and management's expertise. It does not require technical details that could aid attackers, and incident reporting is on Form 8-K for material incidents.

questions.q: Investors and the board of a manufacturing company want an independent CPA report, suitable for general use, on the company's entity-wide cybersecurity risk management program. Which engagement best meets this need?
choices: An agreed-upon procedures engagement on firewall settings
A SOC 2 Type 2 examination restricted to user entities
A SOC 1 Type 2 examination
A SOC for Cybersecurity (cybersecurity risk management) examination
questions.exp: The AICPA cybersecurity risk management examination reports on an entity-wide program and is designed for general use by a broad range of stakeholders. SOC 2 reports address a service organization's system and are intended for knowledgeable users with restricted distribution.

questions.q: After purchasing a cyber insurance policy, the CEO tells the board that cybersecurity risk has been eliminated. Which response is most accurate?
choices: Insurance transfers some financial losses, but operational disruption, reputational harm, uninsured amounts, and exclusions remain as residual risk
Insurance eliminates risk only if the policy has no deductible
Insurance converts the risk into an avoided risk
The CEO is correct because the insurer assumes all losses
questions.exp: Transfer shares part of the financial impact but does not reduce the likelihood of an incident or cover reputational damage, deductibles, limits, and exclusions. Avoidance would require stopping the activity altogether.

questions.q: An attacker calls the IT help desk pretending to be a traveling sales executive who lost his phone and persuades the technician to reset the executive's multifactor authentication enrollment. Which control would best prevent this?
choices: Requiring all executives to use longer passwords
Installing endpoint protection on the help desk's computers
Strong identity verification procedures for credential and MFA resets, such as callback to a number on file or manager approval
Encrypting help desk ticket data
questions.exp: This pretexting attack exploits weak reset procedures; rigorous identity proofing before resets closes the gap. Longer passwords do nothing when the attacker bypasses authentication through the help desk.

questions.q: A company runs monthly simulated phishing campaigns. Which combination of metrics would best indicate improvement in the workforce's resistance to phishing?
choices: The number of phishing emails blocked by the spam filter
The percentage of employees who opened the email
A declining click rate together with an increasing rate of employees reporting the simulated phish
The number of training videos produced
questions.exp: Falling click rates and rising report rates show that employees both avoid and actively escalate suspicious messages. Spam filter blocks measure a technical control, not employee behavior.

questions.q: A security team places a decoy server on the network that has no legitimate business use and logs all connection attempts. Any interaction with it is treated as suspicious. What is this device?
choices: A bastion host
A proxy server
A honeypot
A demilitarized zone
questions.exp: A honeypot is a decoy designed to attract attackers, detect unauthorized activity, and study attacker techniques. A bastion host is a hardened system that provides legitimate access to services from untrusted networks.

questions.q: A critical operating system patch addressing an actively exploited vulnerability is released. The company's change management policy normally requires two weeks of testing. What is the most appropriate approach?
choices: Apply the patch immediately to all production systems without any testing or documentation
Skip the patch because it has not been tested
Use a documented emergency change process with expedited testing and approval, followed by post-implementation review
Wait the full two weeks to follow the normal change process
questions.exp: Emergency change procedures balance speed with control: expedited testing and authorization, documentation, and after-the-fact review. Bypassing change management entirely risks outages and unauthorized changes, while waiting leaves an actively exploited hole open.

questions.q: The finance team has adopted several cloud applications without IT approval, and the CISO has no inventory of where company data is stored. Which tool would best help discover and govern this shadow IT?
choices: A database activity monitor
A cloud access security broker (CASB)
A hardware asset tagging program
An intrusion detection system on the data center network
questions.exp: A CASB analyzes traffic to cloud services to discover unsanctioned applications and enforce data security policies. Hardware asset tags do not reveal software-as-a-service subscriptions.

questions.q: A company's risk register lists 40 cybersecurity risks, but no individual is assigned to any of them and several have remained untreated for over a year. Which improvement would most directly address this weakness?
choices: Purchasing a larger cyber insurance policy
Adding more risks to the register
Converting all risk ratings from qualitative to quantitative
Assigning a risk owner accountable for the response and monitoring of each risk
questions.exp: Accountable risk owners ensure that treatment decisions are made and tracked, consistent with COSO ERM and NIST governance concepts. Changing the rating method does not address the lack of accountability.

questions.q: A company assigns each cyber risk a likelihood and impact rating of high, medium, or low and plots them on a heat map. Which is a primary limitation of this approach compared with quantitative analysis?
choices: It does not readily support cost-benefit comparison of controls in monetary terms and relies on subjective judgment
It requires extensive historical loss data
It cannot rank risks relative to each other
It cannot be presented to the board
questions.exp: Qualitative ratings are fast and easy to communicate but subjective and not directly comparable with control costs. Extensive historical data is a demand of quantitative analysis, not qualitative.

questions.q: A software developer with access to source code plans to steal proprietary algorithms before joining a competitor. Which control would most likely detect unusual activity such as bulk downloads of the code repository?
choices: A disaster recovery plan
User and entity behavior analytics that flag deviations from a user's normal activity
An annual review of the developer's job description
A perimeter firewall
questions.exp: UEBA establishes baselines of normal behavior and alerts on anomalies like unusual download volumes, which is useful against insiders who have legitimate access. A perimeter firewall does not inspect authorized internal access to repositories.

questions.q: A hacktivist group announces that it will target a company's public website in protest of a recent business decision. Which risk does this threat actor most likely pose, based on typical motivations?
choices: Long-term covert theft of trade secrets for a foreign government
Embezzlement through manipulated vendor payments
Accidental deletion of data by an untrained user
Website defacement or denial-of-service attacks intended to gain publicity
questions.exp: Hacktivists are typically motivated by ideology and seek visibility through defacements, DDoS, or data leaks. Covert long-term espionage is more characteristic of nation-state actors.

questions.q: An attacker sends finance employees personalized emails referencing a real pending acquisition and the names of their actual managers, with a link to a fake login page. This attack is best described as:
choices: Vishing
Spear phishing
A denial-of-service attack
A brute-force attack
questions.exp: Spear phishing targets specific individuals with tailored, credible details to increase success. Vishing is voice-based social engineering by telephone.

questions.q: A company subscribes to a threat intelligence feed describing tactics currently used by ransomware groups targeting its industry. How is this information best used in the cybersecurity risk management process?
choices: To replace the annual risk assessment
To update threat likelihood estimates in risk assessments and tune detection rules and controls
To satisfy the SEC's Form 8-K disclosure requirement
To determine the exposure factor for each asset's value
questions.exp: Threat intelligence informs the likelihood component of risk and helps prioritize controls and detection content. It supplements, rather than replaces, structured risk assessment.

questions.q: A risk analyst estimates that a ransomware event would cost $1.2 million in recovery and lost sales. Industry data suggest a 15% chance of such an event in any given year. A managed detection service would cut the probability to 5% and costs $150,000 annually. Based solely on ALE, should the company buy the service?
choices: No, because ALE falls by only $120,000, which is less than the $150,000 cost
No, because the cost exceeds the remaining ALE of $60,000
Yes, because ALE falls by $180,000, which exceeds the cost
Yes, because any reduction in probability justifies the cost
questions.exp: ALE falls from $1.2 million x 15% = $180,000 to $1.2 million x 5% = $60,000, a $120,000 reduction that is less than the $150,000 cost. The $180,000 figure is the original ALE, not the reduction.

questions.q: Attackers have defeated a company's MFA by luring employees to a proxy phishing site that relays their passwords and one-time SMS codes in real time. Which authentication method would best resist this attack?
choices: Security questions in addition to the password
Longer one-time passcodes delivered by SMS
Push notifications that employees approve with a single tap
FIDO2 security keys or passkeys that cryptographically bind authentication to the legitimate site's domain
questions.exp: Phishing-resistant authenticators such as FIDO2/WebAuthn will not authenticate to a look-alike domain, so relayed credentials are useless; CISA recommends them as the strongest MFA. Simple push approvals remain vulnerable to relay and MFA-fatigue attacks.

questions.q: At a manufacturer, the vice president of sales decides who may access customer pricing data and how it is classified, while the IT database team performs backups and implements the access settings she approves. In data governance terms, the IT database team is the:
choices: Data steward
Data owner
Data custodian
Data subject
questions.exp: The data custodian maintains and protects data and implements controls as directed by the owner. The data owner (the VP of sales) is accountable for classification and access decisions.

questions.q: A company appoints individuals within each business unit to maintain data definitions, monitor data quality metrics and resolve data quality issues on a day-to-day basis. These individuals are best described as:
choices: Data subjects
Data stewards
Database administrators
Data custodians
questions.exp: Data stewards manage data quality, definitions and usage on behalf of data owners. Custodians focus on technical storage and protection rather than business definitions and quality.

questions.q: A data quality review finds the same customer recorded three times in the CRM under slightly different names, inflating the customer count. Which data quality dimension is most directly affected?
choices: Validity
Accuracy of individual fields
Timeliness
Uniqueness
questions.exp: Uniqueness means each real-world entity is recorded once; duplicate records violate it. Each duplicate record could have individually valid and accurate fields, so validity is not the main issue.

questions.q: A monthly sales dashboard uses data that is refreshed only quarterly, so managers make decisions on outdated figures. Which data quality dimension is lacking?
choices: Uniqueness
Validity
Timeliness
Consistency
questions.exp: Timeliness concerns whether data are available and current when needed. The data may be accurate as of their date, but they are too stale for monthly decisions.

questions.q: Revenue for the same period differs between the ERP and the data warehouse because the warehouse applies a different definition of 'booked order.' Which data governance tool would most directly prevent this?
choices: Faster network connections
More database indexes
A business glossary and data dictionary with standardized, approved definitions
Additional backups
questions.exp: Standardized definitions in a business glossary and data dictionary ensure systems and reports use consistent meanings. Backups and indexes address recoverability and performance, not definitional consistency.

questions.q: An auditor wants to understand how a figure on a regulatory report was derived, tracing it back through transformations to its source systems. Which data governance capability provides this?
choices: Data lineage
Data retention
Data masking
Data minimization
questions.exp: Data lineage documents the flow of data from source through transformations to reports. Data masking conceals sensitive values and does not show data flow.

questions.q: A company maintains customer data in its CRM, billing and shipping systems, and each system has different addresses for the same customers. Which approach best addresses this?
choices: Implementing master data management to establish a single authoritative source of customer master data
Allowing each system to keep its own version
Encrypting all three databases
Deleting customer data from two systems
questions.exp: Master data management creates a trusted, consistent golden record that is shared across systems. Encryption protects confidentiality but does nothing to reconcile inconsistent data.

questions.q: Under the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), an individual asks a company to delete his personal data, which the company no longer needs for the purpose collected. Which right is he exercising?
choices: Right to data portability
Right to restriction of processing
Right to object to direct marketing only
Right to erasure
questions.exp: The right to erasure ('right to be forgotten') allows individuals to request deletion when data are no longer necessary, among other grounds. Portability concerns receiving data in a reusable format, not deletion.

questions.q: A company is sued and receives a litigation hold notice. Under its retention schedule, some relevant emails are due to be automatically deleted next week. What should the company do?
choices: Allow deletion according to the retention schedule
Suspend deletion of potentially relevant data under the legal hold until the hold is released
Delete all emails immediately to reduce storage
Move relevant emails to employees' personal accounts
questions.exp: A legal hold overrides normal retention and disposal, preserving potentially relevant information. Continuing scheduled deletion could constitute spoliation of evidence.

questions.q: A company's privacy policy requires collecting only the personal data necessary for a specified purpose. A marketing team wants to add date of birth and income fields to a newsletter sign-up form. Which principle most directly argues against this?
choices: Data minimization
Data portability
Data residency
Data lineage
questions.exp: Data minimization limits collection to what is necessary for the stated purpose. Data residency concerns where data are stored geographically, not how much is collected.

questions.q: A company replaces credit card numbers in its order database with random surrogate values; the real numbers are stored in a separate, highly secured vault and can be retrieved only by authorized systems. This technique is:
choices: Tokenization
Hashing
Anonymization
Data masking for display only
questions.exp: Tokenization substitutes sensitive values with tokens that map back to the original values in a secure vault. Anonymization irreversibly removes the link to the original data, which is not the case here.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes pseudonymization from anonymization under GDPR?
choices: Pseudonymized data can be re-identified with additional information kept separately and remain personal data; truly anonymized data cannot be re-identified and fall outside GDPR
Pseudonymization requires deleting the original data
Both remove data from GDPR scope
Anonymized data remain personal data, but pseudonymized data do not
questions.exp: Pseudonymized data are still personal data because re-identification is possible with additional information. Only data that are irreversibly anonymized fall outside GDPR.

questions.q: A company's data classification scheme labels data as Public, Internal, Confidential and Restricted. What is the primary purpose of classification?
choices: To improve database performance
To reduce the volume of data stored
To apply protection controls commensurate with the data's sensitivity and value
To determine depreciation of IT assets
questions.exp: Classification drives handling requirements such as encryption, access restrictions and retention based on sensitivity. It does not by itself reduce storage volume or improve performance.

questions.q: A company stores large volumes of raw, unstructured data such as log files, images and social media feeds in their native format for future analysis. This repository is best described as a:
choices: Data lake
Relational OLTP database
Data dictionary
Data mart
questions.exp: A data lake stores raw data of many types in native format, with schema applied on read. A data warehouse or data mart stores structured, cleansed data organized for reporting.

questions.q: In an extract, transform, load (ETL) process feeding a data warehouse, which control best ensures that data are loaded completely?
choices: Encrypting the warehouse
Running the ETL only once a year
Allowing analysts to edit warehouse tables directly
Reconciling record counts and control totals between source extracts and the loaded warehouse tables
questions.exp: Reconciliations between source and target detect dropped or duplicated records during ETL. Allowing direct edits of warehouse tables undermines integrity rather than ensuring completeness.

questions.q: In a relational database, the system prevents entry of a sales order for a customer ID that does not exist in the customer table. This is enforced through:
choices: Data masking
A data lake schema
Referential integrity using a foreign key constraint
Normalization to third normal form
questions.exp: Referential integrity ensures foreign key values in one table correspond to existing primary key values in the related table. Normalization reduces redundancy but does not by itself block orphan records.

questions.q: A database designer organizes tables so that customer addresses are stored once, rather than repeated in every order record. The primary benefit of this normalization is:
choices: Faster report generation in all cases
Elimination of the need for backups
Reduced redundancy and update anomalies that cause inconsistent data
Automatic encryption of data
questions.exp: Normalization reduces data redundancy and the risk of inconsistent updates. It can actually slow some reporting queries, which is why warehouses often denormalize.

questions.q: A bank's funds transfer fails midway after debiting one account but before crediting the other, and the database rolls back the debit. Which database property does this demonstrate?
choices: Atomicity
Isolation
Durability
Normalization
questions.exp: Atomicity ensures a transaction either completes entirely or not at all. Durability ensures that committed transactions survive failures, which is a different property.

questions.q: A regulator requires that citizens' personal data be stored only within national borders. This requirement relates to:
choices: Data residency (sovereignty)
Data minimization
Data lineage
Data quality
questions.exp: Data residency or sovereignty requirements restrict where data are stored and processed geographically. Cloud deployments must be configured to meet them.

questions.q: A company is building its first data inventory. Which activity should come first to support privacy compliance and data protection?
choices: Deleting all data older than one year
Encrypting all email
Purchasing a new data warehouse
Mapping what personal and sensitive data are collected, where they are stored, how they flow and who has access
questions.exp: Data mapping and inventory provide the foundation for classification, protection, retention and responding to data subject requests. Deleting data without knowing what it is could violate retention requirements.

questions.q: Under the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA, which right allows consumers to direct a business not to sell or share their personal information?
choices: Right to data portability
Right to opt out of sale or sharing
Right to know
Right to correct
questions.exp: CCPA/CPRA grants consumers the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information. The right to know concerns learning what data are collected, not restricting their sale.

questions.q: A data loss prevention (DLP) tool is configured to block emails containing more than ten Social Security numbers from being sent to external domains. Which data governance objective does this most directly support?
choices: Data lineage
Data retention
Data quality
Preventing unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data
questions.exp: DLP tools monitor and block sensitive data from leaving authorized channels, preventing unauthorized disclosure. They do not improve data quality or document lineage.

questions.q: Which governance body is typically responsible for setting enterprise data policies, resolving cross-functional data disputes and prioritizing data initiatives?
choices: The network operations center
The external auditor
The help desk
A data governance council or committee
