questions.q: A company's customer portal went offline for six hours because its TLS certificate expired unnoticed. Which control would best prevent a recurrence?
choices: Maintaining a complete certificate inventory with automated expiration monitoring and renewal
Switching from TLS to an unencrypted connection during renewals
Purchasing certificates with the longest validity period available
Assigning certificate renewal to the help desk on request
questions.exp: Certificate lifecycle management (inventory, alerts, and automated renewal) keeps expirations from going unnoticed, especially as maximum certificate lifetimes shrink. Longer validity periods only delay the problem and are increasingly restricted by browser policy.

questions.q: An insider in accounts payable could alter a payment file after it is generated by the ERP system but before it is uploaded to the bank. Which control best detects or prevents unauthorized changes?
choices: Encrypting the network connection to the bank portal
Reviewing the bank statement at month-end
Requiring the insider to use a stronger password
Having the ERP digitally sign the payment file when it is generated, with the bank verifying the signature before processing
questions.exp: Signing the file at creation protects integrity end to end, so any change after generation causes signature verification to fail. Encrypting only the upload channel does nothing about alterations made before transmission.

questions.q: A call center application shows representatives only the last four digits of customers' Social Security numbers, while the fraud team sees full values. Which control is being applied?
choices: Dynamic data masking based on the user's role
Tokenization of the Social Security numbers at the point of capture
Hashing of the Social Security numbers
Static data masking of the production database
questions.exp: Dynamic masking alters what is displayed at query time according to user privileges while leaving stored data intact, so the fraud team can still see full values. Static masking permanently changes the stored data and would deny the fraud team the real values.

questions.q: A company signs electronic purchase agreements with suppliers. In a later dispute, a supplier claims it never approved an agreement. Which control would best support the company's position?
choices: The agreement was sent over a TLS-encrypted connection
The agreement bears the supplier's digital signature, created with a private key held only by the supplier and verifiable with the supplier's certified public key
The agreement's hash value was recorded in the company's database
The agreement was stored on an encrypted file server
questions.exp: A digital signature tied to a private key under the supplier's sole control provides non-repudiation. TLS and storage encryption protect confidentiality, and a hash recorded by the company proves integrity but not who approved the document.

questions.q: A hospital's data classification policy labels patient records as 'restricted' and marketing brochures as 'public.' What is the main benefit of this classification for data protection?
choices: It allows protection controls such as encryption, access restrictions, and handling rules to be applied in proportion to data sensitivity
It eliminates the need for access controls on public data
It guarantees compliance with HIPAA
It replaces the need for a risk assessment
questions.exp: Classification lets the organization concentrate stronger and costlier controls where the impact of disclosure is highest. Public data still needs integrity controls, and classification alone does not ensure regulatory compliance.

questions.q: A cloud customer must demonstrate to regulators that its cloud provider cannot access the keys protecting its encrypted data. Which arrangement best supports this?
choices: Encrypting only data in transit to the provider
Customer-managed keys held in a customer-controlled hardware security module outside the provider's administrative control
Using the provider's default encryption with provider-managed keys
Relying on the provider's SOC 2 report covering confidentiality
questions.exp: Holding keys in a customer-controlled HSM (often called hold-your-own-key) keeps the provider from decrypting the data. With provider-managed keys, the provider can technically access plaintext, regardless of what its SOC 2 report says about its controls.

questions.q: A company's remote employees connect to the internal ERP system from hotels and coffee shops over public Wi-Fi. Which control best protects the confidentiality of this traffic?
choices: Changing ERP passwords every 60 days
Installing antivirus software on the ERP server
Requiring employees to use only hotels with password-protected Wi-Fi
An encrypted VPN tunnel combined with multifactor authentication for remote access
questions.exp: A VPN encrypts traffic between the device and the corporate network, preventing eavesdropping on untrusted networks, while MFA protects the connection itself. A Wi-Fi password is shared with other guests and does not protect traffic from them.

questions.q: A help desk technician notices that files on an accounting workstation are being renamed with an unfamiliar extension and a ransom note has appeared. What should the technician do first?
choices: Disconnect the workstation from the network while leaving it powered on, and escalate to the incident response team
Power off the workstation immediately
Restore the workstation from last night's backup
Pay the ransom to prevent further encryption
questions.exp: Isolating the host stops the spread while preserving volatile evidence such as memory contents, consistent with NIST SP 800-61 containment guidance. Powering off destroys volatile evidence, and restoring before containment and analysis risks reinfection.

questions.q: Under the incident response life cycle in NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, during which phase does an organization establish an incident response team, acquire tools, and develop playbooks?
choices: Preparation
Post-incident activity
Containment, eradication, and recovery
Detection and analysis
questions.exp: Preparation covers building the capability (team, policies, tools, communication plans, and training) before incidents occur. Post-incident activity feeds lessons learned back into preparation but is not where the capability is first established.

questions.q: An investigator collects a hard drive from a laptop used in a suspected embezzlement scheme. Which practice is most important to ensure the evidence will be admissible in later legal proceedings?
choices: Maintaining a documented chain of custody and analyzing a verified forensic image rather than the original
Analyzing the original drive directly to save time
Storing the drive in the IT manager's desk drawer
Allowing the employee to back up personal files first
questions.exp: A chain of custody documents who handled the evidence and when, and working from a hash-verified forensic copy preserves the original unaltered. Analyzing the original risks modifying it and undermining its credibility.

questions.q: A forensic responder arrives at a compromised server that is still running. Following the order of volatility, which evidence should be collected first?
choices: Archived backup tapes
Printed copies of the system documentation
Contents of system memory (RAM) and running processes
Files on the server's hard drive
questions.exp: The order of volatility calls for collecting the most short-lived data first, and memory and network connections disappear when a system is shut down. Disk files and backup media persist and can be collected afterward.

questions.q: A security analyst observes a single failed login attempt on a server, followed by a successful login from the same user a minute later. How should this be classified?
choices: A security incident requiring activation of the incident response plan
A data breach requiring regulatory notification
A disaster requiring activation of the disaster recovery plan
A security event that does not by itself indicate an incident
questions.exp: An event is any observable occurrence; an incident is a violation or imminent threat of violation of security policies. A single mistyped password followed by success is a routine event, and treating every event as an incident would overwhelm responders.

questions.q: Two incidents are reported at the same time: a malware infection on a marketing intern's laptop and unauthorized access to the database containing customers' Social Security numbers. How should the incident response team prioritize them?
choices: Equally, by splitting the team in half
Based on which can be resolved fastest
Based on functional and information impact, giving priority to the database incident
In the order in which they were reported
questions.exp: SP 800-61 prioritizes incidents by their functional impact, information impact, and recoverability rather than first come, first served. Unauthorized access to sensitive personal data has far greater information impact than a contained laptop infection.

questions.q: During a breach investigation, the company suspects that its email system is controlled by the attacker. How should the incident response team coordinate its activities?
choices: Postpone all communication until the investigation is complete
Use the company's public social media accounts
Continue using corporate email but mark messages confidential
Use pre-arranged out-of-band communication channels, such as separate phones or a secure external collaboration platform
questions.exp: If attackers may monitor normal channels, responders should switch to out-of-band communications established during preparation. Continuing on compromised email tips off the attacker to the response.

questions.q: After an incident is contained, the team removes the malware, deletes attacker-created accounts, and patches the exploited vulnerability. These steps occur during which activity?
choices: Preparation
Detection
Lessons learned
Eradication
questions.exp: Eradication eliminates components of the incident, such as malware and unauthorized accounts, and addresses exploited vulnerabilities. Containment comes first to limit damage, and recovery restores normal operations afterward.

questions.q: A company has eradicated malware from its order management system and is ready to restore operations. Which approach best supports recovery?
choices: Return the systems to service immediately and investigate later
Restore from backups verified to predate the compromise, harden the systems, and monitor closely for signs of reinfection
Restore from the most recent backup without examining it
Reinstall only the operating system and leave application files as they are
questions.exp: The most recent backup may contain the malware or attacker persistence, so recovery should use known-clean backups and heightened monitoring. Returning systems to service without validation risks repeating the incident.

questions.q: Three weeks after resolving a significant data breach, the incident response manager schedules a meeting with IT, legal, communications, and business owners. What is the primary purpose of this meeting?
choices: To identify what happened, how well the response worked, and what changes to controls and procedures would improve future responses
To prepare the company's annual financial statements
To determine which employees should be disciplined
To close the incident ticket and destroy collected evidence
questions.exp: The lessons-learned review in post-incident activity improves security controls and the IR process itself. Evidence should be retained according to retention requirements and potential litigation, not destroyed at closure.

questions.q: Ransomware has encrypted a company's production systems, and management is considering paying the ransom. Which consideration is most critical before any payment?
choices: Whether the payment will be recorded as an operating expense
Whether the payment could violate sanctions regulations, such as OFAC restrictions on payments to designated parties, and involving legal counsel and law enforcement
Whether the attackers offer a discount for prompt payment
Whether the ransom can be expensed for tax purposes
questions.exp: The U.S. Treasury's OFAC has warned that facilitating ransom payments to sanctioned parties can create legal liability, so legal review and law enforcement engagement are essential. Payment also does not guarantee data recovery or deletion of stolen data.

questions.q: A company is developing its business continuity plan. Which activity should be completed first to establish recovery priorities?
choices: Purchasing equipment for an alternate processing site
A business impact analysis that identifies critical processes, their dependencies, and the impact of disruption over time
Conducting a full interruption test
Writing detailed restoration procedures for each server
questions.exp: The BIA determines which processes are critical and sets the maximum tolerable downtime, RTO, and RPO that drive recovery strategies. Buying a site or writing procedures before the BIA risks protecting the wrong things.

questions.q: A BIA concludes that the order fulfillment process can be down no longer than 24 hours (maximum tolerable downtime). After systems are restored, staff need 6 hours to verify data and process the backlog (work recovery time). What is the maximum recovery time objective for the supporting systems?
choices: 18 hours
30 hours
24 hours
6 hours
questions.exp: RTO plus work recovery time must not exceed the MTD, so RTO = 24 - 6 = 18 hours. Setting the RTO equal to the full MTD leaves no time for verification and backlog processing.

questions.q: A distribution company loses $40,000 in gross margin for each hour its warehouse system is down, plus a one-time $25,000 penalty if an outage exceeds 8 hours. What is the total estimated loss from a 10-hour outage?
questions.exp: Lost margin is 10 hours x $40,000 = $400,000, plus the $25,000 penalty triggered because the outage exceeded 8 hours, for $425,000. Omitting the penalty produces the $400,000 trap.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes a business continuity plan (BCP) from a disaster recovery plan (DRP)?
choices: The BCP and DRP are identical documents with different names
The DRP is prepared by external auditors, while the BCP is prepared by management
The BCP addresses continuing critical business functions during and after a disruption, while the DRP focuses on restoring IT systems and data
The BCP addresses only IT systems, while the DRP addresses the whole business
questions.exp: The DRP is a technology-focused component of broader business continuity, which also addresses people, facilities, suppliers, and manual workarounds. Reversing the scope of the two plans is the trap.

questions.q: Members of a company's crisis team gather in a conference room and talk through their responses to a hypothetical ransomware scenario presented by a facilitator, without touching any systems. What type of test is this?
choices: Tabletop exercise
Parallel test
Full interruption test
Simulation with system failover
questions.exp: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based walkthrough of roles and decisions in a scenario, with no actual system activity. A parallel test runs recovery systems alongside production, which involves real processing.

questions.q: A bank wants to confirm that its recovery site can process a full day's transactions accurately, without risking disruption to customers. Which test is most appropriate?
choices: A tabletop discussion among department heads
A full interruption test in which production is shut down
A checklist review of the plan
A parallel test in which the recovery site processes actual transactions while production continues normally
questions.exp: A parallel test verifies that recovery systems can process real workloads and compares results with production, without interrupting operations. A full interruption test gives the most assurance but risks a real outage if recovery fails.

questions.q: Which business continuity test provides the highest level of assurance but also carries the greatest risk to normal operations?
choices: Structured walkthrough
Full interruption test
Parallel test
Checklist review
questions.exp: A full interruption test actually shuts down primary operations and relies on the recovery capability, so it is the most realistic and the most risky. A parallel test keeps production running and therefore carries less risk.

questions.q: A company's business continuity plan was written four years ago. Since then, the company has moved its ERP system to the cloud, closed a plant, and replaced half of its management team. What is the most significant concern?
choices: The plan should be shortened for readability
The plan should be stored only electronically
The plan should be reclassified as a disaster recovery plan
The plan is likely outdated; it should be reviewed and updated after significant changes and on a regular schedule, and then retested
questions.exp: Continuity plans must be maintained as systems, facilities, and personnel change, or they will fail when invoked. Format and storage issues are minor compared with plans that reference systems and people that no longer exist.

questions.q: Only one employee knows how to run the quarterly sales tax filing process, and the procedures are not documented. From a business continuity perspective, what is the best recommendation?
choices: Document the procedures and cross-train at least one other employee
Require the employee to work longer hours near filing deadlines
Move the tax system to a different data center
Purchase additional servers for the tax system
questions.exp: Key-person dependency is a continuity risk addressed through documentation, cross-training, and succession planning. Additional hardware does not solve the risk of the only knowledgeable person being unavailable.

questions.q: During a business impact analysis, a manufacturer discovers that its most critical product depends on a component available from only one supplier located in a region prone to flooding. How should this be addressed?
choices: Ignore it because supplier risk is outside the BIA scope
Transfer the risk by requiring the supplier to sign a confidentiality agreement
Address it only in the IT disaster recovery plan
Include the dependency in the BIA and develop continuity strategies, such as qualifying alternate suppliers or holding safety stock
questions.exp: A BIA should identify external dependencies, including key suppliers, because their failure disrupts critical processes. A confidentiality agreement does nothing to secure supply continuity.

questions.q: An organization's security logs from firewalls, servers, and applications show timestamps that differ by several minutes, making it hard to reconstruct an attack timeline. Which control would most directly address this problem?
choices: Synchronizing all system clocks to an authoritative time source using NTP
Encrypting all log files
Printing logs daily for manual review
Increasing log retention to seven years
questions.exp: Consistent time synchronization allows events from different sources to be correlated accurately during investigations. Longer retention or encryption does not fix inconsistent timestamps.

questions.q: A mid-sized company has no in-house forensic specialists. Which preparation step would most improve its ability to respond quickly to a major breach?
choices: Hiring a full-time forensic team of ten people
Relying on the cloud provider to investigate all incidents
Executing an incident response retainer with a qualified firm in advance, with agreed terms and response times
Planning to search for a forensic firm after a breach occurs
questions.exp: A pre-negotiated retainer allows experts to engage within hours rather than days spent on procurement and contracting during a crisis. Searching after the fact delays containment, and a cloud provider's responsibility is limited under the shared responsibility model.

questions.q: A company with a cyber insurance policy discovers a breach. Before engaging outside forensic firms and breach counsel, what should it confirm?
choices: The policy's notice requirements and whether the insurer requires use of its pre-approved panel of vendors
That the IT staff have been placed on administrative leave
That all affected systems have been reformatted
That the incident has been disclosed on social media
questions.exp: Many cyber policies require prompt notice and use of approved vendors as a condition of coverage, so failing to follow them can jeopardize reimbursement. Reformatting systems would destroy evidence needed for the investigation and claim.

questions.q: A company's breach response involved outside counsel retaining the forensic firm. What is the primary reason organizations often structure investigations this way?
choices: To help preserve attorney-client privilege and work-product protection over investigation findings
Regulators require all forensic firms to be hired by lawyers
It eliminates the need to notify affected individuals
Counsel can perform the technical forensic analysis faster
questions.exp: Engaging forensics through counsel to support legal advice may help protect findings from discovery, though courts have not always upheld the privilege. It does not remove legal notification obligations.

questions.q: A security team receives a vendor advisory that a vulnerability in the company's VPN appliance will be exploited by a known group, and later sees a log entry showing a web shell file created on the appliance. In NIST terminology, these are respectively:
choices: An indicator and a precursor
A precursor and an indicator
Two precursors
Two indicators
questions.exp: SP 800-61 defines a precursor as a sign that an incident may occur in the future, and an indicator as a sign that an incident may have occurred or is occurring. The web shell shows compromise has already happened, so it is an indicator.

questions.q: When selecting a containment strategy for a compromised web server, which factor is least relevant according to NIST SP 800-61?
choices: The need to preserve evidence
The availability of the service to customers
The potential damage to and theft of resources
The original purchase price of the server hardware
questions.exp: SP 800-61 lists factors such as potential damage, evidence preservation, service availability, resources needed, effectiveness, and duration. The hardware's historical cost has little bearing on how to contain the incident.

questions.q: A ransomware attack has shut down a hospital's electronic health record system. Which business continuity element allows clinicians to keep treating patients while systems are restored?
choices: A post-incident lessons-learned report
A penetration test of the EHR system
Pre-defined manual downtime procedures, such as paper forms and printed medication lists
A cyber insurance policy
questions.exp: Manual workarounds enable critical processes to continue during system outages and are a core continuity strategy. Insurance and lessons-learned reports help afterward but do not keep operations running.

questions.q: Who should have primary ownership of and accountability for a company's business continuity plan?
choices: The IT help desk
Senior business management, with participation from business units and IT
The company's insurance broker
The external auditor
questions.exp: Business continuity is a business responsibility because it protects critical operations, and senior management sets priorities and funding; IT supports the technology portions. External auditors must remain independent and cannot own management's plans.

questions.q: A company's incident response plan states that the security team will decide on its own whether to notify customers, regulators, and law enforcement after a breach. What is the most significant weakness?
choices: Law enforcement notification is never appropriate
Notification decisions require involvement of legal counsel, communications, and senior management because they carry legal and reputational consequences
Customers should never be notified of breaches
The security team lacks access to customer email addresses
questions.exp: Breach notification is governed by laws and contracts and affects reputation, so IR plans should define roles for legal, communications, and executives. Leaving these decisions solely to technical staff risks missing obligations or deadlines.

questions.q: An incident response playbook for phishing describes step-by-step actions: identifying recipients, purging the message from mailboxes, resetting compromised credentials, and blocking the sender's domain. What is the main benefit of such playbooks?
choices: They guarantee that no phishing emails will succeed
They eliminate the need for an incident response team
They promote consistent, timely responses to common incident types
They replace the need for security monitoring
questions.exp: Playbooks standardize responses to recurring scenarios, reducing errors and delays under pressure. They support responders rather than replacing the team or preventive controls.

questions.q: An organization's annual business continuity test revealed that the alternate site could not access the payroll application because a license key was tied to the primary site's hardware. What should management do next?
choices: Document the finding, correct the licensing issue, update the plan, and retest the affected component
Remove payroll from the scope of the continuity plan
Report the finding only to the external auditor
Consider the test failed and discontinue future testing
questions.exp: Tests are meant to find gaps; findings should be tracked to remediation and the fix verified through retesting. Removing a critical process from scope merely hides the weakness.

questions.q: A company's BIA rates the accounts payable process as able to tolerate a two-week outage, while customer order entry can tolerate only four hours. How should this affect recovery strategies?
choices: Accounts payable should be recovered first because it involves cash
Order entry warrants a faster, more expensive recovery strategy, while accounts payable can use a slower, lower-cost strategy
Both processes should receive identical hot-site recovery capabilities
Neither process needs a recovery strategy until an outage occurs
questions.exp: Recovery strategies should be proportionate to criticality and tolerable downtime, balancing cost and recovery speed. Giving every process the fastest strategy wastes resources on processes that can tolerate delay.

questions.q: A breach investigation reveals that attackers were present in the network for nine months before detection. Which metric would management track to measure improvement in this area?
choices: Annualized rate of occurrence
Recovery point objective
Return on investment
Mean time to detect (dwell time)
questions.exp: Mean time to detect, closely related to dwell time, measures how long attackers operate before discovery, and reducing it limits damage. RPO measures tolerable data loss for recovery, not detection speed.

questions.q: A regional power outage forces a company to activate its business continuity plan. Which element should the plan contain to ensure employees, customers, and suppliers receive timely and consistent information?
choices: A crisis communication plan with designated spokespersons, contact lists, and pre-approved message templates
The company's chart of accounts
Vendor software license agreements
A detailed network diagram
questions.exp: Crisis communications planning ensures accurate and consistent messaging to stakeholders during a disruption. Network diagrams support technical recovery but do not address stakeholder communications.

questions.q: A company's incident response plan has never been exercised. Which approach would most cost-effectively validate roles, decision-making, and escalation paths before investing in more complex tests?
choices: An unannounced red-team attack on production systems
A tabletop exercise based on a realistic scenario
A full interruption test of production systems
Waiting for an actual incident to test the plan
questions.exp: Tabletop exercises are low-cost and low-risk ways to surface gaps in roles, communication, and decisions, after which more technical tests can follow. A full interruption test is costly and risky for a plan that has never been exercised.

questions.q: An employee reports that she clicked a link in a suspicious email and entered her network password. The security team confirms no further activity has occurred. What is the most appropriate immediate response?
choices: Take no action because no further activity has been observed
Reimage every computer in the company
Reset the employee's password, revoke active sessions, review authentication logs, and check for similar emails sent to others
Terminate the employee for violating the security policy
questions.exp: Prompt credential reset and session revocation contain the risk, while log review and searching for related messages determine the scope. Punishing employees who report incidents discourages the timely reporting that limits damage.

questions.q: A company's continuity plan addresses fires, floods, and data center outages, but a regional public health emergency now prevents 60% of staff from coming to the office for several weeks while all facilities and systems remain intact. Which scenario-planning gap does this reveal?
choices: The plan did not include a full interruption test
The plan lacked a hot site for the data center
The plan's recovery point objective was too long
The plan did not address loss of personnel, such as remote work capability, cross-training, and alternate staffing
questions.exp: Continuity planning should consider loss of people, not just loss of facilities or technology, using strategies like remote access capacity and cross-training. A hot site restores systems, which are unaffected in this scenario.

questions.q: A company's board wants to formally set its cybersecurity risk strategy, assign roles and responsibilities, approve policies, and oversee results. Under the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, which function most directly addresses these activities?
choices: Protect
Govern
Respond
Identify
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 added the Govern function to cover organizational context, risk management strategy, roles and responsibilities, policy, oversight, and supply chain risk management. Identify covers understanding assets and risks, not establishing the strategy and oversight structure.

questions.q: Under CSF version 1.1, a company mapped its cybersecurity supply chain risk management activities to the Identify function. When it updates to CSF 2.0, where will these outcomes primarily be found?
choices: Protect
Detect
Identify
Govern
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 moved cybersecurity supply chain risk management into the Govern function (GV.SC), reflecting its role as an enterprise risk management responsibility. Leaving it under Identify reflects the superseded version 1.1 structure.

questions.q: A company's cybersecurity risk management practices are formally approved as policy, consistently applied across the organization, and regularly updated when business requirements change, but they are not yet adapted in real time based on predictive indicators and lessons learned. Which CSF Tier best describes the organization?
choices: Tier 1, Partial
Tier 3, Repeatable
Tier 4, Adaptive
Tier 2, Risk Informed
questions.exp: Tier 3 (Repeatable) reflects formally approved, organization-wide practices that are consistently updated. Tier 4 (Adaptive) adds continuous adaptation using advanced and predictive indicators and lessons learned, which this organization lacks.

questions.q: The CIO of a mid-sized distributor insists that the company must reach CSF Tier 4 in every area within a year. What is the best response?
choices: Explain that Tiers characterize the rigor of practices and that the target Tier should reflect the organization's risk, resources, and cost-benefit considerations
Recommend skipping Tiers and using only Profiles
Agree, because CSF compliance requires Tier 4 in all areas
Explain that Tiers are maturity levels that must be attained sequentially, one per year
questions.exp: NIST states that Tiers are not a required maturity model; organizations choose target Tiers that are appropriate for their risk and that progression should be cost-effective. CSF is voluntary and has no 'compliance' requirement to reach Tier 4.

questions.q: A company has documented the cybersecurity outcomes it currently achieves and the outcomes it wants to achieve in two years. Under CSF 2.0, what is the next step?
choices: Engage a CPA firm to issue a SOC 2 report on the Target Profile
Submit both Profiles to NIST for certification
Select a CSF Tier and discard the Profiles
Analyze the gaps between the Current and Target Profiles and develop a prioritized action plan
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 describes creating Current and Target Organizational Profiles, analyzing gaps, and implementing a prioritized action plan. NIST does not certify organizations against the CSF.

questions.q: An industry association for regional banks publishes a set of CSF outcomes and priorities tailored to threats and regulations common to its members. Under CSF 2.0, this publication is best described as a(n):
choices: Informative Reference
Community Profile
Implementation Tier
Organizational Profile
questions.exp: A Community Profile is a baseline of CSF outcomes created for a shared interest, such as a sector, that member organizations can use as a starting point for their own Target Profiles. An Organizational Profile describes a single organization's current or target state.

questions.q: A company is building a complete inventory of its hardware, software, data, and the services provided by suppliers. Under CSF 2.0, which category and function does this activity fall under?
choices: Continuous Monitoring, under Detect
Asset Management, under Identify
Platform Security, under Protect
Organizational Context, under Govern
questions.exp: Asset Management (ID.AM) is part of Identify and covers inventories of hardware, software, services, and data. Organizational Context under Govern addresses mission, stakeholders, and legal requirements rather than asset inventories.

questions.q: A company configures its security information and event management (SIEM) system to monitor network traffic and user activity around the clock for indicators of compromise. Which CSF 2.0 function does this activity support?
choices: Respond
Identify
Protect
Detect
questions.exp: Continuous monitoring of assets to find anomalies and indicators of compromise is part of Detect (DE.CM). It does not prevent events, which would be Protect, and it precedes the incident management activities of Respond.

questions.q: Following a ransomware attack, a company restores systems from verified backups, confirms the integrity of restored data, and communicates recovery progress to customers. Which CSF 2.0 function do these activities primarily support?
choices: Govern
Respond
Protect
Recover
questions.exp: Recover covers restoring assets and operations (RC.RP) and communicating recovery activities (RC.CO). Respond focuses on managing, analyzing, containing, and eradicating the incident itself.

questions.q: During an active intrusion, the security team isolates infected servers from the network and blocks the attacker's command-and-control addresses. Which CSF 2.0 function do these actions fall under?
choices: Detect
Respond
Recover
Protect
questions.exp: Containment and eradication are Incident Mitigation activities (RS.MI) within Respond. Protect safeguards are put in place before an incident to prevent or reduce its likelihood.

questions.q: A company rolls out multifactor authentication for all users and mandatory annual security awareness training. Under CSF 2.0, these outcomes are found in which function?
choices: Detect
Protect
Govern
Identify
questions.exp: Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control (PR.AA) and Awareness and Training (PR.AT) are categories of Protect. Govern sets the policies and roles but the safeguards themselves are Protect outcomes.

questions.q: The executive director of a small nonprofit believes the NIST CSF does not apply to her organization because it was designed only for critical infrastructure. Which response is most accurate?
choices: CSF 2.0 applies only to federal agencies and their contractors
CSF 2.0 is explicitly intended for organizations of all sizes and sectors and is voluntary
CSF 2.0 applies only to organizations that process payment cards
She is correct; CSF 2.0 is mandatory only for critical infrastructure operators
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 broadened its stated scope from critical infrastructure to all organizations, regardless of size, sector, or maturity, and remains voluntary. The original 2014 framework focused on critical infrastructure, which is the source of the misconception.

questions.q: A security manager using CSF 2.0 wants to see which specific SP 800-53 controls and ISO/IEC 27001 requirements correspond to each CSF subcategory. Which CSF resource provides this mapping?
choices: Informative References
Community Profiles
Implementation Tiers
Quick-Start Guides
questions.exp: Informative References map CSF outcomes to other standards, guidelines, and control catalogs such as SP 800-53. Tiers describe the rigor of risk practices, not control mappings.

questions.q: A government contractor needs a detailed catalog of specific security and privacy controls, including control enhancements and low, moderate, and high baselines. Which NIST resource is most appropriate?
choices: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 with SP 800-53B baselines
NIST SP 800-30
NIST SP 800-61
NIST CSF 2.0
questions.exp: SP 800-53 Rev. 5 is the comprehensive control catalog, and SP 800-53B provides the control baselines. The CSF describes outcomes rather than prescribing specific controls, and SP 800-30 is a risk assessment guide.

questions.q: Under FIPS 199, an information system processes data assessed as moderate impact for confidentiality, high impact for integrity, and low impact for availability. Which control baseline should be selected for the system under FIPS 200?
choices: A mixed baseline using different levels for each objective
Moderate baseline
High baseline
Low baseline
questions.exp: FIPS 200 uses the high-water mark: the system's overall impact level equals the highest impact among confidentiality, integrity, and availability, which is high here. Averaging to moderate understates the potential impact of an integrity failure.

questions.q: A system processes two information types. Type 1 is rated low confidentiality, moderate integrity, low availability. Type 2 is rated moderate confidentiality, low integrity, low availability. Applying FIPS 199, what is the system's security category?
choices: Confidentiality low, integrity low, availability low; overall impact low
Confidentiality moderate, integrity low, availability low; overall impact moderate
Confidentiality moderate, integrity moderate, availability moderate; overall impact moderate
Confidentiality moderate, integrity moderate, availability low; overall impact moderate
questions.exp: For each objective, the system takes the highest rating among its information types: confidentiality moderate (Type 2), integrity moderate (Type 1), availability low; the overall impact is the highest of these, moderate. Using only Type 2's integrity rating understates integrity.

questions.q: Under the NIST Risk Management Framework (SP 800-37), an independent assessor has tested a system's controls and documented the residual risk. What is the next step?
choices: Prepare the organization for risk management
Select additional controls from the baseline
Authorize the system, in which a senior official decides whether the residual risk is acceptable
Categorize the system
questions.exp: The RMF sequence is Prepare, Categorize, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorize, and Monitor; after assessment, the authorizing official accepts or rejects the risk. Categorization occurs much earlier, before controls are selected.

questions.q: Which RMF step, added in SP 800-37 Rev. 2, establishes organization-level and system-level context, risk strategy, and priorities before a system is categorized?
choices: Prepare
Assess
Select
Monitor
questions.exp: Rev. 2 added the Prepare step to establish context, roles, risk tolerance, and common controls before categorization. Monitor is the final, ongoing step after authorization.

questions.q: After a system receives its authorization to operate, the organization tracks control effectiveness, changes to the system, and threats on an ongoing basis so the authorizing official can maintain a current view of risk. Which RMF step is this?
choices: Assess
Authorize
Implement
Monitor
questions.exp: The Monitor step provides continuous monitoring and supports ongoing authorization. Assess refers to the formal evaluation of controls before the authorization decision.

questions.q: During an SP 800-53A assessment, the assessor attempts to connect to a restricted server port from the internet to confirm that the firewall blocks the traffic. Which assessment method is the assessor using?
choices: Inquire
Interview
Test
Examine
questions.exp: SP 800-53A defines three methods: examine (review documents, settings, records), interview (discuss with personnel), and test (exercise the control under specified conditions). Attempting the connection exercises the control, so it is a test rather than an examination of the firewall rule set.

questions.q: A company wants to use SP 800-53 Rev. 5 to manage risks from suppliers of hardware and software components. Which control family, added in Rev. 5, most directly addresses this?
choices: Program Management (PM)
Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency (PT)
Supply Chain Risk Management (SR)
System and Services Acquisition (SA)
questions.exp: Rev. 5 added the SR family for supply chain risk management, along with the PT family for privacy. SA addresses acquisition and development practices but was not the new family dedicated to supply chain risk.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a significant change in NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 compared with earlier revisions?
choices: It eliminated privacy controls to focus solely on security
It replaced control families with the five CSF functions
It applies only to federal agencies and may not be used by private entities
It integrated privacy controls into the main catalog and made controls outcome-based so they apply to any organization
questions.exp: Rev. 5 removed 'federal' from its title, integrated security and privacy controls into one catalog, and rewrote controls to be outcome-based for any organization. It still uses control families rather than CSF functions.

questions.q: A legacy production system cannot technically support one control in its selected SP 800-53 baseline. According to NIST tailoring guidance, what should the organization do?
choices: Remove the control from the baseline without documentation
Shut down the system until the legacy technology is replaced
Implement a compensating control that provides comparable protection, document the rationale, and have the residual risk accepted
Mark the control as implemented because it is technically infeasible
questions.exp: Tailoring allows compensating controls when baseline controls cannot be implemented, provided the rationale is documented and the authorizing official accepts the resulting risk. Silently removing the control or misreporting it as implemented undermines the authorization decision.

questions.q: A colocation data center provides badge access, cameras, and fire suppression for every application system hosted there. System owners document that their systems rely on these safeguards. In SP 800-53 terminology, these physical controls are best described as:
choices: System-specific controls
Common (inherited) controls
Detective controls only
Compensating controls
questions.exp: Common controls are provided once and inherited by multiple systems, which avoids duplicate implementation and assessment. System-specific controls are implemented by and for a single system.

questions.q: A security assessment identifies several control weaknesses that cannot be corrected before the system's authorization decision. Under the RMF, where should these weaknesses, the planned remediation, and target dates be documented?
choices: The plan of action and milestones (POA&M)
The incident response plan
The organizational Community Profile
The system security categorization
questions.exp: The POA&M documents known weaknesses, the tasks planned to correct them, resources needed, and milestones, and it supports the authorization package. The security categorization records impact levels, not remediation plans.

questions.q: A small defense subcontractor receives Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) from the Department of Defense to perform its contract. Which NIST publication establishes the security requirements the subcontractor's systems must meet?
choices: NIST CSF 2.0
FIPS 199
NIST SP 800-61
NIST SP 800-171
questions.exp: SP 800-171 sets requirements for protecting CUI in nonfederal systems and is the basis for DoD's CMMC program. The CSF is voluntary and does not establish contractual CUI requirements.

questions.q: A risk analyst follows NIST SP 800-30 to assess risks to a payroll system. According to SP 800-30, the level of risk for a threat event is determined primarily by combining which two factors?
choices: The cost of controls and the system's book value
The number of users and the number of transactions
The likelihood that the threat event occurs and results in harm, and the adverse impact if it does
The control baseline and the number of POA&M items
questions.exp: SP 800-30 models risk as a function of the likelihood of a threat event exploiting vulnerabilities and the magnitude of resulting impact. Control costs matter for risk response decisions, not for determining the level of risk.

questions.q: Which statement best describes NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, issued in 2025?
choices: It limits incident response to technical containment performed by IT staff
It integrates incident response recommendations into the CSF 2.0 functions as part of broader cybersecurity risk management
It mandates specific forensic tools for federal agencies
It replaces the CSF as the primary cybersecurity framework
questions.exp: Rev. 3 aligns incident response with all six CSF 2.0 functions, treating preparation, detection, response, recovery, and improvement as part of overall risk management. It explicitly broadens incident response beyond IT staff to leadership, legal, and other parties.

questions.q: A company is documenting its mission, key stakeholders' expectations, and the legal, regulatory, and contractual cybersecurity requirements it must meet. Which CSF 2.0 category does this activity address?
choices: Risk Assessment (ID.RA)
Policy (GV.PO)
Organizational Context (GV.OC)
Asset Management (ID.AM)
questions.exp: Organizational Context under Govern covers mission, stakeholder expectations, dependencies, and legal and regulatory requirements. Risk Assessment under Identify evaluates threats, vulnerabilities, and impacts to assets.

questions.q: After a tabletop exercise, the incident response team identifies several process improvements and updates its plans accordingly. In CSF 2.0, the Improvement category that captures lessons learned across all functions resides in which function?
choices: Respond
Identify
Recover
Govern
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 placed Improvement (ID.IM) in Identify, capturing improvements identified from evaluations, exercises, and incidents across all functions. Candidates often assume it belongs to Respond or Recover because lessons learned follow incidents.

questions.q: A security operations analyst correlates alerts from the firewall, endpoint agents, and authentication logs to determine whether a cluster of unusual logins represents a cybersecurity incident. Under CSF 2.0, this activity falls under which category?
choices: Incident Mitigation, under Respond
Identity Management, Authentication and Access Control, under Protect
Incident Recovery Plan Execution, under Recover
Adverse Event Analysis, under Detect
questions.exp: Adverse Event Analysis (DE.AE) covers analyzing anomalies and indicators to characterize events and decide whether an incident has occurred. Once an incident is declared, Respond categories such as Incident Analysis and Mitigation apply.

questions.q: The board of directors approves a statement specifying the organization's cybersecurity risk appetite and risk tolerance, which management will use to prioritize investments. Which CSF 2.0 category does this most directly support?
choices: Oversight (GV.OV)
Platform Security (PR.PS)
Risk Assessment (ID.RA)
Risk Management Strategy (GV.RM)
questions.exp: Risk Management Strategy under Govern establishes priorities, constraints, risk appetite and tolerance statements. Oversight under Govern reviews results of the strategy to adjust it, rather than setting appetite and tolerance.

questions.q: An organization's cybersecurity practices are ad hoc and reactive, there is limited awareness of cybersecurity risk at the organizational level, and risk is managed case by case. Which CSF Tier best describes this organization?
choices: Tier 2, Risk Informed
Tier 1, Partial
Tier 3, Repeatable
Tier 4, Adaptive
questions.exp: Tier 1 (Partial) describes ad hoc, reactive practices with limited organization-wide awareness. Tier 2 (Risk Informed) has management-approved practices and awareness, but they are not established as organization-wide policy.

questions.q: When designing an information security continuous monitoring program under NIST SP 800-137, how should the organization determine how often each control is monitored?
choices: Monitor only controls that failed in the prior assessment
Monitor every control annually to align with the financial statement audit
Monitor every control daily to ensure maximum assurance
Base monitoring frequency on the risk, volatility, and criticality of each control and the information needed for risk decisions
questions.exp: SP 800-137 calls for risk-based monitoring frequencies so that volatile or critical controls are assessed more often. A uniform annual cycle ignores fast-changing threats, and daily monitoring of everything is rarely cost-effective.

questions.q: A vulnerability scan shows that production servers run numerous unnecessary services and open ports. Which SP 800-53 control family most directly addresses this weakness?
choices: Audit and Accountability (AU)
Configuration Management (CM)
Contingency Planning (CP)
Awareness and Training (AT)
questions.exp: The CM family includes baseline configurations (CM-2) and least functionality (CM-7), which require disabling unneeded ports, protocols, and services. Audit logging would record activity but not reduce the attack surface.

questions.q: A developer at a fintech company can both write code and deploy it directly into the production environment without review. Which SP 800-53 control is most directly violated?
choices: Audit record review (AU-6)
Account management (AC-2)
Contingency plan testing (CP-4)
Separation of duties (AC-5)
questions.exp: AC-5 requires dividing duties so that no single individual can perform conflicting functions, such as developing and promoting code to production without oversight. Account management covers provisioning and removing accounts, not conflicting duties.

questions.q: A CPA firm is engaged to report on a client's cybersecurity risk management program. The client's management wants to use the NIST CSF as its control criteria. In an AICPA SOC for Cybersecurity examination, is this permitted?
choices: Yes; the control criteria may be the Trust Services Criteria or another suitable framework such as NIST CSF or ISO/IEC 27001
No; the NIST CSF may be used only by federal agencies
Yes, but only if NIST certifies the client's Target Profile first
No; only the Trust Services Criteria may be used as control criteria
questions.exp: In a cybersecurity risk management examination, management may select suitable control criteria, including the TSC or frameworks such as NIST CSF or ISO 27001. NIST does not certify organizations, and the CSF is available to any organization.

questions.q: A consultant's CSF gap assessment rated the company only at the function level (for example, 'Protect: partially achieved'), and management cannot tell what specific actions to take. At which level of the CSF Core should the assessment be performed to produce actionable results?
choices: Community Profiles
Functions
Implementation Tiers
Subcategories
questions.exp: The CSF Core is organized as Functions, then Categories, then Subcategories, and Subcategories are the most specific outcome statements against which current and target states can be compared. Tiers describe the rigor of overall risk practices, not specific outcomes to remediate.

questions.q: An auditor wants to rely on an automated three-way match control in a client's purchasing system. IT general controls over program changes and access have been tested and found effective for the period. Which approach to testing the automated control is generally appropriate?
choices: Test the control only at year-end with a sample of 25 transactions
Rely on management's inquiry responses alone
Test the control with a small number of instances, often one per relevant condition, because effective ITGCs support consistent operation
Test a sample of 60 transactions throughout the year
questions.exp: Because automated controls perform consistently unless changed, an auditor can test each relevant scenario once when ITGCs over changes and access are effective. Large manual-control sample sizes are unnecessary for a properly controlled automated control.

questions.q: An auditor plans to use a system-generated aging report of accounts receivable to select confirmations. What should the auditor do before relying on the report?
choices: Request the same report from the client's IT department on a different day
Obtain a written representation from the controller that the report is accurate
Obtain evidence about the completeness and accuracy of the report, such as testing the report logic and reconciling its totals to the general ledger
Accept the report because it was produced by the system
questions.exp: Information produced by the entity must be evaluated for completeness and accuracy before it is used as audit evidence (AU-C 500). A management representation complements but cannot replace evidence about the report's reliability.

questions.q: An auditor tests whether terminated employees' system access was removed timely. Which population and procedure provide the most reliable evidence?
choices: Obtain a list of terminated employees from HR, select a sample, and compare termination dates with access removal dates in system logs
Select a sample of active users from the system and ask managers whether they still work at the company
Inquire of the IT manager about the termination process
Review the IT department's access removal policy
questions.exp: Starting from the HR termination list tests the right direction for the control and comparing it with system evidence shows whether removal was timely. Policy review and inquiry address design only and are not sufficient evidence of operating effectiveness.

questions.q: To test the change management control that all production program changes are approved, an auditor should select the sample from which population?
choices: The list of approved change tickets in the ticketing system
Emails requesting changes from business users
Changes that the IT manager identifies as significant
A system-generated list of changes actually migrated to production, such as from the change log or version control system
questions.exp: Selecting from changes actually made in production tests whether every change had approval, including any made outside the ticketing process. Sampling from approved tickets would never reveal unauthorized changes, because they have no ticket.

questions.q: Which type of audit evidence is generally the most persuasive regarding the operating effectiveness of an IT control?
choices: Inquiry of the system administrator
Reperformance of the control by the auditor
Observation of a control that operates monthly, performed once
A memo from the CIO describing the control
questions.exp: Reperformance gives direct, auditor-generated evidence that the control works as designed, and is generally more persuasive than observation or inquiry. Observation is limited to the moment observed, and inquiry alone is never sufficient.

questions.q: An auditor uses generalized audit software to analyze 100% of a client's 2.4 million vendor payments for duplicates, round amounts, and payments to vendors not on the approved list. What is the primary advantage of this approach?
choices: It replaces the need for professional judgment in evaluating results
It eliminates the need to evaluate the reliability of the data
It eliminates the need to understand the client's controls
It allows the auditor to examine the entire population and identify anomalies that sampling might miss
questions.exp: Data analytics enable testing of entire populations and targeting of unusual items. The auditor must still assess the completeness and accuracy of the data extracted and use judgment to investigate exceptions.

questions.q: An auditor processes fictitious test transactions, including some with invalid customer numbers and excessive credit amounts, through the client's live order-entry program to see whether the edits reject them. What technique is being used?
choices: Embedded audit module
Test data approach
Generalized audit software
Parallel simulation
questions.exp: The test data approach runs auditor-prepared transactions through the client's program and compares results with expected outcomes. Parallel simulation instead reprocesses the client's real data using the auditor's own program.

questions.q: An auditor writes a program that independently recalculates the client's payroll using actual payroll input data and compares the results with the client's payroll register. What technique is this?
choices: Test data approach
Parallel simulation
Integrated test facility
Snapshot technique
questions.exp: Parallel simulation reprocesses actual client data with auditor-controlled software and compares outputs. The test data approach uses fictitious transactions in the client's program.

questions.q: A bank's internal auditors created a dummy branch in the production system so they can continuously enter test transactions alongside real ones and compare results with expectations. What is the main risk of this integrated test facility?
choices: Test transactions may contaminate live financial data if they are not properly reversed or excluded from reporting
It can be used only on weekends
It cannot test programmed controls
It requires the auditor to have no knowledge of the system
questions.exp: An ITF mixes fictitious transactions with production data, so they must be carefully isolated and reversed to avoid misstating records. Testing programmed controls in the live environment is precisely its benefit.

questions.q: An auditor obtains a vendor master file extract from the client to perform analytics. The extract shows invoice totals of $4,512,300, while the accounts payable subledger and the general ledger both show $4,530,800. What should the auditor conclude?
choices: The difference is immaterial and the analytics can proceed
The extract is reliable because the difference is less than 1%
The extract appears incomplete or inaccurate by $18,500, so the auditor should investigate and obtain a complete extract before relying on analytics
The general ledger is overstated by $18,500
questions.exp: Reconciling extracted data to the ledger is a key completeness check; a $4,530,800 - $4,512,300 = $18,500 difference means some records may be missing from the population tested. Treating the GL as wrong ignores that it agrees with the subledger.

questions.q: An auditor selected 40 terminated employees and found that 3 still had active ERP access more than 30 days after termination. The auditor's tolerable deviation rate is 5%. What is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: The auditor should expand the sample to 400 to dilute the exceptions
The sample deviation rate of 7.5% exceeds the tolerable rate, so the control cannot be relied upon as planned
The control is effective because 3 exceptions is a small number
The control is effective because the sample deviation rate is 5%
questions.exp: The sample deviation rate is 3/40 = 7.5%, which exceeds the 5% tolerable rate, so the auditor should not rely on the control as planned and should evaluate the effect on the risk assessment and substantive testing. Expanding the sample to dilute exceptions is not appropriate.

questions.q: An auditor finds that developers at a client have unrestricted access to migrate their own code into production, and no compensating monitoring exists. How does this ITGC deficiency most directly affect the audit?
choices: It has no effect because application controls are tested separately
The auditor must issue an adverse opinion on the financial statements
The auditor may not be able to rely on automated application controls and system-generated reports without additional testing
The auditor can rely on application controls if management states that no unauthorized changes were made
questions.exp: Weak program change controls undermine the assumption that automated controls operated consistently throughout the period, so reliance requires additional procedures or substantive testing. An ITGC deficiency does not automatically lead to an adverse financial statement opinion.

questions.q: A user auditor plans to rely on a SOC 1 Type 2 report covering January 1 through September 30 for an audit of the calendar year. What should the auditor do regarding the October-through-December gap?
choices: Request a SOC 2 Type 1 report instead
Obtain a bridge letter from the service organization and perform additional procedures as needed, such as testing user entity controls, for the uncovered period
Assume controls were ineffective during the gap
Ignore the gap because nine months of coverage is sufficient
questions.exp: A bridge (gap) letter is management's representation about changes after the report period, which the auditor supplements with other evidence based on risk. A SOC 2 Type 1 report addresses different criteria at a point in time and would not fill the gap.

questions.q: A SOC 1 Type 2 report from a payroll processor lists complementary user entity controls (CUECs), including that the user entity reviews payroll registers for accuracy. What is the user auditor's responsibility regarding these CUECs?
choices: Determine whether the user entity has designed and implemented the relevant CUECs and, if relying on them, test their operating effectiveness
None, because CUECs are the service auditor's responsibility
Report the CUECs as deficiencies in the service organization's controls
Request that the service organization perform the CUECs
questions.exp: The service organization's control objectives are achieved only if user entities perform the CUECs, so the user auditor must evaluate them at the client. They are not deficiencies; they are part of the designed control system.

questions.q: A SOC 1 report states that the service organization uses a subservice data center and presents it using the carve-out method. What does this mean for the user auditor?
choices: The subservice organization's controls were fully tested by the service auditor
The carve-out method applies only to SOC 2 reports
The subservice organization's controls are excluded from the report, so the user auditor may need other evidence, such as the subservice organization's own SOC report, about relevant controls
The user auditor cannot use the report at all
questions.exp: Under the carve-out method, the subservice organization's controls are excluded from the description and testing, though complementary subservice organization controls are identified. The inclusive method, by contrast, covers the subservice organization's controls within the report.

questions.q: An auditor observes the client's data center for 30 minutes and sees that the door requires a badge and that visitors sign in. What is the main limitation of this evidence?
choices: Observation is more persuasive than reperformance
Observation provides evidence about the entire audit period
Observation is never acceptable audit evidence
Observation provides evidence only at the time observed and may be affected by the auditor's presence
questions.exp: Observation is limited to the point in time and people may act differently while watched, so it should be supplemented with evidence such as access logs over the period. It is a valid procedure, just limited in scope.

questions.q: During a walkthrough of the sales process, an auditor follows a single transaction from order entry through invoicing and posting to the general ledger, examining documents and system screens. What is the primary purpose of this walkthrough?
choices: To confirm the understanding of the process and evaluate whether relevant controls are designed and implemented
To test the operating effectiveness of controls for the full year
To identify all fraud in the sales cycle
To substantively test the accuracy of revenue
questions.exp: Walkthroughs confirm the auditor's understanding of transaction flows and help evaluate design and implementation of controls. One transaction cannot establish operating effectiveness over the period.

questions.q: Under the risk assessment standards revised by SAS No. 145, what must the auditor do with respect to the client's IT environment?
choices: Rely solely on the client's SOC reports for IT understanding
Obtain an understanding of the IT environment and identify risks arising from the use of IT and the general IT controls that address them, for relevant applications
Exclude IT from the risk assessment if the client uses packaged software
Test all IT general controls regardless of risk
questions.exp: SAS 145 (AU-C 315) requires the auditor to identify IT applications and aspects of the IT environment subject to risks arising from IT, and the related general IT controls. It does not require testing every ITGC regardless of relevance.

questions.q: An auditor tests the client's quarterly user access review for the ERP system. Which procedure provides the best evidence that the review operated effectively?
choices: Inspect a sample of completed reviews for evidence of reviewer sign-off, verify the user listings were complete, and confirm that access flagged for removal was removed
Read the access review policy
Inquire of the IT director whether reviews occurred
Observe a manager sign the access review form
questions.exp: Effective testing confirms that the reviewer used complete data, actually reviewed it, and that identified issues were resolved. A signature alone may indicate a rubber-stamp review if the underlying listing was incomplete or removals were not made.

questions.q: A client's ERP calculates depreciation automatically. To test this calculation, the auditor recomputes depreciation for a sample of assets using the asset cost, useful life, and method in the master file. What procedure is this?
choices: Inquiry
Reperformance
Observation
Confirmation
questions.exp: Independently executing the calculation to verify the system's result is reperformance (recalculation). Confirmation involves obtaining a direct response from a third party.

questions.q: An external auditor plans to use the work of the client's internal audit function in testing IT general controls. Which factor is most important in deciding the extent of such use?
choices: The number of internal auditors on staff
Whether internal audit uses the same audit software as the external auditor
The cost savings to the client
The objectivity and competence of the internal audit function and whether it applies a systematic, disciplined approach
questions.exp: AU-C 610 requires evaluating internal audit's objectivity, competence, and systematic approach before using its work, with the external auditor retaining sole responsibility for the opinion. Fee savings cannot drive the decision.

questions.q: An auditor performs ITGC testing at an interim date covering January through August, for a December year-end. What should the auditor do regarding the remaining period?
choices: Nothing, because interim results apply to the full year
Obtain evidence about significant changes to the controls since the interim date and perform rollforward procedures appropriate to the risk
Rely on management's representation letter alone
Retest all controls in full at year-end
questions.exp: When controls are tested at an interim date, the auditor obtains evidence about changes in the remaining period, with the extent depending on risk and the length of the period. Full retesting is not required unless risks warrant it.

questions.q: An auditor wants to evaluate segregation of duties within a large ERP system with thousands of users and roles. Which approach is most efficient and effective?
choices: Use a data analytics tool to extract user role assignments and compare them with a conflict matrix of incompatible functions
Inspect printed job descriptions for a sample of employees
Interview each user about their job responsibilities
Review the organizational chart
questions.exp: Automated analysis against a conflict rule set evaluates actual system permissions across the entire population. Organizational charts and job descriptions show intended duties but not what the system actually allows.

questions.q: During ITGC testing, an auditor finds that the database administrator also has the ability to approve journal entries in the ERP application. Management has implemented a monthly independent review of all journal entries posted by the DBA. How should the auditor view this review?
choices: As a substitute for all other ITGCs
As a potential compensating control that, if effective, may mitigate the segregation of duties conflict
As irrelevant because only preventive controls matter
As evidence that the conflict is a material weakness
questions.exp: Compensating controls can reduce the risk from a deficiency to an acceptable level if they are precise enough and operate effectively, which the auditor must test. Detective controls can mitigate risk; they are not irrelevant.

questions.q: An auditor relies on a client's system to calculate sales commissions. Which procedure would best establish that the commission rates used by the system are authorized?
choices: Observe a salesperson receive a commission check
Compare the rates in the system's configuration table with approved commission plans and inspect evidence of authorization for changes to the table during the period
Inquire of the sales manager about the rates
Recalculate total commissions as a percentage of total sales
questions.exp: Comparing the configured rates with approved source documents and testing changes to those settings directly addresses authorization. An overall ratio may look reasonable even if individual rates are unauthorized.

questions.q: When testing whether a client's financial reporting system logs all changes to vendor bank account details, what is the auditor's primary concern about relying on the audit log?
choices: That the log was reviewed by external auditors in prior years
That the log is printed in a readable format
That the log is complete and protected from modification or deletion by the users whose activity it records
That the log is longer than one page
questions.exp: An audit log is reliable evidence only if logging cannot be disabled or altered by the users being monitored. If administrators can edit the log, it may not capture unauthorized changes.

questions.q: An auditor identifies a deficiency in an IT general control. Which consideration is most relevant in evaluating its severity?
choices: Whether the ITGC deficiency was caused by an outsourced provider
How many hours IT staff spent remediating the deficiency
Whether the CIO agrees with the finding
Whether the deficiency could lead to a misstatement through the automated controls, reports, or data that depend on the ITGC, and whether compensating controls exist
questions.exp: ITGC deficiencies are evaluated based on their effect on the application controls and information they support, considering compensating controls. Management's agreement does not determine severity.

questions.q: Which situation is most appropriate for a dual-purpose test?
choices: Reviewing the IT strategic plan
Inspecting a sample of sales invoices for evidence of credit approval while also verifying the invoice amounts agree with shipping documents and posted revenue
Observing a data center door during a walkthrough
Inquiring of IT staff about backup procedures
questions.exp: A dual-purpose test uses the same sample to test a control (credit approval) and obtain substantive evidence (accuracy of recorded amounts). The other procedures gather only understanding or control evidence.

questions.q: An IT auditor needs to determine whether password parameters in the ERP system meet the company's policy. Which evidence is most reliable?
choices: An email from the help desk confirming compliance
A spreadsheet prepared by the IT manager summarizing the settings
A screenshot of the password settings obtained directly by the auditor from the system, or observed being generated
The written password policy
questions.exp: Evidence obtained directly by the auditor from the system is more reliable than information compiled by client personnel. A manager's summary spreadsheet could contain errors or omissions.

questions.q: An auditor wants to verify that the client's ERP prevents posting of journal entries to closed periods. Which procedure provides the best evidence?
choices: Count the number of journal entries posted in the period

In a test environment confirmed to mirror production configuration, or by inspecting the production configuration, verify the period-close setting and attempt or observe a posting to a closed period being rejected
Ask the controller whether closed-period postings are possible
Read the month-end close checklist
questions.exp: Inspecting the configuration and observing the system rejecting a test posting provides direct evidence of an automated preventive control. Inquiry and checklists do not show how the system actually behaves.

questions.q: During an audit, the IT manager provides an export of user accounts generated two days earlier. What should the auditor do to ensure the listing is reliable?
choices: Observe the listing being generated from the system or generate it directly, and verify its parameters, so the population is complete and unaltered
Accept the listing because it is recent
Ask the IT manager to sign the listing
Compare the listing to the prior year's listing
questions.exp: Observing or obtaining the extraction directly reduces the risk that the population was manipulated or filtered. A signature attests to nothing about whether accounts were removed from the file.

questions.q: Management plans to remediate an ITGC deficiency identified in the third quarter by implementing a new access provisioning process in November. For an integrated audit of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, what must the auditor do to conclude the remediated control is effective at year-end?
choices: Test only the old control
Wait until the following year to test the new control
Accept management's statement that the control was implemented
Test the new control for a sufficient period of operation before year-end to obtain evidence it is operating effectively
questions.exp: A remediated control must operate for a sufficient period, and be tested, for the auditor to conclude it is effective as of the assessment date. Management's assertion alone is insufficient evidence.

questions.q: An auditor uses an embedded audit module that continuously flags and records transactions over $50,000 processed by the client's payment system. What is the main advantage of this technique?
choices: It requires no involvement in system design
It eliminates the need for ITGC testing
It allows the auditor to change production data
It enables continuous monitoring of transactions as they are processed, providing evidence in a system with no paper trail
questions.exp: Embedded modules capture selected transactions in real time for later review, which supports continuous auditing in paperless environments. They must be built into the application and still depend on effective change controls.

questions.q: An auditor's documentation of IT controls testing states only 'Tested access controls; no exceptions.' What is the primary deficiency in this documentation?
choices: It should have been prepared by the client
It fails to include the auditor's opinion on the financial statements
It is too long
It does not identify the items tested, procedures performed, evidence obtained, and conclusions reached in enough detail for an experienced auditor to understand the work
questions.exp: Audit documentation standards (AU-C 230) require sufficient detail for an experienced auditor with no previous connection to the engagement to understand the nature, timing, extent, and results of procedures. A bare conclusion does not meet this standard.

questions.q: An auditor plans to test an automated control that calculates interest on customer loans. The ITGCs were not tested this year. What is the most appropriate approach?
choices: Rely on last year's ITGC testing without further procedures
Test one instance of the control and rely on it for the full year
Either test the relevant ITGCs or obtain other evidence that the control operated consistently, such as testing it at multiple points or performing more substantive procedures
Assume the control is ineffective and perform no testing
questions.exp: Testing one instance of an automated control is sufficient only when ITGCs provide evidence it did not change; otherwise the auditor needs other evidence of consistent operation. Prior-year ITGC results alone do not cover changes during the current year.

questions.q: An auditor learns that the client's IT department has performed an upgrade of the general ledger application during the year. What is the most relevant audit procedure?
choices: Request that the upgrade be reversed
Obtain evidence that data was completely and accurately converted, and that relevant automated controls and reports were tested and approved after the upgrade
Rely on the vendor's marketing materials describing the upgrade
Ignore the upgrade if it was performed by the software vendor
