questions.exp: System upgrades and data conversions create risks that balances were not transferred correctly and that controls changed, so the auditor tests conversion reconciliations and post-upgrade control functioning. Vendor involvement does not remove these risks.

questions.q: An auditor needs to determine whether a client's daily automated interface between the billing system and the general ledger transfers all transactions. Which procedure provides the best evidence?
choices: Inspect a sample of interface reconciliations comparing record counts and control totals between the billing system and the GL, including resolution of differences
Inquire of the billing manager whether the interface works
Recalculate a single invoice
Review the interface's design document only
questions.exp: Reconciliations of record counts and totals between systems, with evidence that differences were investigated, test both completeness and accuracy of the interface. A design document shows intent, not operation.

questions.q: An auditor finds that a client's ERP generates a sales cutoff report using parameters entered by the user each time it is run. What should the auditor do to rely on this report?
choices: Recalculate the report total only
Test the report logic and also verify the parameters entered when the report was run, such as dates and entities selected
Test only the report's formatting
Rely on the report because it is system generated
questions.exp: User-entered parameters can alter what a report includes, so the auditor must verify that the correct parameters were used in addition to testing the report's logic. Recalculating the total does not prove the report captured the right transactions.

questions.q: An auditor plans to rely on an automated three-way match in the purchasing application. Testing reveals that developers have unrestricted access to move code into production without approval. What is the most significant implication?
choices: The auditor may be unable to rely on the automated control operating consistently throughout the period without additional evidence
The deficiency affects only the IT department and not the financial statement audit
The auditor can still rely on the match because it was working on the date tested
The three-way match should be tested with a larger manual sample of invoices only
questions.exp: Ineffective program change ITGCs mean the application logic could have been altered during the period, so a point-in-time test of the automated control cannot be extended to the whole period. ITGCs are pervasive and directly support the continued functioning of automated controls.

questions.q: Which grouping best represents the typical domains of IT general controls relevant to financial reporting?
choices: Access to programs and data, program changes, program development, and computer operations
Input, processing and output controls
Edit checks, batch totals and reasonableness tests
Preventive, detective and corrective controls
questions.exp: ITGCs are commonly grouped into access to programs and data, program changes, program development (including acquisition), and computer operations. Input, processing and output controls are application controls that depend on these ITGCs.

questions.q: Under AU-C 315 as amended by SAS 145, after identifying IT applications subject to risks arising from the use of IT, the auditor should:
choices: Perform a penetration test of the entity's network
Identify the related risks arising from IT and the general IT controls that address them
Rely on the entity's IT strategy document without further procedures
Test every ITGC in the entity regardless of relevance
questions.exp: SAS 145 requires the auditor to identify the IT applications and other aspects of the IT environment subject to risks arising from IT, those risks, and the general IT controls that address them. It does not require testing every ITGC or performing penetration tests.

questions.q: An auditor tested an automated interest calculation in a prior year and found it effective. In the current year, ITGCs over program changes were tested and found effective, and no changes were made to the calculation. Which approach is most appropriate?
choices: Rely on management's inquiry that the program is unchanged with no further evidence
Abandon reliance because automated controls must be tested every quarter
Use a benchmarking strategy, verifying that the program has not changed and relying on the prior-year test
Retest the calculation using a sample of 60 loans
questions.exp: Benchmarking (baselining) allows reliance on a prior test of an automated control when change and access ITGCs are effective and evidence shows the program was not changed. Inquiry alone is not sufficient evidence that the program is unchanged.

questions.q: The database administrator at a mid-sized company can directly update records in the general ledger tables outside the application, and these changes are not logged or reviewed. Which risk is most significant?
choices: Slow system performance
Excessive software licensing costs
Unauthorized changes to financial data that bypass application controls
Loss of data during backup
questions.exp: Direct database access bypasses application-level edits, approvals and audit trails, creating risk of unauthorized data changes. Logging and independent review of privileged data changes is a key ITGC over access to data.

questions.q: A company's quarterly user access review sends managers a list of usernames only, without the roles or permissions assigned, and managers approve the list without changes. What is the primary weakness?
choices: The review should be performed by external auditors
The review lacks sufficient precision, because reviewers cannot evaluate whether access rights are appropriate
Managers should not be involved in access reviews
The review is performed too frequently
questions.exp: For a user access review to be effective, reviewers need information such as roles and permissions to judge appropriateness. Approving a bare username list cannot detect inappropriate privileges, so the control lacks precision.

questions.q: An auditor wants to test whether program changes were authorized and tested before being moved to production. Which source provides the most reliable population from which to select a sample?
choices: A list provided by the IT manager of significant changes
Emails between developers
A system-generated log of changes actually made to production code or objects
The list of changes in the change ticketing system
questions.exp: Selecting from system-generated evidence of changes actually deployed tests completeness, including changes made outside the ticketing process. Sampling only from the ticketing system would miss unauthorized changes that bypassed it.

questions.q: Which situation represents a segregation of duties conflict within IT that is most relevant to financial reporting risk?
choices: A business analyst who documents user requirements
A help desk technician who resets passwords after identity verification
A network engineer who configures firewalls
A developer who also has the ability to migrate code to the production environment
questions.exp: A developer with production migration rights can introduce unauthorized or untested code without independent review. Password resets with identity verification and requirements documentation are normal duties without such a conflict.

questions.q: A company terminates an accounts payable clerk on March 1, but HR notifies IT on March 20, and the clerk's network and ERP access remain active in the interim. Which ITGC domain is deficient?
choices: Program changes
Access to programs and data
Program development
Computer operations
questions.exp: Timely removal of terminated users' access is a core control over access to programs and data. Computer operations covers batch processing, backups and incident handling, not user provisioning and deprovisioning.

questions.q: The nightly batch job that posts subledger totals to the general ledger occasionally fails, but no one monitors job completion, and failures are discovered only at month-end close. Which ITGC is deficient?
choices: System development methodology
Logical access security
Job scheduling and monitoring within computer operations
Program change management
questions.exp: Monitoring of scheduled jobs and timely resolution of failures is a computer operations ITGC. The issue is not unauthorized access or code changes, but undetected processing failures.

questions.q: Several system administrators share a single generic 'admin' account on the ERP server. What is the main control concern?
choices: Generic accounts cannot be logged at all
The account password will be longer
Shared accounts reduce licensing costs
Activities cannot be attributed to individual users, undermining accountability and monitoring
questions.exp: Shared privileged accounts prevent individual accountability, because logs show only the generic account. Logging still occurs, but it cannot identify who performed an action, which defeats the purpose of reviewing privileged activity.

questions.q: An organization grants 'firefighter' emergency access to production for urgent fixes. Which control best mitigates the associated risk?
choices: Disabling all logging during emergency access to speed resolution
Allowing all developers permanent emergency access
Time-limited access granted on approved request, with activity logged and reviewed independently afterward
Requiring emergency fixes to be documented in the next annual review
questions.exp: Emergency access should be approved, temporary and subject to logging and after-the-fact independent review. Permanent access or delayed documentation defeats the purpose of controlling privileged emergency changes.

questions.q: A company uses a SaaS general ledger. The provider supplies a SOC 1 Type 2 report with an unmodified opinion. Which statement is correct regarding the company's ITGCs?
choices: The SOC 1 report replaces the need for the company to evaluate any controls
The company has no ITGC responsibilities because the provider handles everything
The company remains responsible for complementary user entity controls, such as provisioning and reviewing its own users' access
The company must test the provider's data center physically
questions.exp: Under a shared responsibility model, user entities retain controls such as user access management and must implement CUECs listed in the SOC report. A physical inspection of the provider is not required when an appropriate SOC report is available.

questions.q: During an ICFR audit, an auditor finds that ITGCs over access to the revenue application were ineffective for the first half of the year but remediated in July. Which consideration is most relevant for automated controls in that application?
choices: The deficiency is automatically a material weakness
Only manual controls are affected by ITGC deficiencies
Whether there is evidence that automated controls and data were not inappropriately altered during the deficient period, such as through review of logs
Remediation in July eliminates all concerns for the year
questions.exp: When ITGCs were ineffective for part of the period, the auditor considers whether alternative evidence (e.g., logs or comparison of program versions) shows that automated controls and data were not compromised. ITGC deficiencies are not automatically material weaknesses; their effect depends on the controls and risks they support.

questions.q: A company's patch management process deploys critical operating system patches to production servers without first testing them in a non-production environment. Which risk is most directly increased?
choices: Backups will be retained too long
The company will violate segregation of duties between AP and AR
Patches could disrupt processing or alter system behavior in production
Users will forget their passwords
questions.exp: Patches are changes to infrastructure, and untested changes can cause outages or unintended effects on applications. Proper change management requires testing before production deployment, including for patches.

questions.q: Which procedure provides the most persuasive evidence that password configuration settings comply with policy for an application relevant to ICFR?
choices: Reading the password policy document
Inspecting the system configuration settings directly in the application or directory service
Inquiry of the IT security manager
Reviewing employee training records
questions.exp: Inspecting the actual configured parameters provides direct evidence of how the system enforces passwords. Policies and inquiry describe intent but do not show that the settings were actually implemented.

questions.q: A company backs up its financial systems nightly, but has never tested restoring data from the backups. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
choices: The backup control is effective because backups are scheduled
There is no assurance that backups can actually be used to recover data when needed
Restoration testing is unnecessary for cloud-based backups
Backups are an application control rather than an ITGC
questions.exp: Without periodic restoration testing, the company cannot know whether backups are complete and usable. Backup and recovery is a computer operations ITGC, not an application control.

questions.q: An auditor identifies that the IT function has an effective process for granting access, but there is no periodic review of privileged access to the operating system and database hosting the ERP. Which type of risk is most likely to be unaddressed?
choices: The risk that financial statements contain classification errors from GAAP misapplication
The risk that privileged users bypass application controls or change data without detection
The risk that end users enter incorrect invoice amounts
The risk that the company overpays for hardware
questions.exp: Privileged access at the database and operating system layers can bypass application controls, so periodic review and monitoring are key. Data entry errors are addressed by application input controls, not privileged access reviews.

questions.q: A company is acquiring a new ERP system to replace its legacy system. Which ITGC area is most directly relevant to ensuring that financial data are completely and accurately converted?
choices: Job scheduling
Physical security of the data center
Program development and acquisition, including data conversion controls
Logical access to the network
questions.exp: System implementation and data migration are covered by program development and acquisition ITGCs, including controls over completeness and accuracy of converted data. Job scheduling and physical security do not address conversion accuracy.

questions.q: A financial reporting spreadsheet calculates the allowance for credit losses and is stored on a shared drive accessible to the entire finance department. Which control is most important for this end-user computing tool?
choices: Requiring larger font sizes for readability
Converting the spreadsheet to PDF monthly
Printing the spreadsheet for physical storage
Restricting access, protecting formulas, and reviewing changes to the spreadsheet logic
questions.exp: EUC tools that support significant accounts need ITGC-like controls, including access restriction, change control over formulas, and review of logic and inputs. Converting to PDF only preserves output and does not prevent errors in calculations.

questions.q: Under PCAOB AS 2201, how do ITGC deficiencies generally affect the evaluation of ICFR?
choices: They are irrelevant unless they relate to the general ledger
They are evaluated in relation to their effect on application controls and the risk of material misstatement in related accounts
They are reported only to the IT department
They are always evaluated as material weaknesses because ITGCs are pervasive
questions.exp: ITGC deficiencies are evaluated based on their effect on the application controls and data they support and the related risk of material misstatement. They are not automatically material weaknesses merely because ITGCs are pervasive.

questions.q: A company uses an identity and access management tool to automatically disable network accounts when HR marks an employee as terminated. What type of control is this?
choices: Manual application control over input
Automated preventive ITGC over access
Detective ITGC over computer operations
Corrective control over data backup
questions.exp: Automatically disabling accounts at termination prevents former employees from gaining access and is an access ITGC. It is preventive because it stops unauthorized access before it can occur.

questions.q: Which control most directly addresses the risk that configuration settings for an automated control (such as a three-way match tolerance) are changed without authorization?
choices: Monthly bank reconciliations
Increasing the tolerance to reduce exceptions
Restricting access to change configuration settings and logging and reviewing configuration changes
Annual security awareness training
questions.exp: Configurable controls depend on access and change controls over their settings, so restricting and monitoring configuration changes protects them. Bank reconciliations are a business process control, not a control over application configuration.

questions.q: An organization's change management policy requires that changes be tested by users. In practice, developers perform and sign off on all testing for their own changes. Which control principle is most directly violated?
choices: Independent user acceptance testing as part of segregation of duties
Data minimization
Least privilege
Defense in depth
questions.exp: User acceptance testing by business owners provides independent assurance that changes meet requirements. A developer approving his or her own work lacks independence, which is a segregation of duties failure rather than a least-privilege issue.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between ITGCs and application controls?
choices: ITGCs replace the need for application controls
Application controls support the effectiveness of ITGCs
ITGCs and application controls are independent and do not affect each other
ITGCs support the continued effective operation of application controls
questions.exp: ITGCs, such as change and access controls, provide the environment in which automated application controls continue to function as designed. The relationship runs from ITGCs to application controls, not the reverse.

questions.q: A company's incident management process logs IT incidents but does not track them to resolution or analyze recurring problems. Which ITGC area is weakest?
choices: Computer operations, including incident and problem management
Program development
Data conversion
Logical access
questions.exp: Tracking incidents to resolution and performing root cause analysis of recurring problems are computer operations activities. Program development relates to new systems, not operational incident handling.

questions.q: An auditor identifies a report from the ERP showing all journal entries over $50,000, which management uses in a review control. Before relying on the review control, the auditor should:
choices: Ask management to sign the report
Evaluate whether the report is complete and accurate, including the ITGCs and report logic that produce it
Recalculate the general ledger totals only
Accept the report because it is system-generated
questions.exp: Information produced by the entity used in a control must be complete and accurate for the control to be effective; this depends on report logic, parameters and supporting ITGCs. System generation alone does not guarantee reliability.

questions.q: Which situation would most likely allow an auditor to reduce testing of ITGCs over an application?
choices: Developers have access to the source code and production
The application is heavily customized
The application is a commercial off-the-shelf package whose source code cannot be modified by the entity
The application is newly custom developed in-house
questions.exp: When the entity cannot modify source code, the risk of unauthorized program changes is lower, which can reduce the extent of program change testing (configuration changes still matter). Custom or heavily modified applications increase program change risk.

questions.q: A company uses infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) cloud hosting for its ERP. Under the shared responsibility model, which ITGC is most likely the company's responsibility rather than the provider's?
choices: Managing operating system patches and user access on the virtual machines it runs
Physical security of the provider's data center
Hypervisor patching
Environmental controls such as power and cooling
questions.exp: In IaaS, the customer manages the guest operating system, applications, data and access, while the provider handles physical facilities and virtualization layers. Physical and environmental controls are the provider's responsibility.

questions.q: An organization's network password policy requires 14-character passwords, but the ERP application uses its own authentication with no complexity requirements. What should the auditor conclude?
choices: The ERP is protected because users must first log on to the network
Application-level authentication is a separate access layer that needs its own controls or must be integrated with the stronger directory authentication
The network policy automatically applies to the ERP
Password requirements are irrelevant for ERP systems
questions.exp: Each layer that independently authenticates users needs adequate controls, unless single sign-on ties it to the stronger directory. Relying on network login ignores the risk of access from within the network using weak application credentials.

questions.q: An auditor tests a key automated control in the payroll system. Which ITGCs are most directly necessary to support reliance on that control throughout the year?
choices: Network bandwidth monitoring
Program change and access controls over the payroll application
Physical access and environmental controls only
Help desk procedures for password resets only
questions.exp: Program change and logical access controls provide assurance the automated control was not altered and that unauthorized users could not circumvent it. Environmental controls address availability, not the integrity of control logic.

questions.q: Which procedure is most effective for testing whether terminated employees' access was removed timely?
choices: Compare a list of terminations from the HR system to account deactivation dates in the application
Ask the IT manager whether terminated users are disabled
Read the termination policy
Review the list of current employees for unusual names
questions.exp: Matching HR termination dates with system deactivation dates provides direct evidence of timeliness. Inquiry and reading policy provide evidence of design only.

questions.q: A company's IT steering committee approves all major projects but no one monitors whether developers follow the documented SDLC methodology. This is primarily a weakness in:
choices: Physical access controls
Output distribution controls
Monitoring of program development ITGCs
Input edit checks
questions.exp: Without monitoring adherence to the SDLC methodology, development controls may not operate as designed. Edit checks and output controls are application controls unrelated to SDLC oversight.

questions.q: An auditor learns that changes to the general ledger application are deployed by an automated pipeline that requires a peer-approved pull request before code can be merged and released. Which evidence best supports the operating effectiveness of this control?
choices: The organization chart of the development team
A walkthrough of one change with the lead developer
Inquiry of developers that they always use the pipeline
Inspection of pipeline configuration enforcing approval, plus testing that it could not be bypassed and that its settings were not changed during the period
questions.exp: For an automated change control, the auditor tests the configuration that enforces approval and the access controls that prevent bypassing or altering it. A single walkthrough or inquiry does not establish that the control could not be circumvented.

questions.q: Which of the following is generally considered an application control rather than an ITGC?
choices: A limit check that rejects payments over a set amount without secondary approval
Monitoring backup job completion
Testing changes before production deployment
Restricting access to the production environment
questions.exp: A limit check operates within a specific application at the transaction level and is an application control. Restricting production access, backup monitoring and change testing are ITGCs that apply across applications.

questions.q: A company outsources IT operations to a managed service provider that administers its servers. Which approach best gives the company assurance over ITGCs performed by the provider?
choices: Rely on the contract's indemnification clause
Assume the provider's controls are effective because it is a large firm
Obtain and evaluate a SOC 1 Type 2 report covering the relevant ITGCs, and implement any complementary user entity controls
Ask the provider for its marketing brochure
questions.exp: A SOC 1 Type 2 report gives evidence about the operating effectiveness of the provider's controls relevant to ICFR, and CUECs must be in place at the company. Indemnification shifts financial loss but provides no evidence about controls.

questions.q: An auditor discovers that the company has no process to monitor changes made by IT administrators to the security settings of the ERP, such as user role definitions. What is the most likely effect?
choices: The financial statements are automatically misstated
Segregation of duties enforced by application roles may not be reliable, because role definitions could change without detection
The auditor can rely on segregation of duties built into the roles without further testing
Only the IT budget is affected
questions.exp: Application-enforced segregation of duties depends on the integrity of role definitions, which unmonitored security changes could compromise. This does not automatically misstate the financial statements but reduces the auditor's ability to rely on role-based controls.

questions.q: Which deficiency would most likely undermine the reliability of automated controls across several financial applications at once?
choices: An incorrect approval limit assigned to one purchasing user
A missing reasonableness check on hours in the payroll application
Weak administrative access controls over the shared database server that hosts all of the financial applications
An undocumented manual review of revenue cut-off
questions.exp: A weakness in a shared infrastructure ITGC affects every application relying on that server, which is why ITGC deficiencies can be pervasive. The other deficiencies are confined to a single application or process.

questions.q: The board of a regional bank has delegated to its CIO the authority both to set the bank's I&T strategic direction and to evaluate whether the CIO's own function is achieving that direction. Which COBIT 2019 governance system principle is most directly compromised?
choices: Dynamic governance system
Governance distinct from management
End-to-end governance system
Holistic approach
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 requires a clear distinction between governance (evaluate, direct, monitor, typically the board) and management (plan, build, run, monitor, executive management). Holistic approach concerns building the system from interacting components, not separating oversight from execution.

questions.q: An internal auditor mapping COBIT 2019 objectives notes that 'Ensured risk optimization' belongs to the domain in which the board evaluates strategic options, directs senior management, and monitors achievement. That domain is:
choices: Align, Plan and Organize (APO)
Evaluate, Direct and Monitor (EDM)
Deliver, Service and Support (DSS)
Monitor, Evaluate and Assess (MEA)
questions.exp: EDM is the single governance domain in COBIT 2019 and contains EDM03 Ensured risk optimization. MEA is a management domain covering performance, internal control, compliance and assurance monitoring, not board-level governance.

questions.q: While tailoring its governance system, a company considers that it relies heavily on outsourced cloud providers, uses agile development, and faces heavy regulatory scrutiny. Under COBIT 2019, these considerations are best described as:
choices: Design factors
Focus areas
Governance components
Alignment goals
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 design factors (e.g., sourcing model for IT, IT implementation methods, compliance requirements) influence how the governance system is tailored. Focus areas are specific governance topics such as cybersecurity or SMEs, not enterprise characteristics.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly reflects the COBIT 2019 goals cascade?
choices: Alignment goals, enterprise goals, stakeholder needs, governance and management objectives
Enterprise goals, stakeholder needs, governance and management objectives, alignment goals
Stakeholder drivers and needs, enterprise goals, alignment goals, governance and management objectives
Governance and management objectives, alignment goals, enterprise goals, stakeholder needs
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 translates stakeholder needs into enterprise goals, then into alignment goals (formerly IT-related goals), and finally into prioritized governance and management objectives. The reversed sequence describes rolling results up, not how goals cascade down.

questions.q: A company has thorough, documented change procedures, but staff routinely bypass them because senior leaders openly reward speed of delivery over compliance. Which COBIT 2019 governance component is the root weakness?
choices: Culture, ethics and behavior
Organizational structures
Principles, policies and procedures
Processes
questions.exp: Culture, ethics and behavior is a distinct COBIT 2019 component, and leadership incentives that undermine compliance are a cultural failure. Policies and procedures exist and are adequate here, so the tempting policy answer misses the actual cause.

questions.q: An enterprise's user access review process is well defined across the enterprise and management measures its performance quantitatively with defined metrics, but there is no systematic program of continuous improvement. Under the COBIT 2019 CMMI-based capability scale, the process is at:
choices: Capability level 5
Capability level 3
Capability level 2
Capability level 4
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 capability level 4 means the process achieves its purpose, is well defined, and its performance is quantitatively measured; level 5 adds continuous improvement. Level 3 lacks the quantitative measurement element.

questions.q: The audit committee wants a COBIT 2019 management objective that specifically covers planning, scoping and executing independent assurance initiatives, such as internal audit reviews of I&T. Which objective fits best?
choices: EDM05 Ensured stakeholder engagement
APO11 Managed quality
MEA04 Managed assurance
MEA02 Managed system of internal control
questions.exp: MEA04 Managed assurance, added in COBIT 2019, addresses planning, scoping and executing assurance initiatives. MEA02 is about continuously monitoring and evaluating the internal control environment, not running independent assurance engagements.

questions.q: A governance gap assessment finds that no one is responsible for data quality, data lifecycle, or treating data as an enterprise asset. Which COBIT 2019 objective, introduced as new in the 2019 version, most directly addresses this gap?
choices: APO14 Managed data
BAI09 Managed assets
APO13 Managed security
DSS06 Managed business process controls
questions.exp: APO14 Managed data was added in COBIT 2019 to cover data as a critical asset, including quality and lifecycle management. BAI09 Managed assets focuses on I&T assets such as hardware and software licenses, not data governance.

questions.q: A mid-sized manufacturer wants COBIT 2019 guidance tailored specifically to small and medium enterprises and to DevOps practices. In COBIT 2019 terminology, these are:
choices: Design factors
Alignment goals
Capability levels
Focus areas
questions.exp: Focus areas in COBIT 2019 are specific governance topics, domains or issues (e.g., SME, cybersecurity, DevOps) addressed by a collection of objectives and components. Enterprise size is a design factor, but the SME and DevOps guidance packages themselves are focus areas.

questions.q: Which of the following is a COBIT 2019 governance framework principle rather than a governance system principle?
choices: Dynamic governance system
Tailored to enterprise needs
Aligned to major related standards and frameworks
Provide stakeholder value
questions.exp: COBIT 2019's three governance framework principles are: based on a conceptual model, open and flexible, and aligned to major standards. The other three are among the six governance system principles.

questions.q: In a RACI chart for EDM03 Ensured risk optimization, which party should normally be Accountable?
choices: The board
The chief risk officer
Internal audit
The CIO
questions.exp: EDM objectives are governance objectives, and COBIT 2019 places accountability for governance with the board. The CRO is typically responsible for managing risk activities (APO12), not accountable for governance-level risk optimization.

questions.q: At a retailer, business unit managers own and operate access controls, an IT risk function sets security policy and monitors compliance, and internal audit provides independent assurance to the board. Under the IIA Three Lines Model, the IT risk function is:
choices: The governing body
Second line
First line
Third line
questions.exp: Second-line roles provide expertise, support, monitoring and challenge on risk-related matters, such as an IT risk or compliance function. Operational owners of controls are first line, and only internal audit's independent assurance is third line.

questions.q: Under NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, establishing the organization's cybersecurity risk management strategy, roles and responsibilities, policy, and oversight of cybersecurity supply chain risk falls primarily under which function?
choices: Identify
Respond
Protect
Govern
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 added the Govern function, which includes organizational context, risk management strategy, roles, policy, oversight and supply chain risk management. In CSF 1.1 several of these outcomes sat in Identify, which makes it the tempting wrong answer.

questions.q: A company's cybersecurity risk management practices are formally approved and expressed as policy and are consistently applied organization-wide, but the organization does not yet adapt its practices based on lessons learned and predictive indicators. Which NIST CSF Implementation Tier best describes it?
choices: Tier 3 Repeatable
Tier 2 Risk Informed
Tier 4 Adaptive
Tier 1 Partial
questions.exp: Tier 3 Repeatable describes formally approved, policy-based practices applied consistently across the organization. Tier 4 Adaptive additionally requires adapting practices based on lessons learned and predictive indicators, which is missing here.

questions.q: A company documents the cybersecurity outcomes it currently achieves, documents the outcomes it wants to achieve given its risk appetite, and then prioritizes actions to close the gaps. Which NIST CSF 2.0 construct is it using?
choices: Implementation Tiers
Informative References
Function categories only
Organizational Profiles
questions.exp: CSF 2.0 Organizational Profiles (Current and Target) describe current and desired outcomes and support gap analysis and action planning. Tiers characterize the rigor of risk governance and management practices, not specific outcome gaps.

questions.q: The CFO of a public company must select a framework for management's annual assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting under SOX Section 404. Which framework is most appropriate?
choices: ITIL 4
COBIT 2019
ISO/IEC 27001
COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013)
questions.exp: The COSO 2013 Internal Control framework is the suitable, recognized framework used for management's ICFR assessment. COBIT 2019 can help design and evaluate IT controls that support ICFR, but it is an I&T governance framework, not an ICFR evaluation framework.

questions.q: Under the COSO 2013 Internal Control framework, the principle that the organization selects and develops general control activities over technology to support achievement of objectives belongs to which component?
choices: Monitoring activities
Control activities
Risk assessment
Information and communication
questions.exp: Principle 11 (general controls over technology) is in the Control Activities component. Information and communication (Principle 13) concerns obtaining and using relevant, quality information, not technology general controls.

questions.q: An organization already uses COBIT 2019 for I&T governance and now wants detailed practice guidance for running its service desk and handling incidents, service requests and problems. Which framework best complements COBIT for this purpose?
choices: ITIL 4
NIST SP 800-53B
COSO ERM 2017
questions.exp: ITIL 4 provides detailed IT service management practice guidance, and COBIT 2019 is explicitly aligned with it. ISO 31000 is a general risk management standard and gives no service desk operating guidance.

questions.q: A SaaS customer's contract requires the vendor to obtain third-party certification of its information security management system. Which standard can the vendor be certified against?
choices: NIST CSF 2.0
ISO/IEC 27002
COBIT 2019
ISO/IEC 27001
questions.exp: ISO/IEC 27001 specifies ISMS requirements and is the certifiable standard. ISO/IEC 27002 is a code of practice giving control guidance and cannot itself be certified against, which makes it the tempting trap.

questions.q: Which governance mechanism best ensures that proposed IT projects are prioritized in line with the company's business strategy?
choices: Project managers ranking projects by technical complexity
An IT steering committee of senior business and IT executives that approves and prioritizes the portfolio
The CIO approving and ranking all projects independently
Internal audit selecting which projects proceed
questions.exp: A steering committee with senior business and IT leadership aligns the I&T portfolio with enterprise strategy. Having internal audit select projects would impair its independence, and a CIO acting alone lacks business-side input.

questions.q: The board learns that completed I&T-enabled investments are never compared after implementation with the value promised in their business cases. Which COBIT 2019 governance objective most directly addresses this weakness?
choices: EDM05 Ensured stakeholder engagement
EDM02 Ensured benefits delivery
EDM01 Ensured governance framework setting and maintenance
EDM04 Ensured resource optimization
questions.exp: EDM02 Ensured benefits delivery focuses on optimizing the value contribution of I&T-enabled investments, including monitoring that expected benefits are realized. EDM04 concerns the adequacy of resources (people, technology), not value realization.

questions.q: A company outsources payroll processing, but no one monitors the provider's performance, contract compliance, or risk. Which COBIT 2019 management objective most directly addresses this gap?
choices: BAI09 Managed assets
APO09 Managed service agreements
DSS01 Managed operations
APO10 Managed vendors
questions.exp: APO10 Managed vendors covers selecting, managing relationships with, and monitoring the performance and risk of vendors. APO09 aligns I&T services and service levels with enterprise needs and is not focused on supplier oversight.

questions.q: A governance initiative documents and optimizes IT processes but ignores staff skills, organizational culture, information flows and supporting infrastructure. Which COBIT 2019 governance system principle does this most directly violate?
choices: End-to-end governance system
Governance distinct from management
Provide stakeholder value
Holistic approach
questions.exp: The holistic approach principle says a governance system is built from several interacting components (processes, structures, culture, information, people and skills, services and infrastructure). End-to-end concerns scope across the whole enterprise, not the mix of components.

questions.q: After a company migrates most of its systems to the cloud and changes its business strategy, its governance team re-evaluates the impact on its governance system. Which COBIT 2019 principle calls for this?
choices: Holistic approach
Dynamic governance system
Open and flexible
Tailored to enterprise needs
questions.exp: The dynamic governance system principle states that when design factors change (e.g., strategy or technology), the impact on the governance system must be reconsidered. Tailoring sets the initial design; the dynamic principle addresses ongoing change.

questions.q: A company's I&T governance program covers only systems run by the IT department; spreadsheets and SaaS tools that business units purchase and operate themselves are excluded. Which COBIT 2019 principle is most directly violated?
choices: Holistic approach
End-to-end governance system
Governance distinct from management
Dynamic governance system
questions.exp: The end-to-end principle requires governance to cover all technology and information processing in the enterprise, wherever it occurs, not just the IT function. Holistic approach concerns the types of components, not the organizational scope.

questions.q: Under COBIT 2019's performance management approach, which statement is accurate?
choices: Both processes and focus areas use a 1-10 maturity scale
Processes receive capability levels and focus areas receive maturity levels
Only governance objectives are rated, using a pass/fail scale
Processes receive maturity levels and focus areas receive capability levels
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 uses a CMMI-based scale: capability levels (0-5) for processes and maturity levels for focus areas. Reversing the two terms is the common trap.

questions.q: 'Security of information, processing infrastructure and applications, and privacy' is an example of which COBIT 2019 element?
choices: Design factor
Enterprise goal
Alignment goal
Governance objective
questions.exp: This is alignment goal AG07; alignment goals (formerly IT-related goals) link enterprise goals to governance and management objectives. Enterprise goals are business-level, such as managed business risk or compliance with external laws.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is a governance responsibility under EDM03 Ensured risk optimization rather than a management activity under APO12 Managed risk?
choices: Collecting data on I&T risk events
Analyzing the likelihood and impact of identified risk scenarios
Maintaining a risk register of I&T risk scenarios
Setting the enterprise's I&T risk appetite and tolerance
questions.exp: Setting risk appetite and tolerance is a board-level governance direction in EDM03. Maintaining risk registers, analyzing scenarios and collecting event data are APO12 management activities.

questions.q: To preserve objectivity in reporting security risk, the chief information security officer (CISO) should ideally report to:
choices: The head of network operations
The external auditor
The CEO or chief risk officer, with direct access to the board or its risk committee
The CIO, whose operations the CISO evaluates
questions.exp: A reporting line outside the IT operations being monitored, with board access, reduces conflicts of interest in escalating security risk. Reporting to the CIO is common but creates a conflict when the CISO must report on IT's own shortcomings.

questions.q: A company wants a framework that integrates risk considerations directly into strategy-setting and performance management across the whole enterprise. Which framework best fits?
choices: COSO Enterprise Risk Management - Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017)
ISO/IEC 27002
COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013)
ITIL 4
questions.exp: COSO ERM 2017 explicitly links risk with strategy and performance. COSO 2013 is focused on internal control over operations, reporting and compliance objectives, not strategy-setting.

questions.q: A federal contractor must select security and privacy controls for an information system using low, moderate, or high control baselines. Which source provides the control catalog and baselines?
choices: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 with SP 800-53B baselines
NIST CSF 2.0 Implementation Tiers
COBIT 2019 capability levels
ISO/IEC 27001 certification scheme
questions.exp: SP 800-53 Rev. 5 provides the security and privacy control catalog, and SP 800-53B defines the low, moderate, high and privacy baselines. CSF Tiers describe the rigor of risk practices, not control baselines.

questions.q: Business units at a growing company frequently purchase SaaS applications on corporate cards without IT involvement. Which governance response is most appropriate?
choices: Adopt a policy requiring IT and vendor risk review of all technology acquisitions regardless of funding source
Block all SaaS applications at the firewall
Allow business units to decide freely because they bear the cost
Have internal audit approve each SaaS purchase before it is made
questions.exp: A policy that brings all technology acquisitions under governance review addresses shadow IT while still enabling the business. Internal audit approving purchases would impair its independence, and blanket blocking ignores legitimate business needs.

questions.q: A company decides to create an architecture review board with defined membership and decision rights over technology standards. Which COBIT 2019 governance component does this most directly establish?
choices: Information
Services, infrastructure and applications
Organizational structures
People, skills and competencies
questions.exp: Organizational structures are the key decision-making entities, such as boards and committees, with defined roles and decision rights. People, skills and competencies concerns the capabilities of individuals, not decision-making bodies.

questions.q: Using COBIT 2019 design factors, an enterprise that outsources most of its IT operations to cloud service providers would most likely assign higher priority to which management objective?
choices: DSS03 Managed problems
APO10 Managed vendors
BAI03 Managed solutions identification and build
BAI04 Managed availability and capacity
questions.exp: When the sourcing model design factor emphasizes outsourcing, vendor management becomes more important. In-house build activities such as BAI03 become less important when solutions are sourced from providers.

questions.q: A heavily regulated insurer applies the COBIT 2019 compliance requirements design factor and finds it rates very high. Which management objective is most likely to receive increased priority?
choices: APO11 Managed quality
BAI08 Managed knowledge
MEA02 Managed system of internal control
MEA03 Managed compliance with external requirements
questions.exp: MEA03 covers evaluating whether I&T processes and I&T-supported business processes comply with laws, regulations and contracts. MEA02 is about monitoring internal controls generally and is not specifically about external compliance requirements.

questions.q: Using NIST CSF 2.0, a company discovers it has no current inventory of its hardware, software, services and data. Which function and category does this gap fall under?
choices: Identify - Asset Management
Detect - Continuous Monitoring
Protect - Platform Security
Govern - Organizational Context
questions.exp: Asset Management (ID.AM) in the Identify function covers inventories of hardware, software, services and data. Platform Security in Protect covers securing those assets once they are known.

questions.q: Which metric is most appropriate for measuring COBIT 2019 alignment goal AG03, 'Realized benefits from I&T-enabled investments and services portfolio'?
choices: Percentage of I&T-enabled investments for which claimed benefits were met or exceeded
Number of servers patched each month
Average service desk call resolution time
Percentage of projects delivered on time and within budget
questions.exp: AG03 is about realized value, so the share of investments achieving their claimed benefits measures it directly. On-time, on-budget delivery measures program delivery (AG09); a project can meet schedule and still deliver no value.

questions.q: A 40-employee company is adopting COBIT 2019 for the first time. Which approach is most consistent with the framework?
choices: Adopt ITIL instead, because COBIT is suitable only for large enterprises
Use the design factors and the SME focus area to prioritize objectives and set appropriate target capability levels
Implement all 40 governance and management objectives at capability level 5
Implement only management objectives and skip governance objectives to save cost
questions.exp: COBIT 2019 is designed to be tailored, using design factors such as enterprise size and focus areas such as SME to prioritize objectives and set realistic targets. Requiring level 5 for all objectives ignores the tailoring principle.

questions.q: A company requires employees to enter a password and then answer a security question to log on to the payroll system remotely. Management describes this as multi-factor authentication. Which assessment is correct?
choices: It is not multi-factor because remote access cannot use passwords
It is not multi-factor because both items are something the user knows
It is multi-factor because two separate prompts are used
It is multi-factor because security questions are a possession factor
questions.exp: Multi-factor authentication requires factors from different categories (know, have, are). A password and a security question are both knowledge factors, so this is only two-step, single-factor authentication.

questions.q: Which authentication method provides the strongest protection against phishing attacks that trick users into entering credentials on a fake website?
choices: Security questions with obscure answers
Longer passwords with special characters
FIDO2 hardware security keys bound to the legitimate site
SMS one-time passcodes
questions.exp: FIDO2/WebAuthn authenticators are phishing-resistant because they cryptographically bind authentication to the legitimate origin. SMS codes can be relayed by a phishing site in real time, so they remain vulnerable.

questions.q: Under NIST SP 800-63B guidance on memorized secrets (passwords), which practice is recommended?
choices: Requiring a mix of character types instead of allowing longer passphrases
Screening new passwords against lists of commonly used or previously breached passwords
Forcing password changes every 60 days regardless of compromise
Allowing password hints accessible to unauthenticated users
questions.exp: SP 800-63B recommends checking new passwords against breached and common-password lists and favors length over composition rules. It advises against periodic forced changes absent evidence of compromise, which is the common trap.

questions.q: An employee transfers from accounts payable to treasury. Six months later, she still holds AP invoice-entry access in addition to her new treasury payment-release access. Which issue does this illustrate?
choices: Excessive session timeout
Privilege creep resulting in a segregation of duties conflict
Tailgating
A biometric false acceptance
questions.exp: Access that accumulates through role changes (privilege creep) can create incompatible combinations, here entering invoices and releasing payments. Access should be adjusted at transfer and caught in periodic recertification.

questions.q: A hospital grants clinicians access to patient records based on attributes such as their department, the patient's assigned care team, the time of day and the device used. This model is:
choices: Attribute-based access control
Discretionary access control
Rule of two-person integrity
Mandatory access control
questions.exp: Attribute-based access control evaluates multiple attributes of the user, resource and environment to make dynamic decisions. Discretionary access control lets resource owners grant access at their own discretion without such policy attributes.

questions.q: A military contractor classifies documents as Confidential, Secret or Top Secret, and users can access only documents at or below their clearance; owners cannot override these labels. Which access control model is in use?
choices: Mandatory access control
Attribute-based access control with owner discretion
Discretionary access control
Role-based access control
questions.exp: Mandatory access control enforces system-assigned security labels and clearances that owners cannot change. In discretionary access control, the data owner decides who gets access.

questions.q: A company is selecting a biometric fingerprint system for its data center. Increasing the system's sensitivity reduces false acceptances but increases false rejections. Which metric is most useful to compare the overall accuracy of competing systems?
choices: Crossover error rate (equal error rate)
False rejection rate alone
Enrollment time
False acceptance rate alone
questions.exp: The crossover error rate is where FAR equals FRR; a lower CER indicates a more accurate system overall. Looking at FAR or FRR alone ignores the trade-off between them.

questions.q: For a highly secured data center, which biometric error type is most dangerous from a security standpoint?
choices: Failure to enroll
False acceptance, because an unauthorized person is granted entry
Long processing time
False rejection, because authorized staff are delayed
questions.exp: A false acceptance (Type II error) lets an impostor in, directly compromising security. False rejections (Type I errors) inconvenience authorized users but do not grant unauthorized access.

questions.q: Employees at a data center routinely hold the door open for people walking behind them. Which physical control most directly addresses this tailgating risk?
choices: CCTV cameras recording the entrance
An access control vestibule (mantrap) that allows only one person through at a time
Annual review of badge holder lists
Visitor sign-in sheets at reception
questions.exp: A vestibule or mantrap physically prevents more than one person from entering on a single authentication. CCTV is detective and records tailgating but does not prevent it.

questions.q: A company's server room is protected by a badge reader. Which additional procedure best detects unauthorized physical access attempts?
choices: Periodically reviewing badge access logs and failed entry attempts, investigating anomalies
Painting the door to blend into the wall
Posting a sign that the room is restricted
Issuing badges to all employees for convenience
questions.exp: Reviewing badge logs and failed attempts is a detective control that identifies unauthorized or suspicious access. Signs and camouflage are deterrents at best and do not detect anything.

questions.q: Which control best implements the principle of least privilege for system administrators who occasionally need domain administrator rights?
choices: Sharing a single domain admin password among administrators
Using a privileged access management tool that grants just-in-time elevated access with approval, password vaulting and session recording
Allowing administrators to grant themselves rights as needed
Granting all administrators permanent domain admin rights
questions.exp: Just-in-time privileged access with vaulted credentials and recorded sessions limits standing privileges and creates accountability. Permanent or self-granted rights contradict least privilege.

questions.q: A company implements single sign-on (SSO) using SAML federation for its cloud applications. Which is the most significant risk introduced?
choices: Audit trails become impossible to produce
Compromise of the SSO credential could grant access to all connected applications, so strong MFA on the identity provider is critical
Users can no longer access cloud applications remotely
Users must remember more passwords
questions.exp: SSO concentrates access in one credential, so its compromise has broad impact; strong MFA and monitoring at the identity provider mitigate this. SSO reduces, rather than increases, the number of passwords users manage.

questions.q: An application service account used for nightly batch integration has a password that never expires and is known by several developers. Which control is most appropriate?
choices: Disable logging for the service account to improve performance
Give the service account domain administrator rights to avoid failures
Email the password to the developers each quarter
Store the credential in a secrets vault, rotate it, restrict interactive logon, and limit knowledge of it
questions.exp: Service account credentials should be vaulted, rotated and restricted so they cannot be misused interactively. Granting broad rights or emailing passwords increases exposure.

questions.q: Under NIST SP 800-53, the account lockout control that limits consecutive invalid logon attempts and locks the account or delays further attempts is primarily designed to mitigate:
choices: Denial of service against web servers
Online password guessing (brute force) attacks
Insider misuse of authorized access
Physical theft of laptops
questions.exp: AC-7 Unsuccessful Logon Attempts limits repeated guessing of credentials. Insider misuse involves valid credentials and would not trigger lockouts.

questions.q: A user leaves her workstation unlocked while at lunch, and a coworker uses it to approve a payment. Which control would most directly have prevented this?
choices: Automatic session lock after a short period of inactivity requiring re-authentication
Installing antivirus software
Encrypting the workstation hard drive
Annual access recertification
questions.exp: Device or session lock (SP 800-53 AC-11) prevents use of an unattended, logged-in session. Full-disk encryption protects data at rest when a device is off or stolen, not an active unlocked session.

questions.q: Which approach best reflects a zero trust architecture as described in NIST SP 800-207?
choices: Granting broad network access after VPN logon
Continuously verifying identity, device posture and context for each access request, regardless of network location
Relying solely on a strong perimeter firewall
Trusting all devices once they are inside the corporate network perimeter
questions.exp: Zero trust removes implicit trust based on network location and evaluates each access request per policy. Granting broad access after VPN logon is the perimeter-based model zero trust replaces.

questions.q: An auditor reviewing access to the ERP finds 25 active accounts belonging to employees who left the company more than 90 days ago, though none were used after termination. What is the best conclusion?
choices: No deficiency exists because the accounts were not used
The deprovisioning control is deficient even though no misuse occurred
The deficiency is in change management rather than access
The deficiency is only a physical security issue
questions.exp: A control deficiency exists when the control does not operate as designed, regardless of whether harm occurred. Lack of misuse may affect severity but does not eliminate the deficiency.

questions.q: A company's visitor policy requires visitors to sign in, show identification, wear a distinguishable badge and be escorted at all times. Which risk is primarily being addressed?
choices: Network intrusion from external attackers
Weak passwords
Loss of data from failed backups
Unauthorized physical access and activity by non-employees
questions.exp: Visitor identification, badges and escorts restrict and monitor non-employees' physical presence. These controls do not address network intrusions or password strength.

questions.q: A company's access request form lets requesters check any combination of application roles. Which control most effectively prevents users from being granted conflicting roles?
choices: Allowing managers to approve all requests without restriction
Reviewing access only when an audit is scheduled
Annual review of the request form layout
An automated segregation of duties rule set that flags or blocks conflicting role combinations before provisioning
questions.exp: A preventive SoD rule set checks requested roles against a conflict matrix before access is granted. Unrestricted manager approval often misses conflicts because managers may not know which combinations are incompatible.

questions.q: Which situation represents a possession factor of authentication?
choices: A fingerprint scan
A one-time code generated by an authenticator app on a registered smartphone
A personal identification number
A passphrase
questions.exp: A code from a registered device proves possession of that device, a 'something you have' factor. A PIN and passphrase are knowledge factors, and a fingerprint is an inherence factor.

questions.q: A company's data center is in a multi-tenant building. Which physical control layering is most appropriate?
choices: Building perimeter security, a badge-controlled data center entrance, locked server cages or racks, and monitoring with CCTV
Posting guards only during business hours with no other controls
A single lock on the building's main entrance
Relying on network firewalls to protect servers
questions.exp: Defense in depth for physical security layers perimeter, facility, room and rack controls, with monitoring. Network firewalls do nothing to stop someone physically reaching a server.

questions.q: An attacker uses lists of usernames and passwords stolen from other websites to attempt logons to a company's customer portal. Which control is most effective against this credential stuffing attack?
choices: Multi-factor authentication combined with detection and blocking of automated logon attempts
Displaying a privacy notice on the logon page
Requiring password changes every 30 days
Encrypting the customer database at rest
questions.exp: MFA prevents logon with stolen passwords alone, and bot detection or rate limiting blocks automated attempts. Encryption at rest protects stored data but does nothing to stop logons with valid stolen credentials.

questions.q: A small company has only one IT administrator, who both creates user accounts and reviews the access logs. Which compensating control is most appropriate?
choices: Giving the administrator more privileges
Allowing the administrator to approve his own access changes
Having a business manager independent of IT periodically review user access lists and administrator activity reports
Eliminating access logging
questions.exp: When segregation of duties is impractical, independent review by someone outside the function compensates for the conflict. Eliminating logging removes the evidence needed for any review.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of role-based access control (RBAC)?
choices: Access is granted only to the system administrator
Permissions are assigned to roles based on job functions, and users receive permissions by being assigned to roles
Access is granted based on clearance labels that users cannot change
Users choose who else can access the files they create
questions.exp: RBAC simplifies administration and supports least privilege by tying permissions to job roles. The ability of users to decide who accesses their files describes discretionary access control.

questions.q: An organization's remote access policy allows employees to connect from personal devices. Which control best reduces the risk of a compromised personal device introducing malware into the network?
choices: Allowing any device with a valid password
Network access control that checks device posture (patch level, endpoint protection) before granting access
Encrypting email attachments
Requiring users to sign an acceptable use policy only
questions.exp: Device posture checks enforce minimum security before connection, limiting risk from unmanaged devices. A signed policy communicates expectations but does not technically prevent a compromised device from connecting.

questions.q: A finance company keeps its backup tapes in an unlocked cabinet in an office hallway. Which risk is most directly created?
choices: Slow restoration times
Incompatibility with new tape drives
Inability to perform backups
Unauthorized removal or disclosure of sensitive data on the tapes
questions.exp: Unsecured backup media can be stolen or copied, exposing sensitive data. Physical access controls (and encryption) are needed for media, wherever it is stored.

questions.q: Which control is most effective in ensuring that privileged database administrator activities are appropriate?
choices: Allowing DBAs to review their own activity logs
Logging privileged activities to a tamper-resistant repository that DBAs cannot alter, reviewed by an independent party
Requiring DBAs to change passwords monthly
Disabling audit logging to protect performance
questions.exp: Independent review of tamper-resistant logs provides accountability over powerful users. Self-review is ineffective because the person reviewing is the one being monitored.

questions.q: A company issues employees proximity badges for building entry. An employee reports her badge lost. What is the most important immediate action?
choices: Deactivate the lost badge in the access control system
Wait until the next quarterly access review to disable it
Reprogram all building door locks
Issue a second badge while leaving the first active
questions.exp: Promptly deactivating the lost credential prevents its use by whoever finds it. Waiting for a periodic review leaves a window of unauthorized access.

questions.q: Under the principle of need-to-know, which situation is a violation even though the user has appropriate clearance?
choices: A payroll analyst with access to all employee salary data browses salaries of executives unrelated to her assigned tasks
A help desk technician resets a password after verifying identity
An auditor views data within the scope of the audit
A manager approves a subordinate's access request
questions.exp: Need-to-know restricts access to information required for specific tasks, even if the user has broad authorization. The other activities are consistent with assigned duties.

questions.q: An internal auditor finds that default vendor passwords on a newly installed network switch were never changed. Which risk is most significant?
choices: The switch warranty will be voided
Attackers can easily gain administrative access using publicly known credentials
Users will be locked out of the network
The switch will have lower throughput
questions.exp: Default credentials are published and widely known, making unauthorized administrative access trivial. Configuration baselines should require changing defaults before deployment.

questions.q: A company wants to restrict access to its sales database so that each regional sales manager can see only customers in her region. Which control most directly accomplishes this?
choices: Requiring stronger passwords
Row-level security that filters data based on the user's region attribute
Encrypting the database
Logging all queries
questions.exp: Row-level (data-level) security restricts which records users can view based on attributes. Encryption and passwords control access to the database overall, not which rows a legitimate user can see.

questions.q: Which of the following is a detective physical access control?
choices: Bollards in front of the building
A mantrap
Motion sensors and alarms that alert security when a restricted area is entered after hours
A locked server cage
questions.exp: Motion sensors and alarms detect and alert on intrusion. Locks, mantraps and bollards are preventive controls that stop or impede access.

questions.q: When an employee is terminated involuntarily, which sequence of actions is most appropriate?
choices: Disable logical access and collect physical access credentials at or before the time of notification
Collect the badge but leave system access active for knowledge transfer
Disable access at the next quarterly review
Allow the employee two weeks to transfer files, then disable access
questions.exp: For involuntary terminations, access should be revoked at or before notification to prevent retaliation or data theft. Delaying revocation, even for knowledge transfer, creates an unnecessary window of risk.

questions.q: A company uses biometric hand geometry readers but allows employees to bypass them by entering a four-digit code posted next to the reader. What is the most significant weakness?
choices: Hand geometry is less accurate than retina scanning
The bypass code undermines the strength of the biometric control, effectively reducing it to a shared knowledge factor
The reader should be placed inside the room
Biometrics have high false rejection rates
questions.exp: A widely known bypass code lets anyone enter, so the effective control is only as strong as the posted code. Comparing biometric types is irrelevant when the control can be bypassed.

questions.q: Which access control activity best detects users whose access no longer matches their job responsibilities?
choices: Account lockout after failed attempts
Single sign-on
Periodic user access recertification by business owners
Password complexity enforcement
questions.exp: Access recertification has business owners confirm that each user's access remains appropriate, detecting excessive or outdated rights. Password complexity and lockout protect authentication but do not evaluate whether rights are appropriate.

questions.q: A company's cloud storage buckets containing customer files are set to allow public read access because a developer needed to share a file quickly. Which control would most effectively prevent this misconfiguration?
choices: Increasing storage capacity
Annual security awareness training
Organization-wide policy guardrails that block public access settings unless an approved exception exists, with continuous configuration monitoring
Encrypting files before upload
questions.exp: Preventive guardrails and configuration monitoring stop or quickly detect public exposure of storage. Encryption at rest typically does not prevent access through a public link, because the provider decrypts for authorized reads.

questions.q: Which is the best example of an access control that enforces separation of duties under NIST SP 800-53 AC-5?
choices: Requiring 12-character passwords
Configuring the ERP so the user who creates a journal entry cannot approve it
Logging all logon attempts
Locking a session after 15 minutes
questions.exp: AC-5 Separation of Duties defines and enforces incompatible duties, such as preventing a preparer from approving the same entry. Passwords, session locks and logging serve different control objectives.

questions.q: A bank is redesigning entry to its vault room. Which combination provides true multi-factor authentication?
choices: A badge and a second badge issued to the same employee
A PIN and a memorized passphrase
A password and the answer to a security question
A smart card badge plus a PIN entered on the reader
questions.exp: A smart card (something you have) combined with a PIN (something you know) uses two different factor categories. Two badges or two memorized secrets are each a single factor type repeated.

questions.q: A company hosts a public web server and an internal accounting database. Which network design best protects the database if the web server is compromised?
choices: Place both servers on the same internal subnet behind one firewall
Place the web server inside the internal network and the database in the DMZ
Place the database directly on the internet with strong passwords
Place the web server in a screened subnet (DMZ) and the database on an internal segment, with firewall rules allowing only required traffic between them
questions.exp: A DMZ isolates internet-facing systems so a compromise does not give direct access to internal systems; only narrowly defined traffic is allowed inward. Putting both servers on one internal subnet lets an attacker pivot directly to the database.

questions.q: A firewall tracks the state of active connections and allows inbound packets only if they belong to a session initiated from inside. This is a:
choices: Application-level proxy firewall
Web application firewall
Static packet-filtering firewall
Stateful inspection firewall
questions.exp: Stateful inspection firewalls maintain a connection table and evaluate packets in the context of established sessions. Static packet filters evaluate each packet independently against rules without session awareness.

questions.q: A company's e-commerce site is repeatedly targeted by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which control is specifically designed to filter this type of traffic?
choices: A network-layer packet-filtering router
A web application firewall
A VPN concentrator
A DHCP server
questions.exp: A WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic at the application layer and blocks attacks such as SQL injection and XSS. Packet-filtering routers examine IP addresses and ports and cannot interpret web application payloads.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes an intrusion detection system (IDS) from an intrusion prevention system (IPS)?
choices: An IDS blocks traffic; an IPS only logs it
An IDS monitors and alerts on suspicious activity; an IPS sits inline and can block malicious traffic automatically
An IPS is a physical security device
Both only scan for viruses on endpoints
questions.exp: An IDS is a detective control that alerts, while an IPS is inline and preventive. Reversing their roles is the common trap.

questions.q: To reduce the scope of its PCI DSS assessment, a retailer isolates systems that store, process or transmit cardholder data from the rest of the corporate network. This practice is:
choices: Network segmentation
Network address translation
Port mirroring
Load balancing
questions.exp: Segmentation separates the cardholder data environment so that only it, and connected systems, fall in scope, while also limiting attackers' lateral movement. NAT hides internal addresses but does not isolate environments.

questions.q: A ransomware infection on one employee's laptop quickly spreads to servers across the company because the network is flat. Which architectural control would most directly limit such lateral movement?
choices: Micro-segmentation with restrictive rules between workloads and user segments
Adding more DNS servers
Using a single large VLAN for all devices
Increasing internet bandwidth
questions.exp: Micro-segmentation restricts east-west traffic so compromised systems cannot freely reach others. A single large VLAN is effectively a flat network and enables spread.

questions.q: An organization configures its firewalls so that all traffic is blocked unless explicitly permitted by a rule. This approach is:
choices: Fail-open
Default allow
Implicit trust
Default deny
questions.exp: Default deny (deny by default, allow by exception) minimizes exposure to unanticipated traffic. Default allow permits anything not explicitly blocked, leaving unknown services exposed.

questions.q: An attacker sets up a wireless access point in a coffee shop with the same network name as the shop's legitimate Wi-Fi to intercept customers' traffic. This attack is called:
choices: A SYN flood
A replay attack on Kerberos
A SQL injection
An evil twin attack
questions.exp: An evil twin is a rogue access point mimicking a legitimate SSID to intercept traffic. A SYN flood is a denial-of-service attack that does not involve impersonating a network.

questions.q: Which wireless security protocol provides the strongest protection for a corporate Wi-Fi network?
choices: WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X authentication
An open network with a hidden SSID
WEP
WPA with TKIP
questions.exp: WPA3-Enterprise with 802.1X provides individual authentication and strong encryption. Hiding the SSID offers no real protection because it is easily discovered.

questions.q: A company's online store is overwhelmed by traffic from thousands of compromised devices, making it unavailable to customers. Which control is most effective?
choices: Adding a second web server in the same data center only
Encrypting the product database
Using a DDoS mitigation service or content delivery network that absorbs and filters malicious traffic upstream
Requiring stronger customer passwords
questions.exp: Distributed denial-of-service attacks are best handled by upstream scrubbing services or CDNs with large capacity. One additional local server is quickly overwhelmed, and passwords and encryption do not address traffic volume.

questions.q: Employees working remotely need secure access to internal applications over the internet. Which technology creates an encrypted tunnel between the remote device and the corporate network?
choices: A virtual private network (VPN)
A network switch
A DMZ
A honeypot
questions.exp: A VPN encrypts traffic between the remote endpoint and the corporate network across untrusted networks. A DMZ is a network zone, not a means of securing remote connections.

questions.q: A security team deploys a decoy server with fake data that has no legitimate business use, so any access to it indicates malicious activity. This is a:
choices: Proxy server
Bastion host for administration
Honeypot
Load balancer
questions.exp: A honeypot lures attackers and generates high-fidelity alerts because legitimate users have no reason to access it. A bastion host is a hardened system intentionally used for legitimate administrative access.

questions.q: Administrators must connect to sensitive production servers. Which design best controls and monitors this access?
choices: Opening remote desktop to the internet for convenience
Requiring administrators to connect through a hardened jump server (bastion host) with MFA and session logging
Allowing administrators to connect directly from any workstation
Sharing a single administrator account
questions.exp: A jump server centralizes privileged access, enforcing MFA and logging, and limits direct connections to production. Exposing remote desktop to the internet is a common ransomware entry point.

questions.q: A vulnerability scan reveals that Remote Desktop Protocol (TCP port 3389) on a finance server is reachable from the internet. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Block direct internet access to RDP and require access through a VPN or secure gateway with MFA
Ignore it because RDP requires a password
Leave it open but change the port number
Disable logging on the server
