questions.exp: Internet-exposed RDP is frequently exploited for brute-force and ransomware attacks, so it should be reachable only through secure, authenticated channels. Changing the port is security through obscurity and is easily discovered by scanning.

questions.q: Which protocol should replace Telnet for remote administration of network devices?
choices: SSH
HTTP
SNMPv1
FTP
questions.exp: SSH provides encrypted remote administration, while Telnet sends credentials in clear text. FTP and SNMPv1 also transmit credentials unencrypted.

questions.q: A company's mail domain is being spoofed in phishing emails sent to its customers. Which combination of controls best helps receiving mail servers reject spoofed messages?
choices: Stateful firewall rules on the company's internal network
A larger mailbox quota
SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for the company's domain
Antivirus on employee laptops
questions.exp: SPF, DKIM and DMARC let receiving servers verify that mail claiming to be from the domain is authorized and authentic, and tell them how to handle failures. Internal firewall rules do not affect mail sent from attackers' infrastructure.

questions.q: A security operations center collects logs from firewalls, servers and applications into one platform that correlates events and generates alerts. This platform is a:
choices: Network address translation device
Data loss prevention system
Virtual private network
Security information and event management (SIEM) system
questions.exp: A SIEM aggregates and correlates logs across sources to detect security events. DLP focuses on preventing sensitive data from leaving the organization.

questions.q: Which device operates mainly at OSI layer 3 and forwards traffic between different networks based on IP addresses?
choices: Hub
Router
Layer 2 switch
Repeater
questions.exp: Routers operate at the network layer, forwarding packets between networks using IP addresses. Layer 2 switches forward frames within a network using MAC addresses.

questions.q: An organization wants to inspect outbound web traffic for malware and enforce acceptable-use policies for remote and office users alike, without backhauling traffic through headquarters. Which architecture best fits?
choices: Disabling remote work
Port forwarding on home routers
A single on-premises proxy at headquarters
A secure access service edge (SASE) model with cloud-delivered secure web gateway
questions.exp: SASE delivers network security functions such as secure web gateways from the cloud close to users wherever they are. Backhauling to a single headquarters proxy adds latency and does not scale for remote users.

questions.q: A company's firewall rules have not been reviewed in five years and include many rules with 'any' as source or destination. What is the most appropriate control?
choices: Adding more rules to cover new applications
Disabling the firewall during business hours
Periodic firewall rule review to remove unused, overly permissive or undocumented rules, with business justification for each rule
Replacing the firewall with a router
questions.exp: Regular rule reviews ensure rules are needed, documented and as restrictive as possible. Adding rules without cleanup compounds the risk of overly permissive access.

questions.q: An attacker on the same local network sends forged ARP messages so that traffic intended for the default gateway passes through the attacker's machine. This is an example of:
choices: A man-in-the-middle attack via ARP spoofing
Phishing
A brute-force password attack
A denial-of-service flood
questions.exp: ARP spoofing associates the attacker's MAC address with the gateway's IP, letting the attacker intercept traffic. It is a local-network interception technique, not a volume-based DoS.

questions.q: Which control best detects unusual data flows, such as a server suddenly sending large volumes of data to an unfamiliar external IP address?
choices: Annual security training
Network traffic monitoring and flow analysis with alerting on anomalies
Disk encryption
Password complexity rules
questions.exp: Flow monitoring (e.g., NetFlow) and anomaly detection identify unusual traffic patterns that may indicate exfiltration. Password rules and encryption do not reveal what data are being sent where.

questions.q: Why is egress (outbound) filtering at the network perimeter an important control?
choices: It limits malware's ability to communicate with command-and-control servers and exfiltrate data
It prevents all phishing emails from arriving
It speeds up inbound web browsing
It is required only for wireless networks
questions.exp: Restricting outbound traffic to approved destinations and ports can disrupt command-and-control and data exfiltration. Egress filtering does not stop inbound phishing emails.

questions.q: A company's manufacturing plant has operational technology (OT) systems controlling production equipment. Which architecture is most appropriate?
choices: Segmenting OT networks from the corporate IT network, with tightly controlled and monitored conduits between them
Placing OT and IT on the same flat network for easier management
Removing all firewalls from the OT network to reduce latency
Connecting OT devices directly to the internet for remote vendor support
questions.exp: Segmentation between IT and OT, with controlled conduits, limits the spread of attacks to systems that control physical processes. Direct internet exposure of OT devices is a major risk.

questions.q: Which DNS security measure helps ensure that DNS responses have not been forged or tampered with?
choices: DHCP reservations
Increasing DNS cache time
Using a single DNS server
DNSSEC digital signatures
questions.exp: DNSSEC uses digital signatures so resolvers can verify DNS data authenticity and integrity, mitigating cache poisoning. Longer cache times could prolong the effects of poisoned records rather than prevent them.

questions.q: A company moves workloads to a public cloud. Which control most directly functions as a virtual firewall for individual cloud instances?
choices: Antivirus on employee laptops
The cloud provider's physical data center guards
Cloud security groups and network access control lists restricting traffic to and from instances
The company's on-premises perimeter firewall
questions.exp: Security groups and network ACLs control traffic to cloud resources at the instance or subnet level and are the customer's responsibility. On-premises firewalls do not inspect traffic that never passes through them.

questions.q: A company uses network address translation (NAT) at its perimeter. Which statement best describes its security effect?
choices: It replaces the need for a firewall
It prevents phishing attacks
It hides internal IP addresses from external networks, but it is not a substitute for firewall filtering
It encrypts all outbound traffic
questions.exp: NAT conceals internal addressing, which offers some obscurity, but it does not enforce security policy like a firewall. It provides no encryption.

questions.q: An organization requires that every device connecting to its network be authenticated and checked for compliance (e.g., patches, endpoint protection) before being placed on the appropriate network segment. This is:
choices: A demilitarized zone
Port address translation
Network address translation
Network access control (NAC)
questions.exp: NAC enforces authentication and posture checks before granting network access and can quarantine noncompliant devices. NAT and PAT translate addresses and do not evaluate device compliance.

questions.q: Which approach best reflects defense in depth for a company's network?
choices: Encrypting data only at rest
Layering perimeter firewalls, segmentation, endpoint protection, monitoring and access controls so that the failure of one control does not expose systems
Relying solely on a strong perimeter firewall
Using one vendor's single security product for everything
questions.exp: Defense in depth uses multiple, overlapping layers of controls. Relying only on the perimeter fails once an attacker gets inside, for example through phishing.

questions.q: A company's internal network allows employees to plug any device into wall jacks in conference rooms and gain full network access. Which control would most directly address this?
choices: Encrypting the file servers
Port security or 802.1X authentication on switch ports, with unused ports disabled
Posting signs prohibiting personal devices
Increasing bandwidth to conference rooms
questions.exp: 802.1X and port security require authentication before network access and prevent unauthorized devices from connecting. Signs rely on voluntary compliance and do not technically prevent connection.

questions.q: Which statement about TLS is most accurate?
choices: TLS 1.0 is the recommended current version
TLS protects data in transit by providing encryption, integrity and server authentication, and current guidance recommends TLS 1.2 or 1.3
TLS protects data at rest on a server's disk
TLS replaces the need for authentication of users
questions.exp: TLS secures communication channels; older versions such as TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated in favor of 1.2 and 1.3. TLS does not protect stored data or replace user authentication.

questions.q: A penetration tester performs a port scan of a company's external IP range. What is the primary purpose of this step?
choices: To patch vulnerable systems automatically
To train employees
To identify open ports and services that could be attack vectors
To encrypt network traffic
questions.exp: Port scanning maps exposed services so testers (or attackers) can identify potential entry points. It does not remediate vulnerabilities by itself.

questions.q: A company uses a load balancer to distribute customer traffic across several web servers. Which security objective does this most directly support?
choices: Authentication of employees
Availability and resilience of the service
Confidentiality of stored data
Non-repudiation of transactions
questions.exp: Load balancing spreads traffic and allows failover, supporting availability. It does not encrypt stored data or authenticate users.

questions.q: A company's guest Wi-Fi network shares the same network segment as its corporate servers. What is the primary risk?
choices: The guest network will require more IP addresses
Corporate users will be unable to use Wi-Fi
Guests or compromised guest devices could reach internal systems
Guests will experience slower speeds
questions.exp: Without segmentation, untrusted guest devices can access internal resources. Guest networks should be isolated, typically allowing only internet access.

questions.q: An application-level proxy firewall differs from a packet-filtering firewall in that it:
choices: Only examines source and destination IP addresses
Terminates connections and inspects application-layer content before forwarding requests on the client's behalf
Cannot log traffic
Operates exclusively at the physical layer
questions.exp: Proxy firewalls act as intermediaries, inspecting application content for specific protocols. Packet filters examine header information such as IP addresses and ports without understanding application content.

questions.q: A security analyst redirects DNS queries for known malicious domains to an internal server that returns a non-routable address, preventing infected hosts from reaching attacker infrastructure. This technique is a:
choices: DNS zone transfer
VLAN trunk
Reverse proxy
DNS sinkhole
questions.exp: A DNS sinkhole returns false answers for malicious domains to block communication and identify infected hosts. A zone transfer replicates DNS records between servers and is not a blocking technique.

questions.q: Under NIST SP 800-53, which control family includes boundary protection, transmission confidentiality and integrity, and network disconnect controls?
choices: System and Communications Protection (SC)
Awareness and Training (AT)
Physical and Environmental Protection (PE)
Access Control (AC)
questions.exp: The SC family includes SC-7 Boundary Protection, SC-8 Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity, and SC-10 Network Disconnect. AC covers account management and access enforcement rather than network boundary protection.

questions.q: An IPS placed inline at the network perimeter is configured to fail open, so traffic passes uninspected if the device fails. Which trade-off does this configuration reflect?
choices: It prioritizes availability of network traffic over security inspection during a device failure
It converts the IPS into a firewall
It eliminates the need for monitoring
It prioritizes confidentiality over availability
questions.exp: Fail-open keeps traffic flowing when the device fails, favoring availability but allowing uninspected traffic through; fail-closed would block traffic and favor security. It does not change the device's function or remove the need for monitoring.

questions.q: A U.S.-based online retailer with no offices in Europe sells products to consumers in France and Germany and tracks their browsing behavior on its website. Does the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) apply to the retailer's processing of these customers' data?
choices: Only if the retailer stores the data on servers located in the EU
Yes, because GDPR applies to organizations outside the EU that offer goods or services to, or monitor the behavior of, individuals in the EU
No, because the retailer has no establishment in the EU
Only if the retailer has more than 250 employees
questions.exp: GDPR Article 3(2) extends its territorial scope to non-EU organizations that target or monitor people in the EU. Server location is irrelevant to whether GDPR applies.

questions.q: A European subsidiary of a U.S. company discovers that an attacker accessed a database of customer contact and purchase information, creating a risk to individuals' rights. Under GDPR, within what time frame must the company generally notify the supervisory authority?
choices: Within four business days after determining materiality
Within 60 days of discovery
Within 72 hours after becoming aware of the breach
Within 30 days of discovery
questions.exp: GDPR Article 33 requires notification to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach, unless it is unlikely to result in a risk to individuals. Four business days is the SEC Form 8-K timeline for material incidents.

questions.q: A company hires a cloud-based payroll service to process its EU employees' personal data according to the company's instructions. Under GDPR, how are the two parties classified, and what is required between them?
choices: Both are processors because neither collects the data directly
Both are joint controllers and need no written agreement
The company is the controller and the payroll service is a processor, and a written data processing agreement meeting Article 28 is required
The payroll service is the controller, and the company is the processor
questions.exp: The controller determines the purposes and means of processing; a processor acts on its behalf and must be bound by a contract with the terms specified in Article 28. Reversing the roles is a common trap because the service performs the processing.

questions.q: A company replaces customer names in its analytics dataset with random identifiers and keeps the lookup table in a separate, secured system. How does GDPR treat the analytics dataset?
choices: It is exempt from GDPR as long as it is encrypted
It remains personal data because it is pseudonymized and can be re-identified with additional information
It is anonymous data and falls outside GDPR entirely
It is special category data requiring explicit consent
questions.exp: Pseudonymized data is still personal data under GDPR because re-identification is possible using the separately held key, although pseudonymization is a recognized safeguard. Only truly anonymized data, where individuals are not reasonably identifiable, falls outside GDPR.

questions.q: A European customer asks a company to delete all personal data it holds about her. The company must retain her invoices for seven years under tax law. How should the company respond under GDPR?
choices: Delete all of her data, including the invoices, because erasure rights override other laws
Erase personal data that is no longer necessary, retain the invoice data required by law, and explain the basis for retention
Ignore the request until the seven-year period expires
Refuse the request entirely because some data must be retained
questions.exp: The right to erasure (Article 17) does not apply where processing is necessary to comply with a legal obligation, so the company erases what it can and explains what it must keep. Refusing the whole request ignores data that is no longer needed.

questions.q: A health insurer plans to use an AI model to profile members and predict which ones are likely to develop costly conditions, using large volumes of health data. Under GDPR, what must the insurer complete before beginning this processing?
choices: A data protection impact assessment, because the processing is likely to result in a high risk to individuals
Registration of the model with the European Central Bank
A SOC 2 Type 2 examination
A penetration test of the AI model
questions.exp: Article 35 requires a DPIA before processing likely to result in high risk, such as large-scale processing of health data and systematic profiling. A penetration test addresses technical security but not the broader privacy risks a DPIA evaluates.

questions.q: A mobile app requires users to agree to receive marketing from partner companies as a condition of creating an account, through a pre-checked box. Why does this fail GDPR's standard for valid consent?
choices: Consent is never a lawful basis for marketing
Consent must be renewed every 30 days
Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and an unambiguous affirmative act, and it is not freely given when bundled as a condition of a service that does not need it
Consent can be given only in writing on paper
questions.exp: Pre-checked boxes and bundling consent with unrelated service terms do not meet GDPR Articles 4(11) and 7. Consent is a valid basis for marketing when properly obtained, so the problem is how it was obtained.

questions.q: A U.S. company wants to transfer EU employees' personal data to its U.S. headquarters, and the recipient is not certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. Which mechanism most commonly provides a lawful basis for the transfer under GDPR?
choices: Storing the data in a U.S. data center operated by an EU-based company
Encrypting the data before transfer, which removes it from GDPR
Obtaining approval from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission
Standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, supported by a transfer risk assessment
questions.exp: Without an adequacy decision or Data Privacy Framework certification, SCCs (or binding corporate rules) are the typical safeguard for transfers outside the EEA. Encryption is a supplementary measure but does not by itself legalize the transfer.

questions.q: Under GDPR, what is the maximum administrative fine for the most serious infringements, such as violating the basic principles of processing?
choices: A flat €1 million per violation
4% of the EU subsidiary's annual profit
€20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
€10 million or 2% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
questions.exp: Article 83 sets the upper tier at €20 million or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding year, whichever is higher. The €10 million or 2% tier applies to lesser infringements such as certain controller and processor obligations.

questions.q: A software company designing a new customer portal decides at the design stage to collect only the fields needed for the service, set privacy-protective default settings, and build in automated deletion. Which GDPR principle does this best illustrate?
choices: Accountability through annual audits
Data protection by design and by default
Legitimate interest balancing
Data portability
questions.exp: Article 25 requires embedding data protection into system design and making the most privacy-protective settings the default. Data portability is an individual right to receive data in a usable format, not a design principle.

questions.q: A marketing team wants to reuse customer data collected for warranty registration to build profiles for an unrelated advertising partnership. Which GDPR principle is most directly at issue?
choices: Integrity and confidentiality
Storage limitation
Accuracy
Purpose limitation
questions.exp: Purpose limitation requires that data be collected for specified purposes and not further processed in ways incompatible with them. Storage limitation concerns how long data is kept, not how it is reused.

questions.q: A California consumer submits a verified request asking a retailer that is subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the CPRA, to stop selling or sharing her personal information. What must the retailer do?
choices: Comply only if the consumer pays a processing fee
Comply only after the next annual privacy notice update
Stop selling or sharing her personal information, and not discriminate against her for exercising the right
Delete all of her personal information immediately
questions.exp: The CCPA/CPRA gives consumers the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information, and businesses may not retaliate by denying service or charging different prices without a permissible financial incentive. Opting out is distinct from the right to delete.

questions.q: Which business is most likely subject to the CCPA as amended by the CPRA?
choices: A for-profit Texas company doing business in California that annually buys, sells, or shares personal information of 150,000 California consumers
A nonprofit hospital in California with $500 million in revenue
A California state government agency
A California sole proprietorship with $2 million in revenue that does not sell personal information
questions.exp: The CCPA covers for-profit businesses doing business in California that meet a threshold, including buying, selling, or sharing personal information of 100,000 or more consumers or households. Nonprofits and government agencies generally are not covered, and the small business falls below every threshold.

questions.q: A website subject to the CCPA receives a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal from a California visitor's browser. How should the business treat this signal?
choices: As a valid request to opt out of the sale or sharing of the visitor's personal information
As a request to delete the visitor's data
As consent to share the visitor's data with advertisers
As having no legal effect unless the visitor also emails the business
questions.exp: California regulations require businesses to honor opt-out preference signals such as GPC as valid opt-out requests. Treating it as a deletion request overstates what the signal communicates.

questions.q: A hospital outsources medical billing to a company that will receive patients' protected health information (PHI). Under HIPAA, what must be in place before the billing company receives PHI?
choices: A business associate agreement that requires the billing company to safeguard PHI and comply with applicable HIPAA requirements
Written authorization from every patient
A SOC 1 report from the billing company
Registration of the billing company with the Department of Health and Human Services
questions.exp: HIPAA permits covered entities to share PHI with business associates performing functions on their behalf, provided a BAA is in place. Individual patient authorization is not required for treatment, payment, or health care operations.

questions.q: A billing clerk at a medical practice needs patients' insurance information and procedure codes to submit claims. Under the HIPAA Privacy Rule, which standard limits the clerk's access to complete medical histories?
choices: The breach notification rule
The right of access
The minimum necessary standard
The accounting of disclosures requirement
questions.exp: The minimum necessary standard requires covered entities to limit uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum needed for the purpose, typically enforced through role-based access. The right of access is the patient's right to obtain his or her own records.

questions.q: A health clinic discovers a breach of unsecured PHI affecting 750 residents of a single state. Under the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, which notifications are required?
choices: Notice to affected individuals and HHS without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of discovery, plus notice to prominent media outlets in that state
Notice to affected individuals only, within 30 days
Notice to HHS only, in an annual log
No notice, because fewer than 1,000 people were affected
questions.exp: For breaches affecting 500 or more residents of a state, HIPAA requires notice to individuals, HHS, and prominent media within 60 days of discovery. Breaches affecting fewer than 500 individuals may be logged and reported to HHS annually.

questions.q: A physician's laptop containing PHI is stolen. The drive was encrypted consistent with HHS guidance, and the decryption key was not stored with the laptop. What are the clinic's HIPAA breach notification obligations?
choices: Notify all affected individuals within 60 days
Notify the media because more than 500 records were on the laptop
Notification is generally not required because properly encrypted PHI is not 'unsecured PHI'
Notify HHS within 72 hours
questions.exp: The Breach Notification Rule applies to unsecured PHI; encryption meeting HHS guidance, with the key not compromised, provides a safe harbor. This illustrates why encryption of portable devices is a high-value control.

questions.q: A health system wants to share patient data with university researchers without patient authorization. Under HIPAA, which approach would permit this as de-identified data?
choices: Removing the 18 identifiers specified by the safe harbor method, or obtaining an expert determination that the risk of re-identification is very small
Removing only Social Security numbers and medical record numbers
Replacing patient names with initials
Encrypting the data before sending it
questions.exp: HIPAA recognizes two de-identification methods: safe harbor removal of 18 identifier types (with no actual knowledge of re-identification risk) and expert determination. Encrypted data is still PHI because it can be decrypted.

questions.q: Under the HIPAA Security Rule, which of the following is an example of an administrative safeguard rather than a physical or technical safeguard?
choices: Locks on doors to the server room
Automatic logoff of workstations after inactivity
Conducting a periodic risk analysis and implementing a security awareness and training program
Encryption of PHI transmitted over the internet
questions.exp: Administrative safeguards include risk analysis, risk management, workforce training, and security management processes. Automatic logoff and encryption are technical safeguards, and door locks are physical safeguards.

questions.q: A consumer finance company is subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA). Which requirement does the GLBA Privacy Rule impose regarding sharing nonpublic personal information with nonaffiliated third parties?
choices: The company must provide a privacy notice and give consumers a reasonable opportunity to opt out before sharing, subject to certain exceptions
Sharing is permitted without any notice if the third party is in the United States
Sharing requires opt-in consent by written signature
Sharing is prohibited under all circumstances
questions.exp: GLBA requires initial and, where applicable, annual privacy notices and an opt-out right before sharing nonpublic personal information with nonaffiliated third parties, with exceptions such as service providers. It is an opt-out regime, not opt-in.

questions.q: Under the FTC's amended GLBA Safeguards Rule, which element is required of a covered non-bank financial institution's information security program?
choices: Storing all customer data only on premises
Annual SOC 2 Type 2 examination by a CPA firm
Designating a qualified individual to oversee the program and having that individual report in writing to the board at least annually
Appointing a chief privacy officer who reports to the FTC
questions.exp: The Safeguards Rule requires a qualified individual, a written risk assessment, specific safeguards such as MFA and encryption, and at least annual written reporting to the board. It does not mandate a SOC 2 examination.

questions.q: A mortgage broker covered by the FTC Safeguards Rule discovers that unencrypted customer information of 2,000 consumers was acquired without authorization. Under the rule's notification requirement effective in 2024, what must the broker do?
choices: Notify the SEC within four business days
Notify the FTC as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
Notify the FTC only if more than 10,000 consumers are affected
No federal notice is required; only state law applies
questions.exp: The amended Safeguards Rule requires notifying the FTC of a notification event involving the unencrypted information of at least 500 consumers no later than 30 days after discovery. SEC Form 8-K requirements apply to public companies' material incidents, a different regime.

questions.q: A consultant explains that the Trust Services Criteria distinguish confidentiality from privacy. Which statement correctly describes the distinction?
choices: Privacy applies only to employees, and confidentiality applies only to customers
Confidentiality applies only to health information, and privacy applies to all other data
There is no difference; the two categories are interchangeable

Confidentiality addresses information designated as confidential, such as trade secrets and business plans, while privacy addresses the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information
questions.exp: Under the TSC, confidentiality protects information designated as confidential, which may include personal information, while the privacy criteria focus specifically on personal information and the entity's privacy commitments. Personal information may fall under both categories, but they are not interchangeable.

questions.q: A service organization's SOC 2 report includes the confidentiality category. Which control most directly supports the criterion addressing disposal of confidential information?
choices: Procedures to identify confidential information that has reached the end of its retention period and to securely destroy it, with documentation of destruction
Daily backup of confidential files
Multifactor authentication for remote access
Annual review of the privacy notice
questions.exp: The confidentiality criteria (C1.2) address disposing of confidential information to meet objectives, which requires identifying it and destroying it securely. Backups extend retention, which works against timely disposal.

questions.q: An educational gaming website directed to children collects names and email addresses from users under 13 in the United States. Which law most directly requires the site to obtain verifiable parental consent?
choices: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act
HIPAA
The Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)
The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
questions.exp: COPPA requires operators of websites directed to children under 13 to obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting their personal information. GLBA governs financial institutions, not children's websites.

questions.q: A company subject to multiple privacy laws cannot answer regulators' questions about what personal data it holds, where it is stored, and with whom it is shared. Which step should be the foundation of its privacy program?
choices: Purchasing cyber insurance
Publishing a longer privacy notice
Creating a data inventory and data flow map that identifies personal data, its sources, locations, uses, and recipients
Encrypting all email
questions.exp: A data inventory or record of processing (required under GDPR Article 30) underpins compliance with access, deletion, notice, and security obligations. A privacy notice cannot be accurate unless the company knows what it collects and how it uses it.

questions.q: A retailer's privacy notice states that it never shares customer data with third parties, but the retailer actually provides customer lists to an analytics firm. Which U.S. regulator most commonly brings enforcement actions for such misrepresentations?
choices: The Securities and Exchange Commission, as a financial reporting violation
The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
The Internal Revenue Service
The Federal Trade Commission, under its authority over unfair or deceptive practices
questions.exp: Section 5 of the FTC Act prohibits deceptive practices, and failing to honor privacy promises is a common basis for FTC enforcement. The PCAOB oversees auditors of public companies, not company privacy practices.

questions.q: A California consumer submits a verifiable request to know the personal information a business subject to the CCPA has collected about her. Absent an extension, within how many days must the business respond?
choices: 10 days
90 days
45 days
30 days
questions.exp: The CCPA requires a response to requests to know, delete, or correct within 45 calendar days, extendable once by an additional 45 days with notice. Ten business days is the deadline to confirm receipt of the request, not to respond.

questions.q: Under the CPRA amendments to the CCPA, which right allows a consumer to direct a business to restrict its use of information such as precise geolocation, Social Security number, and racial or ethnic origin?
choices: The right to know
The right to limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal information
The right to correct
The right to data portability
questions.exp: The CPRA created a category of sensitive personal information and a right to limit its use to purposes necessary to provide the requested goods or services. The right to correct addresses inaccurate data, not restrictions on use.

questions.q: A company is designing access controls for its HR system, which contains salary, performance, and medical leave information. Which approach best protects employee data confidentiality?
choices: Relying on employees' agreement to keep information confidential
Allowing managers to view all employees' records company-wide
Giving all HR staff full access for efficiency
Role-based access granting each user only the data needed for the job, with periodic access reviews
questions.exp: Least-privilege, role-based access with periodic reviews limits exposure of sensitive personal data. Broad access for convenience increases the risk of inappropriate disclosure, and agreements alone are not a preventive control.

questions.q: An EU data subject asks a company to provide her personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format so she can move it to a competitor. Which GDPR right is she exercising?
choices: The right to data portability
The right to restriction of processing
The right to rectification
The right to object
questions.exp: Article 20 gives individuals the right to receive data they provided in a machine-readable format and transmit it to another controller where processing is based on consent or contract and carried out by automated means. Rectification concerns correcting inaccurate data.

questions.q: A global retailer applies the same data retention period of 'indefinitely' to all customer records because storage is inexpensive. Which privacy principle does this practice most clearly violate?
choices: Lawfulness
Accuracy
Storage limitation
Transparency
questions.exp: Storage limitation requires keeping personal data no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was processed. Low storage cost does not justify indefinite retention, which also increases breach exposure.

questions.q: A bank employee receives a call from someone posing as a customer who provides the customer's name and address and asks for the account balance. Which GLBA provision most directly addresses this attempt?
choices: The Privacy Rule's annual notice requirement
The opt-out right for affiliate sharing
The pretexting provisions prohibiting obtaining customer information under false pretenses
The Safeguards Rule's encryption requirement
questions.exp: GLBA's pretexting provisions make it unlawful to obtain customer information through false pretenses, and institutions should train staff and verify identity to prevent it. Annual privacy notices do not address impersonation attempts.

questions.q: A company conducts business in the EU, California, and several other U.S. states with differing privacy laws. Which approach to compliance is generally most efficient?
choices: Creating entirely separate, independent programs for each jurisdiction
Ignoring the smaller jurisdictions
Following only the law of the state where the company is headquartered
Building a privacy program around common principles and controls, then mapping and adding jurisdiction-specific requirements
questions.exp: Most privacy laws share core principles such as notice, choice, access, minimization, and security, so a common control framework with jurisdiction-specific overlays avoids duplicated effort. Following only the headquarters state ignores laws that apply based on where individuals reside.

questions.q: An EU-based controller uses automated software to reject loan applications without any human review. Under GDPR Article 22, what right do applicants generally have?
choices: The right to have their data transferred to the United States
The right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing that produces legal or similarly significant effects, subject to exceptions with safeguards such as human intervention
The right to a refund of application fees
The right to receive the source code of the algorithm
questions.exp: Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with significant effects, and where they are permitted, individuals have rights to human intervention, to express their view, and to contest the decision. GDPR does not require disclosure of source code.

questions.q: A company's employees routinely print confidential customer reports and leave them on shared printers. Which control would most directly reduce this risk?
choices: Annual penetration testing
Encrypting the database that generates the reports
Increasing the frequency of backups
Secure print release requiring user authentication at the printer, combined with a clean-desk policy
questions.exp: Secure print release ensures documents print only when the authorized user is present, and a clean-desk policy addresses physical exposure. Database encryption protects stored data but not printed output.

questions.q: An employee in Germany submits a subject access request asking her employer what personal data it holds about her. Under GDPR, absent an extension for complex or numerous requests, how quickly must the employer respond, and may it charge a fee?
choices: Within 72 hours, free of charge
Within 60 days, with a fee based on the number of pages
Within 45 days, with a standard processing fee
Within one month, generally free of charge unless the request is manifestly unfounded or excessive
questions.exp: Article 12 requires responding to data subject requests within one month, extendable by two further months where necessary, and the first copy is generally free. The 45-day period is the CCPA's response deadline, not GDPR's.

questions.q: A user auditor plans to reduce assessed control risk for revenue transactions processed by a third-party billing service. The service organization provides only a SOC 1 Type 1 report. What is the main limitation of relying on this report?
choices: It does not address whether the service organization's description is fairly presented
It covers only the security category of the trust services criteria
It is restricted to management of the service organization and cannot be given to user auditors
It provides no evidence that controls operated effectively over a period
questions.exp: A Type 1 report addresses the fair presentation of the description and the suitability of design as of a date, so it gives no evidence about operating effectiveness needed to support a lower control risk assessment (AU-C 402). It does address fair presentation of the description, and user auditors are intended users of SOC 1 reports.

questions.q: A payroll service organization uses a separate data center company to host its servers. The service organization's description excludes the data center's controls but includes the service organization's own controls for monitoring the data center. Which method is being used?
choices: Carve-out method
Integrated method
Inclusive method
Bridge method
questions.exp: Under the carve-out method the subservice organization's controls are excluded from the description and scope, though the service organization's monitoring controls over the subservice organization are included. The inclusive method would bring the data center's relevant controls into the description and testing.

questions.q: A service organization's SOC 1 report states that user entities are expected to review exception reports and restrict access to their own terminals for the stated control objectives to be achieved. How should a user auditor respond to these statements?
choices: Treat them as complementary subservice organization controls
Ignore them, because the service auditor's opinion already covers them
Evaluate whether the user entity has designed and implemented these complementary user entity controls
Request that the service auditor test them at each user entity
questions.exp: Complementary user entity controls are assumed in the design of the service organization's controls, so the user auditor must determine whether the user entity has them in place (AU-C 402). The service auditor's opinion is explicitly conditioned on these controls; it does not test them.

questions.q: Under SSAE 18, when a service organization uses the carve-out method, its description must also identify:
choices: Controls the service organization assumes are implemented by the subservice organization that are necessary to achieve the control objectives
The results of the subservice auditor's tests of controls
The fees charged by the subservice organization
The subservice organization's financial statements
questions.exp: SSAE 18 requires disclosure of complementary subservice organization controls (CSOCs) when the carve-out method is used. Test results of the subservice organization's auditor are not included under carve-out; that is a feature of how the inclusive method brings controls into scope.

questions.q: Management of a service organization refuses to provide a written assertion for a SOC 1 Type 2 engagement. Under AT-C 320, the service auditor should:
choices: Issue an unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph
Prepare the assertion on management's behalf
Withdraw from the engagement when withdrawal is possible under applicable law or regulation
Issue a qualified opinion on operating effectiveness only
questions.exp: A written assertion from management is a precondition for a SOC 1 engagement, and if management refuses to provide it, AT-C 320 requires withdrawal when possible (or a disclaimer if withdrawal is not permitted). The service auditor cannot write management's assertion, because doing so would impair independence.

questions.q: A calendar-year user entity receives a SOC 1 Type 2 report covering October 1 through September 30. To address the October-December gap, the user entity obtains a letter stating there have been no significant changes in controls. Who issues this bridge letter?
choices: Management of the user entity
Management of the service organization
The service auditor
The user auditor
questions.exp: A bridge (gap) letter is a representation by service organization management and is not an attestation by the service auditor. The user auditor considers it with other evidence, but it carries less assurance than a service auditor's report.

questions.q: A cloud-hosting customer wants assurance about a provider's controls relevant to security and availability, not financial reporting, and the report will be shared only with customers under NDA. Which report best meets this need?
choices: SOC for Cybersecurity
SOC 1 Type 2
SOC 3
SOC 2 Type 2
questions.exp: A SOC 2 Type 2 report addresses controls relevant to the trust services categories (e.g., security and availability) with detailed tests and results, and is intended for knowledgeable users. A SOC 3 covers the same criteria but is a general-use report without the detailed description and test results.

questions.q: A service organization wants to post its assurance report publicly on its website for marketing purposes. Which report is designed for general use?
choices: SOC 3
SOC 1 Type 2
SOC 2 Type 2
SOC 1 Type 1
questions.exp: SOC 3 reports are general-use reports based on the trust services criteria. SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports are restricted to specified users who understand the system and the related user entity controls.

questions.q: In a SOC 1 Type 2 report, which section contains information that the service auditor reads for material inconsistencies but does not express an opinion on?
choices: The description of the system
The description of tests of controls and results
Other information provided by the service organization, such as management's responses to deviations
Management's written assertion
questions.exp: Other information provided by the service organization is not covered by the service auditor's opinion; the service auditor reads it only to identify material inconsistencies. The system description is directly covered by the opinion on fair presentation.

questions.q: A service auditor uses the work of the service organization's internal audit function to perform some tests of controls in a SOC 1 Type 2 engagement. Which statement is correct?
choices: The opinion should state that responsibility is divided with internal audit
The description of tests of controls should describe the internal auditors' work and the service auditor's procedures with respect to that work
Internal audit's work cannot be used in a SOC 1 engagement
Internal audit must issue its own separate report attached to the SOC 1 report
questions.exp: AT-C 320 permits use of internal audit's work, and when it is used in tests of controls the description of tests in a Type 2 report must describe that work and the service auditor's related procedures. The service auditor retains sole responsibility and does not divide it in the opinion.

questions.q: In a SOC 1 Type 2 engagement, the service auditor finds that the control objective related to authorized changes to application programs was not achieved during the period because key controls were not operating effectively. The service auditor would most likely issue:
choices: An unmodified opinion with deviations listed in the tests section
A qualified opinion on operating effectiveness
A disclaimer of opinion on the entire report
An adverse opinion on the fairness of the description
questions.exp: When deviations cause a control objective not to be achieved, the service auditor modifies the opinion on operating effectiveness, usually as a qualification. The description can still be fairly presented, so an adverse opinion on the description is not indicated.

questions.q: A service auditor discovers that the system description lists a daily reconciliation control that the service organization never actually implemented. Which part of the opinion is most directly affected?
choices: The opinion on the fair presentation of the description
None, because the service auditor simply omits the control from testing
Only the section of other information
The restricted-use paragraph
questions.exp: A description that includes controls that were not implemented is not fairly presented, so the opinion on the description must be modified. Simply dropping the control from testing would leave a misleading description, and other information is not covered by the opinion.

questions.q: Under the inclusive method, which of the following is required?
choices: The subservice organization's controls are excluded, but CSOCs are listed
Only the service organization's monitoring controls over the subservice organization are tested
A separate SOC 3 report from the subservice organization
A written assertion from management of the subservice organization covering the subservice organization's controls included in the description
questions.exp: Under the inclusive method, the subservice organization's relevant controls are included in the description and tested, so the subservice organization's management must also provide a written assertion. Excluding the controls and listing CSOCs describes the carve-out method.

questions.q: Which of the following is the responsibility of service organization management, not the service auditor, in a SOC 1 engagement?
choices: Evaluating whether deviations are significant to the opinion
Expressing an opinion on operating effectiveness
Specifying the control objectives and preparing the description of the system
Determining the nature, timing and extent of tests of controls
questions.exp: In SOC 1 engagements, service organization management specifies the control objectives, prepares the description and provides the assertion. Designing tests and forming the opinion are the service auditor's responsibilities.

questions.q: A user auditor relying on a SOC 1 Type 2 report notes that the service auditor reported deviations in testing of user access removal. What should the user auditor do?
choices: Report the deviations to the PCAOB
Require the service organization to issue a new report
Disregard the deviations because the opinion was unmodified
Consider the nature and cause of the deviations and their effect on the user auditor's risk assessment and further procedures
questions.exp: AU-C 402 requires the user auditor to evaluate deviations, even when the service auditor's opinion is unmodified, and determine their effect on the planned audit approach. An unmodified opinion does not mean the deviations are irrelevant to a particular user entity's assertions.

questions.q: A user auditor issues an unmodified opinion on a client's financial statements after relying on a SOC 1 Type 2 report. How should the user auditor refer to the service auditor in the audit report?
choices: Not refer to the service auditor's work
Refer to the service auditor to indicate shared responsibility
Name the service auditor in an other-matter paragraph
Attach the service auditor's report to the financial statements
questions.exp: AU-C 402 prohibits referring to the service auditor's work in an unmodified opinion on the user entity's financial statements. Unlike a group audit with a component auditor, there is no division of responsibility.

questions.q: With respect to independence, a service auditor performing a SOC 2 examination must be independent of:
choices: Every subservice organization carved out of the description
The service organization
Every user entity that will receive the report
The user auditors who will read the report
questions.exp: Under AT-C 105/205, the practitioner must be independent of the responsible party, which is the service organization. Independence from each of potentially hundreds of user entities is not required.

questions.q: Which criteria are used to evaluate the description of a service organization's system in a SOC 2 examination?
choices: NIST SP 800-53 baselines
Control objectives specified by service organization management
Description criteria in DC 200
COSO 2013 principles
questions.exp: The SOC 2 description is evaluated against the AICPA description criteria (DC section 200), and controls are evaluated against the trust services criteria. Management-specified control objectives are the hallmark of SOC 1, not SOC 2.

questions.q: A hospital system requires a vendor to report on controls relevant to security and also on its compliance with HIPAA security requirements in one examination. Which report best fits?
choices: A SOC 3 report
A SOC 2+ report that addresses additional subject matter and criteria
An agreed-upon procedures report on the financial statements
A SOC 1 Type 2 report
questions.exp: SOC 2 examinations can be expanded (often called SOC 2+) to cover additional subject matter such as HIPAA requirements alongside the trust services criteria. SOC 1 addresses controls relevant to user entities' financial reporting, not security or HIPAA compliance.

questions.q: A SOC 1 Type 2 report covers January 1 through June 30. A service organization implemented a new automated control on April 1 that replaced a manual control. How should this be handled?
choices: Test only the new control and describe it as operating for the entire period
Omit both controls from the report
Disclose the change in the description and test each control for the portion of the period it operated
Test only the manual control, because it existed at the start of the period
questions.exp: Significant changes to controls during the period must be included in the description, and a Type 2 report should cover each relevant control for the part of the period it was in operation. Presenting the new control as operating all period would misstate the description.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports?
choices: SOC 1 is always a Type 2; SOC 2 is always a Type 1
SOC 1 is performed under AT-C 205 only; SOC 2 under AU-C 402

SOC 1 addresses controls relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting; SOC 2 addresses controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, or privacy
SOC 1 is for general use; SOC 2 is restricted
questions.exp: SOC 1 (AT-C 320) focuses on ICFR-relevant controls, and SOC 2 (AT-C 205) uses the trust services criteria. Both have Type 1 and Type 2 versions and both are restricted-use; AU-C 402 governs the user auditor, not the service auditor.

questions.q: During a SOC 2 examination, the service auditor learns that a service organization employee intentionally altered system logs to hide a security incident affecting several user entities. What should the service auditor do?
choices: Report the matter only in a separate management letter that is not part of the engagement
Ignore the matter because it relates to an individual employee
Immediately notify all user entities directly without informing management
Evaluate the effect on the description, the controls and the opinion, and consider communicating with appropriate parties
questions.exp: The practitioner must consider known or suspected fraud, noncompliance and incidents and evaluate their effect on the subject matter and the report, including whether the description must disclose the incident. Bypassing management to notify users directly is not the required first response.

questions.q: A user auditor obtained a SOC 1 Type 2 report covering January 1 through June 30 for a client with a December 31 year end. Which additional procedure is most appropriate?
choices: Obtain information about changes in controls during the remaining period, such as a bridge letter, and consider additional testing
Conclude that the report is irrelevant and test everything at the service organization
Ask the service auditor to extend its opinion verbally to December 31
Rely fully on the report for the entire year without additional procedures
questions.exp: AU-C 402 requires the user auditor to consider the period not covered and obtain additional evidence, for example through bridge letters, inquiry, or additional tests. A report covering half the year cannot by itself support reliance on controls for the full period.

questions.q: Which element is included in a SOC 1 Type 2 report but NOT in a SOC 1 Type 1 report?
choices: Opinion on suitability of design
Description of the service organization's system
Management's written assertion
Description of the service auditor's tests of controls and results
questions.exp: Only a Type 2 report includes the service auditor's description of tests of controls and their results, because it opines on operating effectiveness over a period. The assertion, description and opinion on design appear in both types.

questions.q: A SOC 2 Type 2 report on a software company lists 'logical access to the production database is restricted to authorized personnel' and indicates that 3 of 40 sampled terminated users retained access for over 30 days. A prospective customer reading the report should primarily:
choices: Assess whether the exception is significant to its own use of the service and whether compensating controls exist
Assume the service auditor's opinion must be adverse
Disregard it, because SOC 2 tests are not relevant to customers
Require the service auditor to retest using a larger sample
questions.exp: Report users evaluate reported exceptions in the context of their own risks and any compensating controls at their organization or the provider. Exceptions do not automatically make an opinion adverse; the service auditor judges whether criteria were still met.

questions.q: SSAE 18 requires the service auditor in a SOC 1 engagement to obtain an understanding of the service organization's controls and to evaluate the reliability of information produced by the entity (IPE) used in testing. Which procedure best addresses the reliability of a system-generated list of terminated employees used to select a sample?
choices: Ask management whether the list is complete
Accept the list because it is system generated
Test the accuracy and completeness of the list, for example by testing its source and the report logic
Reperform the termination process for every name on the list
questions.exp: Service auditors must evaluate whether information produced by the entity is sufficiently reliable, including its accuracy and completeness, before using it. Inquiry alone or assuming system output is reliable does not meet this requirement.

questions.q: When a SOC 1 Type 2 report is distributed, which parties are the intended users?
choices: Any member of the public, including potential investors
Management of the service organization, user entities during the period, and their auditors
Only the service auditor and the PCAOB
Only the board of directors of the service organization
questions.exp: SOC 1 reports are restricted to service organization management, user entities of the system during the report period, and user auditors. They are not intended for the general public, unlike SOC 3 reports.

questions.q: In a SOC 2 examination, which party selects the trust services categories (e.g., security, availability, confidentiality) to include?
choices: Service organization management, typically considering user needs and commitments
Each user entity independently
The AICPA, which mandates all five categories
The service auditor alone
questions.exp: Service organization management selects the categories, though security (the common criteria) is always included. The AICPA does not mandate all five categories, and the service auditor does not choose the subject matter.

questions.q: A user auditor is evaluating a service auditor's SOC 1 report. Under AU-C 402, which of the following should the user auditor be satisfied about?
choices: That the service auditor is also the subservice organization's auditor
That the service auditor audited the user entity's financial statements
The service auditor's professional competence and independence from the service organization
That the service auditor's fees are reasonable
questions.exp: AU-C 402 requires the user auditor to be satisfied as to the service auditor's professional competence and independence and the adequacy of the standards used. There is no requirement that the service auditor also audit the user entity or the subservice organization.

questions.q: Which situation would generally make a SOC 1 report the least relevant choice?
choices: A user entity outsources claims processing that feeds its revenue and expense records
A company wants assurance about a vendor's data center security controls protecting customer personal data unrelated to financial reporting
A user entity outsources payroll and needs assurance for its year-end audit
A bank outsources loan servicing that updates its general ledger
questions.exp: SOC 1 reports address controls relevant to user entities' ICFR, so a security and privacy concern unrelated to financial reporting is better served by SOC 2. Payroll, claims processing and loan servicing all flow into financial statements.

questions.q: A service auditor's SOC 2 Type 2 report is dated September 15 for a period ending June 30. Between July 1 and September 15, a significant breach affecting the system occurred. What should the service auditor consider?
choices: Whether the event is a subsequent event that should be disclosed in the description, and whether the report should be modified if it is not disclosed
Extending the examination period automatically to September 15
Nothing, because events after the period end are always outside the scope
Withdrawing the report from all users already in possession of it
questions.exp: The practitioner inquires about events up to the report date that could affect the subject matter or assertion, and an undisclosed significant subsequent event may require disclosure or report modification. Subsequent events are not simply ignored because they occurred after period end.

questions.q: A service organization's description states that it uses a subservice organization for check printing, but the SOC 1 report uses the carve-out method. A user auditor needs assurance about the check printing controls. What should the user auditor do?
choices: Obtain a SOC 1 report from the subservice organization or perform other procedures over its relevant controls
Ignore check printing because it is immaterial by definition
Rely on the service organization's report because carve-out includes subservice controls
Ask the service auditor to issue a separate opinion on the subservice organization's controls
questions.exp: Under carve-out, the subservice organization's controls are excluded from the report, so the user auditor needs separate evidence, such as the subservice organization's own SOC 1 report. Carve-out explicitly does not cover subservice organization controls.

questions.q: Which statement about the opinion in a SOC 1 Type 2 report is correct?
choices: It covers whether the service organization complied with laws and regulations
It covers fair presentation of the description, suitability of design, and operating effectiveness throughout the specified period
It covers only operating effectiveness as of the report date
It covers fair presentation of the user entity's financial statements
questions.exp: A Type 2 opinion addresses the description, design and operating effectiveness throughout the period. Operating effectiveness 'as of a date' is not meaningful; that point-in-time concept applies only to a Type 1's design and implementation.

questions.q: A service organization undergoing its first SOC examination has had its controls in operation for only two weeks. A customer wants a SOC report quickly. Which option is most practical?
choices: A SOC 3 report, which requires no testing
A bridge letter issued by the service auditor
A Type 2 report covering two weeks, which provides the same assurance as a 12-month report
A Type 1 report on design and implementation as of a specified date, followed later by a Type 2 report
questions.exp: A Type 1 report is often used as a first step when controls have not operated long enough for meaningful operating-effectiveness testing. A very short Type 2 period gives limited evidence, and bridge letters come from management, not the service auditor.

questions.q: In a SOC 1 engagement, management's description identifies control objectives that do not address a significant risk relevant to user entities' financial reporting, such as the completeness of transaction processing. What is the most likely consequence?
choices: The service auditor may conclude the description is not fairly presented or the control objectives are not reasonable, and modify the report
There is no consequence because management may specify any objectives it wants
The service auditor adds the missing control objective without telling management
The user auditor must issue an adverse opinion on the user entity's financial statements
questions.exp: Control objectives must be reasonable in the circumstances; omitting objectives relevant to user entities' ICFR can make the description misleading and lead to a modified opinion. The service auditor cannot unilaterally add objectives, because the description is management's responsibility.

questions.q: A service auditor performing a SOC 2 Type 2 examination identifies that management's description omits a significant system incident that occurred during the period and caused the entity's service commitments to not be met. Under the description criteria, this incident should be:
choices: Disclosed in the description, and its omission would affect the opinion on fair presentation
Disclosed only in the service auditor's management letter
Omitted, because SOC 2 descriptions address only controls, not incidents
Reported only to the AICPA
questions.exp: DC 200 requires disclosure of system incidents that resulted in a significant failure to achieve service commitments and system requirements, including the nature, timing and extent. Omitting a required disclosure means the description is not fairly presented.

questions.q: Before accepting a SOC 2 engagement, a practitioner should determine whether the criteria are suitable and available to intended users. Which statement best reflects how the trust services criteria satisfy this?
choices: They are suitable only if the service organization modifies them for each customer
They must be approved by each user entity before use
They are available only to the service auditor
They are suitable because they were developed by an AICPA body following due process, and are publicly available
questions.exp: The 2017 trust services criteria were issued by the AICPA Assurance Services Executive Committee following due process and are publicly available, so they are suitable criteria under AT-C 105. They are not customized per customer or approved by each user.

questions.q: A publicly traded manufacturer (not a service organization) wants a CPA's examination report on its entity-wide cybersecurity risk management program that can be shared with investors and other general users. Which engagement best fits?
choices: SOC for Cybersecurity examination
SOC 2 Type 2 examination
SOC 3 examination
SOC 1 Type 2 examination
questions.exp: A SOC for Cybersecurity examination reports on an entity's cybersecurity risk management program and controls and is intended for general use. SOC 2 and SOC 3 address a service organization's system used to provide services to user entities, not an entity-wide program.

questions.q: A cloud provider commits to 99.9% availability for a service that operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. What is the maximum downtime per year permitted under this commitment?
choices: 52.6 minutes
3.65 days
87.6 hours
8.76 hours
questions.exp: Annual hours are 24 x 365 = 8,760, and 0.1% of 8,760 is 8.76 hours. The 52.6-minute figure corresponds to 99.99% availability.

questions.q: A payment platform's SLA guarantees 99.95% availability measured over a 30-day month of continuous operation. What is the maximum allowable downtime in the month?
choices: 43.2 minutes
3.6 minutes
21.6 minutes
6 hours
questions.exp: A 30-day month has 720 hours; 0.05% x 720 = 0.36 hours, or 21.6 minutes. The 43.2-minute figure corresponds to 99.9% availability over the same month.

questions.q: A server has a mean time between failures (MTBF) of 990 hours and a mean time to repair (MTTR) of 10 hours. What is its expected availability?
questions.exp: Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR) = 990 / 1,000 = 99.0%. Dividing MTTR by MTBF (10/990) and subtracting from 100% gives the slightly different 98.99% trap.

questions.q: An order-processing service requires a web server (99.0% available), an application server (99.5% available), and a database server (99.8% available), all of which must be running for the service to work. Assuming independent failures, what is the approximate availability of the service?
questions.exp: Components in series multiply: 0.990 x 0.995 x 0.998 = about 0.983, or 98.3%. The service is less available than its weakest component, so 99.0% overstates it.

questions.q: A company replaces a single application server that is 95% available with two identical servers running in parallel behind a load balancer, so the service is available if either server is running. Assuming independent failures and a perfectly reliable load balancer, what is the service's availability?
questions.exp: Both servers must fail for an outage: probability 0.05 x 0.05 = 0.0025, so availability is 1 - 0.0025 = 99.75%. Multiplying 0.95 x 0.95 = 90.25% is the formula for components in series, not parallel.

questions.q: An SLA promises 99.9% monthly availability for a $50,000 monthly fee, with a 10% service credit if availability falls below 99.9% but stays at or above 99.0%, and a 25% credit below 99.0%. In a 30-day month, the service was down for 2 hours. What credit is the customer owed?
questions.exp: Availability = (720 - 2) / 720 = 99.72%, which is below 99.9% but above 99.0%, earning a 10% credit of $5,000. Assuming 2 hours falls below 99.0% would require more than 7.2 hours of downtime.

questions.q: Under the Trust Services Criteria, which control most directly supports the availability criterion addressing the maintenance and monitoring of processing capacity to meet the entity's commitments (A1.1)?
choices: A code of conduct signed annually by employees
Monitoring CPU, memory, storage, and network utilization against thresholds, with capacity forecasts reviewed by management
Encryption of data in transit
Quarterly user access reviews
questions.exp: A1.1 addresses managing current capacity and forecasting future demand so the system can meet availability commitments. Access reviews and encryption support security and confidentiality rather than capacity.

questions.q: A retailer's website crashed on Black Friday when traffic tripled, though no attack occurred. Which control would most likely have prevented the outage?
choices: Stronger password requirements
Data loss prevention software
Capacity planning with load testing and auto-scaling based on forecast peak demand
A larger cyber insurance policy
questions.exp: Forecasting peak demand, load testing, and elastic scaling ensure systems can handle predictable spikes. Insurance might compensate for losses but does not keep the site running.

questions.q: A company's online banking portal is flooded with traffic from thousands of compromised devices, making it unavailable to customers. Which control most directly mitigates this type of attack?
choices: Multifactor authentication for customers
Full-disk encryption on servers
Daily vulnerability scans
A DDoS mitigation service that filters malicious traffic upstream, such as through a scrubbing center or content delivery network
questions.exp: Distributed denial-of-service attacks overwhelm capacity, so they are best mitigated by upstream filtering and absorbing traffic at scale. MFA protects accounts but does nothing to stop volumetric traffic.

questions.q: A review of a company's network architecture finds that all internet traffic passes through a single firewall with no failover. Which availability concept is most directly at issue?
choices: Data minimization
Defense in depth
A single point of failure
Least privilege
questions.exp: A component whose failure stops the entire service is a single point of failure, addressed through redundancy such as clustered firewalls. Defense in depth concerns layering security controls rather than eliminating unique dependencies.

questions.q: Which Trust Services Criterion within the availability category is most directly supported by periodic testing of recovery plan procedures, including restoring backups at an alternate site?
choices: C1.1 identifying confidential information
A1.3 testing recovery plan procedures
PI1.2 input controls
CC6.1 logical access security
questions.exp: A1.3 requires the entity to test recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives. CC6.1 addresses logical access, a common criterion for security.

questions.q: A company's SOC 2 report covers processing integrity for its claims processing system. Which statement best describes processing integrity under the Trust Services Criteria?
choices: Personal information is collected and used in accordance with the privacy notice
Information designated as confidential is protected
The system is protected against unauthorized access
System processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized to meet the entity's objectives
questions.exp: Processing integrity addresses whether processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized. Protection against unauthorized access is the security category, which is the common criteria baseline for every SOC 2.

questions.q: A data entry clerk keys a customer number with two digits transposed. The system rejects it because the last digit, calculated from the other digits by an algorithm, no longer matches. Which input control is this?
choices: Completeness check
Limit check
Check digit verification
Sequence check
questions.exp: A check digit is derived mathematically from the other digits, so transpositions and most single-digit errors produce a mismatch. A limit check tests whether a value exceeds a predefined amount, not whether an identifier is valid.

questions.q: A payroll system rejects any time card reporting more than 80 hours for a single week. Which input control is being applied?
choices: Limit check
Validity check
Hash total
Field (format) check
questions.exp: A limit check compares a value against a predetermined upper or lower bound. A field check tests that data is of the correct type, such as numeric characters only.

questions.q: An accounts payable system compares the vendor number on each invoice against the vendor master file and rejects invoices from vendors not on the file. Which control is this?
choices: Range check
Reasonableness check
Validity check
Sequence check
questions.exp: A validity check compares entered data against a list of valid values, such as authorized vendors in the master file. A reasonableness check tests whether a value is logical in relation to other data.

questions.q: A payroll clerk adds the employee identification numbers on a batch of time cards and compares the sum with the total computed by the system after input. The sum has no meaning other than as a control. What is this total called?
choices: Financial total
Run-to-run total
Hash total
Record count
questions.exp: A hash total sums a field that has no arithmetic meaning, such as employee numbers, and detects lost, added, or altered records. A financial total sums a meaningful amount field like gross pay.

questions.q: A batch of vendor invoices has a control sheet showing 250 documents totaling $125,400. After processing, the system reports 249 documents totaling $124,900. What do these batch controls most likely indicate?
choices: One invoice of $500 was not processed and should be investigated
The batch was processed correctly
The vendor master file contains an invalid vendor
One invoice was processed twice
questions.exp: The record count is short by one (250 - 249) and the financial total is short by $500 ($125,400 - $124,900), suggesting one $500 invoice was lost or rejected. A duplicate would increase, not decrease, the totals.

questions.q: A billing system rejects 3% of transactions for data errors and places them in a suspense file. Which additional control is most important to ensure processing integrity?
choices: Monitoring the suspense file so rejected items are investigated, corrected, and resubmitted on a timely basis
Deleting rejected transactions at month-end
Reporting rejected transactions to the external auditor only
Allowing any user to edit the suspense file
questions.exp: Error handling must ensure rejected items are tracked to resolution; otherwise valid transactions may never be recorded, impairing completeness. Deleting suspense items guarantees that legitimate revenue is lost.

questions.q: Each nightly job in a multistep inventory processing run compares the record count and total quantity at the start of the step with those of the prior step's output. What type of control is this?
choices: Preventive access control
Input control
Run-to-run (processing) control
Output distribution control
questions.exp: Run-to-run totals verify that data is not lost or altered between processing steps, which is a processing control. Input controls validate data as it enters the system.

questions.q: Two clerks simultaneously update the same customer's credit limit, and one update overwrites the other without warning. Which control would prevent this problem?
choices: Batch control totals
Record locking or concurrency controls in the database
Daily backups
A limit check on the credit field
questions.exp: Concurrency controls such as record locking prevent simultaneous updates from overwriting each other, preserving data integrity. A limit check validates the value but not the conflict between updates.

questions.q: A sales order entry screen will not save an order until the customer number, product code, quantity, and ship-to address fields are all filled in. Which control is this?
choices: Check digit
Completeness check
Sequence check
Reasonableness check
questions.exp: A completeness check ensures that all required fields contain data before a record is accepted. A sequence check verifies that items are in the expected order or that numbered documents have no gaps.

questions.q: A company prints checks using prenumbered forms. At the end of each run, a clerk accounts for all check numbers, including voided ones, and investigates any gaps. Which control does this represent?
choices: Field check
Validity check
Sequence check on prenumbered documents
Limit check
questions.exp: Accounting for the numeric sequence of prenumbered documents detects missing, duplicate, or unauthorized items. A validity check compares values against a list of authorized entries.

questions.q: Payroll registers containing employee salaries are automatically emailed to all department managers, including those who supervise none of the listed employees. Which processing integrity and confidentiality weakness is present?
choices: Run-to-run totals are missing
The suspense file is not monitored
Output is distributed beyond authorized recipients
Input validation is insufficient
