questions.exp: Output controls should ensure reports reach only authorized users who need them. Input validation and run-to-run totals address data accuracy rather than who receives the output.

questions.q: A company's ERP system interfaces nightly with its bank to send payment files. Which control best ensures the files sent were completely and accurately received and processed?
choices: Reconciling the record counts and totals in the transmitted file with the bank's acknowledgment and the subsequent bank activity
Changing the bank portal password monthly
Printing the payment file for filing
Encrypting the payment file
questions.exp: Reconciling control totals and acknowledgments confirms completeness and accuracy of the interface. Encryption protects confidentiality and integrity in transit but does not confirm the bank processed every payment.

questions.q: A distribution company wants to ensure that its customer-facing order system defines what constitutes a valid order and how orders are processed, consistent with processing integrity criterion PI1.1. Which practice addresses this criterion?
choices: Documenting and communicating the system's data definitions and processing specifications, such as required fields, valid values, and processing rules
Encrypting stored order data
Performing annual penetration tests
Requiring background checks for data entry clerks
questions.exp: PI1.1 addresses obtaining or generating and communicating information about the objectives and specifications of processing, including data definitions. Encryption and penetration tests relate to security rather than processing specifications.

questions.q: A subscription billing system occasionally charges customers twice when a network timeout causes the payment request to be resubmitted. Which control would best address this?
choices: Reviewing the general ledger monthly
Assigning unique transaction identifiers and rejecting duplicate submissions with the same identifier
Adding a limit check on the payment amount
Increasing server memory
questions.exp: Duplicate detection using unique transaction IDs ensures each payment is processed only once even when requests are retried. A limit check would accept two charges that are each within the limit.

questions.q: A company's data center has redundant power feeds, generators, raised floors, and temperature and humidity monitoring. Which availability criterion do these controls most directly support?
choices: CC6.2, user registration
A1.2, environmental protections and recovery infrastructure
A1.1, capacity management
PI1.3, processing accuracy
questions.exp: A1.2 addresses environmental protections, software, data backup processes, and recovery infrastructure. CC6.2 concerns registering and authorizing users, which is a logical access control.

questions.q: A web application went down for six hours because a single expired disk license caused the storage array to stop accepting writes. Monitoring tools existed but alerts were sent to a mailbox no one reviewed. Which improvement would most directly reduce the risk of recurrence?
choices: Increasing the RPO
Encrypting the storage array
Purchasing a second monitoring tool
Routing monitoring alerts to an on-call team with defined escalation procedures and response time targets
questions.exp: Monitoring adds value only if alerts reach someone accountable for responding. A second tool sending alerts to the same unattended mailbox would not help.

questions.q: A sales system checks whether the quantity ordered by a retail customer is consistent with that customer's historical ordering pattern and flags orders that are ten times the norm. Which control is this?
choices: Check digit
Reasonableness check
Field check
Hash total
questions.exp: A reasonableness check evaluates whether data is logical relative to other information, such as historical patterns. A field check only tests data type or format.

questions.q: An insurer's claims system calculates benefits automatically. To verify processing accuracy as part of PI1.3, which control is most effective?
choices: Restricting physical access to the server room
Requiring claimants to use strong passwords
Periodic backup of the claims database
Testing benefit calculation logic before deployment and periodically comparing a sample of system calculations with independent recalculations
questions.exp: PI1.3 addresses processing that is complete, accurate, and timely; validating calculation logic and periodically recalculating samples tests accuracy directly. Physical security and backups support other criteria.

questions.q: An organization schedules maintenance windows for system patches on Sunday mornings and excludes them from the availability calculation in its customer SLA. What should a user entity understand about this arrangement?
choices: The SLA guarantees the system will be available every minute of the year
Maintenance windows are prohibited under the Trust Services Criteria
Scheduled maintenance always counts as unplanned downtime
The stated availability percentage may overstate the actual uptime experienced, so users should review SLA definitions and exclusions
questions.exp: SLAs often exclude scheduled maintenance from availability calculations, so the headline percentage may not reflect total time the system is usable. The TSC do not prohibit maintenance windows; they require meeting commitments as defined.

questions.q: A company wants its database to remain available if one server's power supply fails. Which hardware design best accomplishes this?
choices: A larger single power supply
Monthly hardware inspections
A UPS with five minutes of battery
Redundant, hot-swappable power supplies connected to separate power circuits
questions.exp: Redundant power supplies on separate circuits allow the server to keep running if one fails and to replace it without downtime. A larger single supply is still a single point of failure.

questions.q: Which statement best explains why processing integrity is distinct from data integrity in a SOC 2 examination?
choices: Processing integrity is a security criterion and is always included in SOC 2

Processing integrity addresses whether the system's processing meets its objectives completely, validly, accurately, timely, and with authorization, not whether the underlying data was accurate when supplied by external sources
Data integrity is a TSC category, while processing integrity is not
Processing integrity applies only to financial systems, while data integrity applies to all systems
questions.exp: The TSC note that processing integrity does not necessarily imply the data input from outside parties is correct; it focuses on the system processing that data as intended. Processing integrity is an optional category, not part of the security common criteria.

questions.q: A company's e-commerce application writes order data to a primary database and a reporting database. Reports occasionally show orders that never appear in the primary database. Which control would best detect this problem?
choices: Increasing server capacity
Encrypting the reporting database
Automated daily reconciliation of record counts and totals between the primary and reporting databases, with exceptions investigated
Requiring complex passwords for report users
questions.exp: Reconciliations between data stores detect inconsistencies such as phantom or missing records, supporting both processing and output integrity. Capacity and passwords do not address data consistency.

questions.q: A cloud SaaS provider experienced three outages in a quarter, lasting 2 hours, 1.5 hours, and 30 minutes, during a 90-day quarter of continuous service. What was its availability for the quarter, rounded to two decimals?
questions.exp: Total downtime is 2 + 1.5 + 0.5 = 4 hours out of 90 x 24 = 2,160 hours, so availability = 2,156 / 2,160 = 99.81%. Counting only the longest outage, or using a 30-day month as the base, produces the incorrect figures.

questions.q: An application occasionally posts transactions with a date in the following year because users mistype the year. Which input control would best prevent this?
choices: A hash total of transaction dates
A sequence check on invoice numbers
A range check limiting transaction dates to the current open accounting period
A check digit on the customer number
questions.exp: A range check enforces upper and lower bounds, such as dates within the open period. A hash total could detect changes in a batch, but would not prevent a keyed future date.

questions.q: A company's availability commitments state that customer data will be recoverable to within one hour of any failure. Which control most directly supports meeting this commitment?
choices: Weekly full backups
Continuous or at least hourly replication or backup of customer data, with monitoring of job success
Annual review of the backup policy
Restricting access to the backup room
questions.exp: A one-hour recovery point commitment requires capturing data at least hourly and confirming those jobs succeed. Weekly backups would allow up to a week of data loss.

questions.q: A company archives processed loan records to a data warehouse used for regulatory reporting. Which control most directly supports the processing integrity criterion that stored data be maintained completely and accurately over time (PI1.5)?
choices: Periodic integrity checks, such as comparing stored record counts and checksums with source totals, and restricting changes to archived records
Limiting the number of reports users can run each day
Encrypting loan records while they are transmitted to the warehouse
Requiring loan officers to complete privacy training
questions.exp: PI1.5 addresses storing inputs, items in processing, and outputs completely, accurately, and timely, which integrity checks and change restrictions on stored data support. Encryption in transit protects data on the way in but does not show that the stored data remains complete and unaltered.

questions.q: A company is replacing its general ledger system and wants to minimize the risk that the new system fails at go-live, even at the cost of extra effort. Which conversion approach best meets this goal?
choices: Pilot conversion at one location
Parallel conversion
Phased conversion by module
Direct (plunge) conversion
questions.exp: Parallel conversion runs old and new systems simultaneously so results can be compared and the old system remains available if the new one fails. Direct conversion is cheapest but riskiest because there is no fallback.

questions.q: A retailer implements a new point-of-sale system in three stores first, evaluates the results, and then rolls it out to its other 200 stores. This conversion approach is:
choices: Big-bang conversion
Direct conversion
Pilot conversion
Parallel conversion
questions.exp: A pilot conversion implements the full system at a limited location or group first to identify problems before broader rollout. Parallel conversion runs old and new systems side by side rather than limiting implementation to a subset.

questions.q: During which SDLC phase is it most cost-effective to incorporate security and control requirements?
choices: Requirements definition and design
Implementation
Operations and maintenance
Testing
questions.exp: Building controls in during requirements and design is far cheaper than retrofitting them after development or go-live. Waiting until testing often means discovering missing controls when changes are expensive.

questions.q: Before approving a new system project, management evaluates whether the expected benefits justify the costs. This is the:
choices: Economic feasibility analysis
Operational feasibility analysis
Schedule feasibility analysis
Technical feasibility analysis
questions.exp: Economic feasibility compares costs and benefits, often using NPV or payback. Technical feasibility asks whether the technology and expertise exist to build the system.

questions.q: A project team is concerned that employees will resist using a new system because it changes their workflows significantly. Which feasibility dimension does this concern relate to?
choices: Technical feasibility
Operational feasibility
Legal feasibility
Economic feasibility
questions.exp: Operational feasibility evaluates whether the system will be used and fit the organization's operations and people. Technical feasibility concerns the availability of technology, not user acceptance.

questions.q: Which development methodology delivers working software in short iterations, with requirements that evolve through collaboration between a product owner and the development team?
choices: Traditional structured analysis
Agile (e.g., Scrum)
Spiral with fixed requirements
Waterfall
questions.exp: Agile methods such as Scrum use short sprints, a prioritized backlog and frequent feedback, allowing requirements to evolve. Waterfall completes each phase sequentially with requirements largely fixed up front.

questions.q: A key control risk in agile development is that rapid iterations may lead to:
choices: Inability to change requirements
Too much upfront documentation
Insufficient documentation and inconsistent control over approvals, testing and security if not built into the definition of done
Excessive time between releases
questions.exp: Agile speed can erode documentation and control steps unless security, testing and approval are embedded in the process (e.g., definition of done). Excessive upfront documentation and rigid requirements are waterfall characteristics.

questions.q: A software development model emphasizes iterative risk analysis at each cycle, with prototypes built to resolve the highest risks before proceeding. This model is:
choices: Rapid application development
Spiral
Kanban
Waterfall
questions.exp: The spiral model cycles through planning, risk analysis, engineering and evaluation, focusing on risk reduction in each iteration. Waterfall proceeds linearly without repeated risk-driven cycles.

questions.q: Developers test each individual function of a new billing module in isolation to confirm it works as designed. This is:
choices: Integration testing
User acceptance testing
System testing
Unit testing
questions.exp: Unit testing verifies individual components in isolation. Integration testing verifies that components work together, such as the billing module's interface with the GL.

questions.q: After components of a new ERP are tested individually, the team tests whether data flow correctly between the procurement, inventory and accounts payable modules. This is:
choices: Regression testing
Integration testing
Stress testing
Unit testing
questions.exp: Integration testing verifies that separately developed components interact correctly. Regression testing checks that changes have not broken existing functions, which is a different purpose.

questions.q: Before go-live, business users execute real-world scenarios in a test environment and formally sign off that the system meets their requirements. This is:
choices: Unit testing
Load testing
Penetration testing
User acceptance testing
questions.exp: UAT is performed by business users to confirm that the system meets business requirements before acceptance. Penetration testing focuses on security vulnerabilities rather than business functionality.

questions.q: A bank's new online banking platform is tested by simulating 50,000 concurrent users to see whether performance degrades. This is:
choices: Code review
User acceptance testing
Unit testing
Stress (load) testing
questions.exp: Stress or load testing evaluates system behavior under high volumes or extreme conditions. UAT focuses on business requirements, not performance under load.

questions.q: A development team copies the full production customer database, including Social Security numbers, into the test environment for realistic testing. Which control is most appropriate?
choices: Restrict testing to developers only
Allow it, because testing needs real data
Delete the test environment after each sprint
Mask or de-identify sensitive data before use in non-production environments, or use synthetic data
questions.exp: Test environments typically have weaker controls, so sensitive production data should be masked, de-identified or replaced with synthetic data. Limiting who uses the environment does not remove the exposure of unmasked personal data.

questions.q: During development, the project sponsor keeps adding new features without adjusting the budget or timeline. This problem is known as:
choices: Gold plating by developers
Scope creep
Technical debt
Regression
questions.exp: Scope creep is uncontrolled expansion of project scope without corresponding changes to budget, time and resources. A formal change control process for requirements helps manage it.

questions.q: A company selects a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) ERP rather than building custom software. Which step is most important for reducing implementation risk?
choices: Defining requirements, evaluating vendors against them through an RFP process, and performing fit-gap analysis
Modifying the vendor's source code extensively to match current processes
Skipping requirements definition because the software is prebuilt
Avoiding vendor references to save time
questions.exp: Clear requirements, structured vendor evaluation and fit-gap analysis help select a package that fits and identify needed configuration or process changes. Extensive source code modification increases cost and complicates future upgrades.

questions.q: A company purchases critical software from a small vendor. To protect itself if the vendor goes out of business, it should obtain:
choices: A source code escrow agreement
A larger software license
A SOC 3 report
An extended warranty only
questions.exp: Source code escrow places code with a third party to be released to the customer under defined conditions, such as vendor bankruptcy. A warranty does not help if the vendor no longer exists to honor it.

questions.q: Which practice best reflects 'shifting security left' in a DevSecOps pipeline?
choices: Waiting for customers to report vulnerabilities
Running a penetration test only after the system is in production
Integrating automated static code analysis and dependency scanning into the build process
Performing an annual security audit
questions.exp: Shifting left embeds security testing early in development, such as static analysis and software composition analysis during builds. Production-only testing finds issues late, when they are costlier to fix.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes static application security testing (SAST) from dynamic application security testing (DAST)?
choices: DAST must be performed before any code is written
SAST tests a running application from the outside; DAST examines source code
SAST analyzes source code or binaries without executing them; DAST tests the running application by simulating attacks
Both test only network devices
questions.exp: SAST inspects code without execution and can run early; DAST probes a running application, often in test environments. Reversing the definitions is the common trap.

questions.q: NIST SP 800-218, the Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF), recommends practices organized into which groups?
choices: Govern, Map, Measure and Manage
Prepare the Organization, Protect the Software, Produce Well-Secured Software, and Respond to Vulnerabilities
Plan, Do, Check and Act
Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover
questions.exp: The SSDF organizes secure development practices into PO, PS, PW and RV groups. Identify-Protect-Detect-Respond-Recover are CSF functions, and Govern-Map-Measure-Manage come from the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

questions.q: A requirements traceability matrix is maintained throughout a project. Its primary purpose is to:
choices: List users' passwords
Ensure each requirement is designed, built and tested, and that no unapproved features are added
Record hardware serial numbers
Track developer hours for billing
questions.exp: Traceability links requirements to design elements and test cases, confirming coverage and helping control scope. It is not a time-tracking or asset-inventory tool.

questions.q: Before migrating data from a legacy system to a new ERP, which control best ensures the completeness and accuracy of the converted data?
choices: Relying on the vendor's migration tool without verification
Deleting legacy data before conversion to save space
Reconciling record counts and control totals between legacy and new systems and reviewing exception reports, with business owner sign-off
Converting data only after go-live
questions.exp: Reconciliations of counts and balances, review of exceptions and owner sign-off provide evidence that conversion was complete and accurate. Deleting legacy data before validation removes the ability to reconcile or recover.

questions.q: An internal auditor is invited to participate in a major system development project. To preserve objectivity, the auditor's role should be to:
choices: Serve as the project manager
Design and approve the application's controls
Write the system's code
Provide advice on control requirements and review the project's control processes without taking ownership of management decisions
questions.exp: Internal auditors can advise on controls during development but should not design or own controls or make management decisions, which would impair objectivity. Approving controls is a management responsibility.

questions.q: When a system reaches the end of its life, which activity is most important from a control standpoint in the disposal phase?
choices: Archiving data required for retention and sanitizing media according to guidance such as NIST SP 800-88
Throwing away documentation
Keeping the old servers running indefinitely
Selling the hardware as-is to recover costs
questions.exp: Disposal requires retaining records needed for legal or business reasons and sanitizing media to prevent data leakage. Selling unsanitized hardware risks exposing sensitive data.

questions.q: Six months after a new procurement system goes live, management compares actual benefits and costs to the original business case and identifies lessons learned. This is:
choices: A system design review
Unit testing
A feasibility study
A post-implementation review
questions.exp: A post-implementation review evaluates whether the project achieved its objectives and identifies lessons for future projects. A feasibility study occurs before the project is approved.

questions.q: Which approach builds working models quickly so users can see and react to a system's look and functionality before final requirements are set?
choices: Parallel conversion
Direct conversion
Prototyping
Waterfall
questions.exp: Prototyping creates preliminary versions for user feedback to refine requirements. Parallel and direct conversion are implementation approaches, not development methodologies.

questions.q: A key risk of rapid application development (RAD) and prototyping is that:
choices: Development takes too long
Requirements cannot change
Users are not involved enough
Prototypes may be put into production without adequate controls, documentation or testing
questions.exp: Pressure to deliver quickly may lead organizations to deploy prototypes that lack controls, testing and documentation. RAD typically increases user involvement and speeds development.

questions.q: In the waterfall model, which statement is most accurate?
choices: Each phase is completed and approved before the next begins, making later requirement changes costly
There is no documentation
Testing occurs before design
Phases overlap continuously and requirements change every sprint
questions.exp: Waterfall is sequential with formal phase gates, which provides control and documentation but makes late changes expensive. Continuous iteration describes agile.

questions.q: A project steering committee approves moving a project from design to development only after reviewing design documents, control requirements and security reviews. This mechanism is a:
choices: Change freeze
Code escrow
Phase gate (quality gate) review
Regression test
questions.exp: Phase or quality gates require formal review and approval before advancing, enforcing control over the project. A change freeze restricts production changes and is unrelated to project phase progression.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes technical debt in software development?
choices: The cost of software licenses purchased on credit
The implied future cost of rework caused by choosing expedient but suboptimal solutions now
Unpaid invoices to developers
The depreciation of hardware
questions.exp: Technical debt reflects shortcuts in design or code that create future maintenance costs and risks, including security weaknesses. It is not a financial liability recorded in the accounts.

questions.q: An organization's SDLC policy requires security and privacy requirements, threat modeling, and a privacy impact assessment for new systems processing personal data. When should the privacy impact assessment be performed?
choices: After the system has been in production for a year
During disposal
Only if a breach occurs
Early, during requirements and design, and updated as the system changes
questions.exp: Privacy impact assessments should be done early so privacy-by-design controls can be built in, and updated when changes occur. Performing them after deployment or only after a breach misses the opportunity to prevent issues.

questions.q: A development team performs threat modeling during design. What is its primary purpose?
choices: Testing performance under load
Estimating project costs
Training users
Identifying potential threats and attack paths to the system so that mitigating controls can be designed in
questions.exp: Threat modeling systematically identifies how a system could be attacked so controls can be designed proactively. It is not a performance or cost estimation activity.

questions.q: A company's SDLC requires that users receive training on a new system before go-live. Which risk does this primarily address?
choices: Hardware failures
Unauthorized program changes
Network intrusions
Errors and control failures caused by users not understanding how to use the system correctly
questions.exp: Training reduces user errors and helps ensure manual and IT-dependent controls are performed properly. It does not address program change control or infrastructure failures.

questions.q: Which document produced during the design phase specifies how the system will be built, including data structures, interfaces, processing logic and controls?
choices: Request for proposal
System design specification
Business case
Post-implementation review report
questions.exp: The system design specification translates requirements into a technical blueprint. The business case justifies the project and comes before design.

questions.q: A company's developers use open-source libraries extensively. Which control best addresses the risk of known vulnerabilities in these components?
choices: Prohibiting all open-source use
Allowing developers to choose any library without review
Maintaining a software bill of materials and using software composition analysis to identify vulnerable components
Reviewing libraries only after a breach
questions.exp: An SBOM and software composition analysis identify components and known vulnerabilities so they can be updated. A total ban is usually impractical, and post-breach review is too late.

questions.q: A system implementation runs significantly over budget. The steering committee considers whether to continue based on the money already spent. Which concept should guide its decision?
choices: Costs already incurred should be the primary factor
The project must be completed because it was approved
Only technical feasibility matters
Decisions should focus on future incremental costs and benefits, because costs already incurred are sunk
questions.exp: Sunk costs cannot be recovered and should not drive continuation decisions; only future costs and benefits are relevant. Continuing merely because money has been spent is the sunk cost fallacy.

questions.q: Which conversion method has the greatest risk but the lowest cost?
choices: Pilot conversion
Phased conversion
Parallel conversion
Direct (plunge) conversion
questions.exp: Direct conversion switches to the new system at once with no fallback, which is cheapest but riskiest. Parallel conversion is costliest because both systems run simultaneously.

questions.q: A company implements a new ERP one module at a time, starting with general ledger, then payables, then receivables. This approach is:
choices: Direct conversion
Pilot conversion
Parallel conversion
Phased conversion
questions.exp: Phased conversion introduces the system gradually by module or function. Pilot conversion implements the whole system at a limited location first, not module by module.

questions.q: During development, which practice best helps detect logic errors and security flaws before code is merged?
choices: Relying on end users to report problems
Deploying code to production to see if it works
Removing comments from code
Peer code review using a defined checklist, supported by automated analysis
questions.exp: Peer code review, ideally with checklists and automated tools, detects errors and vulnerabilities early. Relying on production use or end users detects issues only after they cause harm.

questions.q: A regional bank outsources its core deposit processing to a technology service provider. Bank management states that because the provider now runs the system, the provider is responsible for any regulatory compliance failures. What is the best response?
choices: Responsibility is shared equally by contract
The bank's regulators supervise only the provider, not the bank
Management is correct because outsourcing transfers regulatory responsibility
The bank retains accountability for the outsourced activity and must manage the third-party relationship as if it performed the activity itself
questions.exp: The 2023 interagency guidance on third-party relationships states that using a third party does not diminish the banking organization's responsibility to operate safely and in compliance with law. Outsourcing transfers execution, not accountability.

questions.q: A company with 600 vendors has limited staff to perform vendor risk assessments. Which approach is most effective?
choices: Assess vendors only after a security incident
Assess only the vendors with the largest annual spend
Tier vendors by inherent risk, such as criticality and access to sensitive data or systems, and scale due diligence and monitoring accordingly
Assess all vendors with the same detailed questionnaire every year
questions.exp: Risk-based tiering directs resources to vendors whose failure or compromise would have the greatest impact. Spend is a poor proxy for risk because a low-cost vendor may have privileged access to sensitive systems.

questions.q: A company is reviewing a prospective cloud payroll vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report before signing a contract. Which aspect should the company examine first to determine whether the report is relevant?
choices: The name of the CPA firm's engagement partner
The number of pages in the report
Whether the report includes a SOC 3 summary
Whether the report's scope, including the system described, Trust Services categories covered, and period, matches the services the company will use
questions.exp: A SOC report is useful only if it covers the system, services, categories, and period relevant to the user. A clean opinion on a different system or a stale period gives little assurance.

questions.q: A service auditor's SOC 2 Type 2 report lists several exceptions in testing of user access removal, but the opinion is unmodified. What should the user entity do?
choices: Terminate the vendor immediately
Request that the service auditor reissue the report without exceptions
Evaluate the nature and impact of the exceptions on its own risks, review management's response, and consider additional controls or follow-up with the vendor
Disregard the exceptions because the opinion is unmodified
questions.exp: Even with an unmodified opinion, testing exceptions can be significant to a particular user, so users should assess their relevance and the vendor's remediation. Exceptions are disclosed precisely so users can make this evaluation.

questions.q: A company needs assurance about a vendor's controls over the security and availability of a hosted CRM system, which does not affect financial reporting. Which report is most appropriate?
choices: SOC 2 Type 2 covering security and availability
An agreed-upon procedures report on the vendor's financial statements
SOC 1 Type 2
SOC 3
questions.exp: SOC 2 addresses controls relevant to the Trust Services categories such as security and availability, and Type 2 covers operating effectiveness over a period. SOC 1 addresses controls relevant to user entities' internal control over financial reporting.

questions.q: A vendor offers its SOC 3 report as evidence of its security controls. What is the primary limitation of a SOC 3 report for a customer's vendor risk assessment?
choices: It is a general-use summary that omits the detailed description of controls, tests performed, and results
It covers only financial reporting controls
It is always a Type 1 report
It is not issued by a CPA firm
questions.exp: A SOC 3 report provides the opinion and a summary for general use but omits the detailed control descriptions and test results needed for in-depth risk assessment. It is issued by a CPA firm under the same TSC as a SOC 2.

questions.q: A data analytics vendor stores a company's customer data in a cloud platform run by another provider and uses a third firm for customer support. What risk do these additional parties represent for the company?
choices: Market risk
Fourth-party (nth-party) risk arising from the vendor's own subcontractors
Credit risk
Concentration risk only
questions.exp: Fourth parties are the vendor's vendors, whose failures or breaches can affect the company even though it has no direct contract with them. Contracts should require disclosure and approval of subcontractors and flow-down of security obligations.

questions.q: Which contract provision best enables a company to verify a critical vendor's ongoing compliance with security obligations?
choices: A clause prohibiting the vendor from working with competitors
A clause requiring the vendor to use the company's logo
A clause fixing prices for five years
A right-to-audit clause permitting the company or its designee to assess the vendor's controls, or obtain independent assurance reports, periodically
questions.exp: A right-to-audit clause, often satisfied through SOC reports or onsite assessments, gives the company contractual means to obtain evidence about vendor controls. Without it, the company may have no leverage to obtain information after signing.

questions.q: A company's contract with a payment processor requires the processor to notify the company of security incidents 'promptly.' What is the most significant weakness?
choices: Notification should be required only after the processor completes its investigation
The clause should be removed because notification is the regulator's responsibility
The term is vague; the contract should specify a defined time frame, the information to be provided, and cooperation duties so the company can meet its own regulatory deadlines
Notification should be provided only to the company's external auditors
questions.exp: Vague terms can delay notice beyond regulatory deadlines such as GDPR's 72 hours or SEC disclosure timelines; contracts should set specific time frames and content. Waiting for the vendor to finish its investigation could take months.

questions.q: A company terminates its relationship with a marketing vendor that held customer data and had VPN access to the company's network. Which offboarding steps are most important?
choices: Revoking all vendor access and credentials promptly and obtaining certification that company data was returned or securely destroyed as the contract requires
Sending a thank-you letter
Retaining the vendor's VPN account in case the relationship resumes
Deleting the vendor from the accounts payable system only
questions.exp: Offboarding must remove access and confirm the disposition of company data, which are common gaps after termination. Leaving dormant vendor accounts active creates an easy entry point for attackers.

questions.q: A manufacturer allows its equipment vendor to connect remotely to plant control systems for maintenance. Which control set best manages the risk of this access?
choices: Always-on remote access so the vendor can respond quickly
A shared vendor password that never expires
A nondisclosure agreement signed by the vendor
Unique vendor accounts with multifactor authentication, access enabled only for approved maintenance windows, and session monitoring or recording
questions.exp: Third-party remote access should follow least privilege and just-in-time principles with strong authentication and monitoring. A shared, permanent account was the root cause of several well-known breaches involving vendors.

questions.q: Attackers inserted malicious code into a widely used IT monitoring product's software update, which was digitally signed and distributed to thousands of customers. Which control would best help a customer reduce the impact of such a software supply chain attack?
choices: Relying on the vendor's code signature as proof of safety
Limiting the privileges and network access of third-party software to only what it needs, and monitoring its behavior for anomalies
Disabling all software updates permanently
Requiring the vendor to sign a nondisclosure agreement
questions.exp: Because a compromised build can produce validly signed malware, customers should constrain and monitor third-party software rather than trust it implicitly. Disabling updates creates other vulnerabilities by leaving known flaws unpatched.

questions.q: A software company requires its vendors to provide a software bill of materials (SBOM). What is the primary benefit for the company?
choices: It replaces the need for vulnerability scanning
It reduces the license cost of the software
It provides an inventory of the components in the software, enabling the company to identify exposure quickly when a vulnerability is disclosed in a component
It certifies that the software contains no vulnerabilities
questions.exp: An SBOM lists the components and dependencies in software, so customers can determine quickly whether they are affected by newly disclosed vulnerabilities. It does not guarantee the components are free of vulnerabilities.

questions.q: A company relies on vendors' completed security questionnaires to assess risk. What is the main limitation of this approach?
choices: Questionnaires are too short to be useful
Questionnaire responses are self-reported and may not be validated, so higher-risk vendors require corroborating evidence such as independent assurance reports or testing
Questionnaires must be completed by the company's own auditors
Questionnaires cannot be used for cloud vendors
questions.exp: Self-assessments are useful for scoping but represent the vendor's assertions; critical vendors warrant independent evidence such as SOC 2 reports, certifications, or onsite reviews. Questionnaires are widely used for cloud vendors, including standardized ones like the CAIQ.

questions.q: A company's vendor provides an ISO/IEC 27001 certificate as evidence of its security. What should the company verify before relying on it?
choices: That the certificate's scope covers the specific services, locations, and systems the company uses, and that it is current and issued by an accredited certification body
That the certificate is printed on official letterhead
That the certificate was issued by the vendor's internal audit department
That the vendor has more than 1,000 employees
questions.exp: ISO 27001 certification applies to a defined scope of the information security management system, which may exclude the services a customer uses. Certification must come from an accredited, independent body, not the vendor's own staff.

questions.q: A bank discovers that 70% of its critical applications are hosted by a single cloud provider in one region. Which risk is most directly highlighted?
choices: Concentration risk
Credit risk
Fourth-party risk
Interest rate risk
questions.exp: Concentration risk arises when heavy reliance on a single provider or location means one failure can disrupt many critical services. Fourth-party risk concerns a vendor's subcontractors, not the bank's own dependence on one vendor.

questions.q: A company depends on a small software firm for a custom inventory application and does not have access to the source code. What contractual arrangement best protects the company if the software firm goes out of business?
choices: A clause requiring annual price reductions
A most-favored-customer pricing clause
A source code escrow agreement with defined release conditions, such as vendor bankruptcy or discontinued support
A noncompete clause
questions.exp: Source code escrow places the code with a neutral party that releases it to the customer under specified events, allowing continued maintenance. Pricing clauses do nothing if the vendor ceases to exist.

questions.q: During due diligence on a prospective critical vendor, which assessment is most relevant to the risk that the vendor will be unable to continue providing services?
choices: The vendor's financial condition and business continuity capabilities
The vendor's number of social media followers
The vendor's marketing materials
The vendor's office décor
questions.exp: Financial stability and tested continuity plans indicate whether the vendor can sustain services through financial stress or disruption. Marketing materials and public profile do not provide reliable evidence of resilience.

questions.q: A company's contract with a critical vendor contains no provisions for what happens at contract end. Which clause would best ensure an orderly transition to a new provider?
choices: A clause requiring the company to renew automatically
A clause prohibiting the company from switching vendors
Exit or termination assistance provisions requiring the vendor to support transition and return data in a usable format within a defined time
A confidentiality clause only
questions.exp: An exit strategy, including termination assistance and data return in usable formats, prevents lock-in and service disruption. Automatic renewal clauses do not address how to transition away when needed.

questions.q: A company subscribes to a service that continuously rates its vendors' external security posture by scanning their internet-facing systems. How should the company use these ratings?
choices: As one input to ongoing monitoring that can trigger follow-up when a vendor's rating deteriorates, supplementing deeper assessments
As proof that vendors comply with contractual obligations
As a complete replacement for all other due diligence
As a basis for terminating any vendor below the industry average
questions.exp: Outside-in security ratings provide timely signals but see only externally visible indicators, so they complement rather than replace assessments of internal controls. Automatic termination ignores context and the ability to remediate.

questions.q: A vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report uses the carve-out method for its colocation data center provider and lists complementary subservice organization controls (CSOCs). What should the user entity do?
choices: Assume the colocation provider's controls were tested by the service auditor
Determine how the vendor monitors the colocation provider, and consider obtaining the colocation provider's own SOC report if its controls are significant
Ignore the CSOCs because they are the vendor's concern
Request that the vendor change data centers
questions.exp: With the carve-out method, the subservice organization's controls were not tested in the vendor's report, so users need other evidence that the CSOCs operate. The inclusive method would have included those controls in testing.

questions.q: A vendor's SOC 2 report covers January 1 through June 30, and the company is evaluating the vendor in December. Which additional document should the company request?
choices: A SOC 1 Type 1 report
A bridge letter from vendor management describing any significant changes in controls since the report period
The vendor's tax return
The vendor's articles of incorporation
questions.exp: A bridge letter covers the gap between the report period end and the current date, providing management's representation about changes. It is not audited, so the company considers it along with other monitoring.

questions.q: A SOC 2 Type 2 report on a cloud vendor includes a qualified opinion because controls over change management were not operating effectively. How should a customer interpret this?
choices: The specified criteria related to change management were not met, so the customer should evaluate the impact on its risks and seek information about remediation
The vendor's entire control environment has failed
The qualification is irrelevant because the remaining controls were effective
The report is unusable and should be discarded
questions.exp: A qualified opinion means controls were effective except for the matter described, which the customer must assess in relation to its use of the service. An adverse opinion, not a qualified one, would indicate pervasive failures.

questions.q: A vendor management program requires all vendors to be reassessed every three years regardless of risk. What is the best recommendation?
choices: Reassess vendors only at contract renewal
Reassess all vendors monthly
Set reassessment frequency based on risk tier, with critical and high-risk vendors reviewed at least annually and upon significant changes or incidents
Eliminate reassessments for vendors with no prior incidents
questions.exp: Monitoring frequency should be commensurate with risk, with triggers for changes such as breaches, ownership changes, or new services. Monthly reassessment of every vendor would waste resources on low-risk relationships.

questions.q: A company is selecting a vendor that will process EU residents' personal data. Which contractual requirement is mandated by GDPR for this relationship?
choices: A guaranteed availability of 99.99%
A source code escrow agreement
An exclusivity clause
A data processing agreement specifying, among other things, that the vendor processes data only on documented instructions, ensures confidentiality, and assists with data subject requests
questions.exp: GDPR Article 28 requires a contract with processors setting out mandatory terms, including processing only on instructions and engaging sub-processors only with authorization. Availability guarantees and escrow are business choices, not GDPR mandates.

questions.q: A procurement analyst can create new vendors in the vendor master file and also approve payments to vendors. Which risk does this create?
choices: The risk of exceeding the vendor's SLA
Concentration risk
Fourth-party risk
The risk that a fictitious vendor could be created and paid without detection
questions.exp: Combining vendor setup and payment approval is a segregation of duties conflict that enables fictitious vendor fraud. Vendor master changes should be performed by someone independent of purchasing and payment, with review of changes.

questions.q: Which procedure provides the strongest validation when onboarding a new vendor into the accounts payable system?
choices: Accepting vendor information submitted by email
Relying on the requesting department's assurance
Verifying the vendor's legal existence and taxpayer identification number, and confirming bank account details through an independent channel before activation
Adding the vendor and verifying details after the first payment
questions.exp: Independent verification of identity, TIN, and bank details before payment prevents fictitious vendors and payment diversion. Verifying after the first payment allows a fraudulent payment to occur first.

questions.q: A cloud provider's shared responsibility matrix states that the customer is responsible for configuring access controls and encrypting data in its storage buckets. A customer's data is exposed because a bucket was publicly accessible. Who is primarily responsible?
choices: No one, because public cloud storage is inherently insecure
The CPA firm that issued the provider's SOC 2 report
The customer, because configuration of access to its data was its responsibility under the shared responsibility model
The cloud provider, because it hosts the data
questions.exp: Under the shared responsibility model, providers secure the underlying infrastructure while customers secure their configurations and data. Misconfiguration by customers is a leading cause of cloud data exposures.

questions.q: A company learns from news reports that a key SaaS vendor suffered a breach. Its contract requires notification within 48 hours, but the vendor has not contacted the company after five days. What should the company do first?
choices: Post a public statement blaming the vendor
Immediately file a lawsuit against the vendor
Wait for the vendor to make contact
Contact the vendor through established channels to determine whether its data was affected, invoke contractual notification and cooperation provisions, and activate its own incident response process
questions.exp: The company must determine its exposure quickly to meet its own obligations, using contractual rights and its incident response plan. Waiting passively may cause it to miss regulatory deadlines.

questions.q: A company engages a vendor that will host sensitive customer data. Before signing, the company asks for the vendor's most recent penetration test results. What is the most appropriate way to use this information?
choices: To publish the findings on the company's website
To evaluate the scope and independence of the testing, the severity of findings, and whether remediation was completed
To replace the need for a SOC 2 report
To confirm that no vulnerabilities exist in the vendor's environment
questions.exp: A penetration test summary is useful when the company understands what was tested, by whom, and whether critical findings were fixed. No test proves that vulnerabilities do not exist.

questions.q: A company's vendor inventory is incomplete because business units sign agreements with service providers without involving procurement. What is the most effective corrective action?
choices: Establish a policy and process requiring all third-party engagements to go through a central intake and risk assessment, supported by accounts payable controls that block payments to unregistered vendors
Allow business units to continue but require them to notify IT within one year
Hire more vendor risk analysts
Ask business units annually whether they have new vendors
questions.exp: Centralized intake tied to payment controls ensures that third parties cannot be engaged and paid without entering the risk management process. Annual surveys rely on voluntary reporting and leave long gaps.

questions.q: A company's contract with a data center provider includes SLAs with service credits for downtime. Management considers the SLA sufficient protection against outages. What is the main limitation?
choices: SLAs apply only to software vendors
SLAs are not legally enforceable
Service credits must be paid by the company to the provider
Service credits typically compensate only a small fraction of the fee and do not cover the company's business losses, so continuity planning is still required
questions.exp: Service credits are usually capped at a percentage of fees, far less than the cost of lost business, so they do not substitute for redundancy or continuity planning. SLAs are generally enforceable contract terms.

questions.q: Why should a user entity care about complementary user entity controls (CUECs) listed in a vendor's SOC 2 report?
choices: CUECs are optional suggestions with no effect on the report
CUECs are controls the vendor plans to implement next year
CUECs are controls the service auditor failed to test
The vendor's control objectives or criteria are met only if the user entity also implements the CUECs, such as reviewing user access it administers
questions.exp: The vendor's system is designed assuming user entities perform certain controls; if they do not, the criteria may not be achieved for that user. CUECs are not testing gaps or future plans.

questions.q: A healthcare company's vendor risk assessment of a new transcription service reveals that the service will store PHI. Which element must be in place before the vendor receives PHI?
choices: A noncompete agreement
A HIPAA business associate agreement
A source code escrow agreement
A SOC 1 Type 2 report
questions.exp: HIPAA requires a business associate agreement before a vendor creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on a covered entity's behalf. A SOC 1 report addresses financial reporting controls and is not a HIPAA requirement.

questions.q: A company relies on an open-source software library maintained by a single volunteer. Which risk is most relevant from a third-party perspective?
choices: The library carries no risk because it is free
Vulnerabilities may go unpatched or the project may be abandoned, so the company should monitor the component and have a contingency plan
The library will automatically comply with all regulations
The library cannot be scanned for vulnerabilities
questions.exp: Open-source components are third-party code without a contractual support obligation, so maintenance and security depend on the community. Free software still introduces supply chain risk, as incidents like Log4Shell demonstrated.

questions.q: A vendor risk team discovers that a vendor's SOC 2 report excludes the specific data center where the company's data is hosted. What is the most appropriate next step?
choices: Request additional evidence covering that location, such as a separate assurance report or other testing, before relying on the vendor's controls
Disregard the vendor's controls entirely and terminate the contract
Ask the CPA firm to amend the report to include the data center
Accept the report because it covers the vendor's other data centers
questions.exp: When the scope of a report excludes relevant systems or locations, the user needs other evidence to address those risks. A CPA firm cannot simply amend a report to cover locations it did not examine.

questions.q: Which metric would best indicate the effectiveness of a company's third-party risk management program?
choices: The percentage of critical vendors with current risk assessments and the time to remediate significant vendor findings
The total number of vendors
The number of vendors located in the company's home state
The average invoice amount per vendor
questions.exp: Coverage of critical vendors and timely remediation of findings show whether the program is managing the highest risks. Vendor counts and invoice sizes describe the portfolio, not risk management performance.

questions.q: A vendor has asked to subcontract part of its work, which involves access to the company's customer data, to an offshore firm. What should the company's contract require?
choices: Prior notice and approval of subcontractors handling company data, with flow-down of the same security and privacy obligations
That the subcontractor be paid directly by the company
Nothing, because subcontracting is the vendor's business decision
That the subcontractor be located in the same city as the company
questions.exp: Contracts should give the company visibility and approval rights over subcontractors that handle its data, and require equivalent obligations to flow down. Without this, the company's data may move to parties it has never assessed.

questions.q: A SaaS provider engages a CPA for a SOC 2 examination and wants to limit scope to the availability category only. How should the practitioner respond?
choices: Accept, because management may select any single category
Explain that the security category (common criteria) is always included in a SOC 2 examination
Accept, but issue a SOC 3 report instead
Decline, because availability can only be reported with processing integrity
questions.exp: The common criteria (CC1-CC9) form the security category and apply to every SOC 2 examination; additional categories such as availability add their own criteria. Management selects additional categories, but cannot drop security.

questions.q: A data analytics firm holds clients' unreleased merger plans and pricing strategies, none of which involves information about individuals. Which trust services category most directly addresses protecting this information as committed?
choices: Confidentiality
Processing integrity
Availability
Privacy
questions.exp: Confidentiality addresses protecting information designated as confidential, such as business plans and intellectual property, consistent with commitments. Privacy applies only to personal information about individuals, which is not involved here.

questions.q: A payment processor commits to customers that transactions will be processed completely, accurately, timely and only when authorized. Which trust services category most directly addresses this commitment?
choices: Confidentiality
Processing integrity
Security
Availability
questions.exp: Processing integrity addresses whether system processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely and authorized to meet objectives. Security protects against unauthorized access and damage but does not by itself address the accuracy of processing.

questions.q: Under the 2017 trust services criteria, which statement about points of focus is correct?
choices: Points of focus describe important characteristics of a criterion but are not requirements; an entity may meet a criterion without addressing every point of focus
Points of focus replace the criteria for service organizations under 100 employees
Every point of focus must be met or the related criterion is not met
Points of focus are required only for the privacy category
questions.exp: Points of focus (revised in 2022) help management and practitioners design, implement and evaluate controls, but they are not individually required. The criteria are what must be met, which is why treating every point of focus as mandatory is a trap.

questions.q: The common criteria CC1 through CC5 of the 2017 trust services criteria are organized around:
choices: The 17 principles of the COSO 2013 Internal Control framework
The ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A control themes
The five functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework
The 40 COBIT 2019 governance and management objectives
questions.exp: CC1-CC5 align to the COSO 2013 components and 17 principles (control environment, communication and information, risk assessment, monitoring and control activities). CC6-CC9 add criteria specific to logical and physical access, operations, change management and risk mitigation.

questions.q: A service organization ensures that disk drives are degaussed before decommissioned servers are sent to a recycler. Which common criterion does this control most directly address?
choices: CC8.1, managing changes to infrastructure
CC2.3, communicating with external parties
CC6.5, discontinuing protections over physical assets only after the ability to read or recover data has been diminished
CC7.2, monitoring system components for anomalies
questions.exp: CC6.5 addresses secure disposal so data cannot be recovered from physical assets once protections are removed. CC8.1 concerns authorizing and testing changes, not decommissioning media.

questions.q: A cloud provider maintains geographically separate backup sites and periodically performs full failover tests of its recovery plan. Which trust services category's additional criteria most directly cover these controls?
choices: Availability
Confidentiality
Processing integrity
Privacy
questions.exp: Availability criteria A1.2 and A1.3 address backup, recovery infrastructure and testing of recovery plan procedures. Processing integrity is concerned with complete, accurate processing, not the ability to recover service.

questions.q: A company monitors CPU, storage and network utilization and forecasts demand so it can add capacity before customers experience degradation. Which criterion does this most directly support?
choices: C1.1, identifying confidential information
CC6.1, logical access security software
PI1.3, system processing
A1.1, managing processing capacity to meet demand
questions.exp: A1.1 requires the entity to maintain, monitor and evaluate current processing capacity and use to manage capacity demand. PI1.3 concerns whether processing is complete and accurate, not whether capacity is sufficient.

questions.q: A company's intrusion detection system flags an anomalous login pattern. A security analyst then evaluates whether the event is a security incident that could result in failure to meet objectives. Which common criterion does the analyst's evaluation most directly address?
choices: CC7.1
CC7.3
CC7.5
CC9.2
questions.exp: CC7.3 addresses evaluating security events to determine whether they could or have resulted in a failure to meet objectives (i.e., incidents). CC7.5 concerns recovering from identified incidents, which comes later.

questions.q: After a ransomware incident is contained, the company restores affected systems from clean backups, communicates with affected customers, and implements changes to prevent recurrence. Which common criterion most directly covers these activities?
choices: CC3.1, specifying objectives
CC7.2, monitoring system components
CC7.5, recovering from identified security incidents
CC6.2, registering new users
questions.exp: CC7.5 addresses identifying, developing and implementing activities to recover from security incidents, including restoration and remediation. CC7.2 concerns detecting anomalies before an incident is identified.

questions.q: Which control best addresses CC7.1, which requires the entity to identify configuration changes that introduce new vulnerabilities and susceptibilities to newly discovered vulnerabilities?
choices: Encrypting data in transit with TLS
Annual security awareness training for all employees
Periodic vulnerability scanning and configuration monitoring against approved baselines
Physical badge readers on data center doors
questions.exp: CC7.1 points of focus include configuration standards, monitoring infrastructure for changes, and conducting vulnerability scans. Training and encryption address other criteria (CC2.2 and CC6.7 respectively).

questions.q: A company requires all customer data sent to external partners to travel over encrypted channels and blocks unauthorized USB storage devices. Which criterion does this most directly support?
choices: CC6.8, malicious software prevention
CC5.3, policies and procedures
CC6.3, role-based access
CC6.7, restricting the transmission, movement and removal of information
questions.exp: CC6.7 addresses restricting the transmission, movement and removal of information to authorized users and protecting it during transmission. CC6.8 addresses unauthorized or malicious software rather than data movement.

questions.q: A company deploys endpoint detection and response software and allows only approved applications to execute on servers. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC8.1, change management
CC6.6, protecting against threats from outside system boundaries
CC6.8, preventing or detecting and acting on unauthorized or malicious software
A1.2, environmental protections
questions.exp: CC6.8 addresses controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorized or malicious software, such as EDR and application allowlisting. CC6.6 focuses on boundary protection such as firewalls and secure remote access.

questions.q: A service organization's firewall rules restrict inbound traffic, and remote administrative access requires a VPN with multi-factor authentication. Which criterion does this most directly support?
choices: CC6.6, implementing logical access security measures against threats from sources outside system boundaries
CC6.4, restricting physical access
PI1.2, system inputs
CC1.4, attracting and retaining competent individuals
questions.exp: CC6.6 covers boundary protection, such as firewalls and secured remote access, against external threats. CC6.4 is limited to physical access to facilities and protected assets.

questions.q: Which control best addresses CC6.2, which concerns registering and authorizing new internal and external users before issuing system credentials?
choices: Requiring an approved access request from the user's manager before an account is created
Quarterly review of firewall logs
Automatic screen lock after 10 minutes of inactivity
Encrypting backup tapes
questions.exp: CC6.2 is about authorizing users before granting credentials, which a manager-approved access request directly addresses. Screen locks are a session control and do not address the registration and authorization of users.

questions.q: A company performs quarterly reviews in which managers confirm that each subordinate's access remains appropriate for the job, and access is removed for role changes. Which criterion is most directly supported?
choices: CC6.3, authorizing, modifying or removing access based on roles, least privilege and segregation of duties
CC7.4, responding to security incidents
C1.2, disposing of confidential information
CC2.1, generating quality information
questions.exp: CC6.3 covers role-based access, modifying and removing access, and least privilege and segregation of duties. Incident response under CC7.4 does not address periodic recertification of access rights.

questions.q: A company requires that all production code changes be authorized, tested, approved and documented before implementation, including emergency changes. Which criterion is addressed?
choices: CC7.3
CC8.1
CC5.1
CC9.1
questions.exp: CC8.1 addresses authorizing, designing, developing, configuring, documenting, testing, approving and implementing changes to infrastructure, data, software and procedures. CC5.1 is the COSO-based criterion on selecting control activities generally.

questions.q: A service organization purchases cyber insurance and has business continuity plans to mitigate the impact of potential business disruptions. Which criterion most directly addresses these activities?
choices: CC9.1, identifying, selecting and developing risk mitigation activities for risks from potential business disruptions
CC9.2, managing vendor and business partner risk
A1.1, managing capacity
CC3.4, assessing changes that could affect internal control
questions.exp: CC9.1 covers risk mitigation for business disruptions, and its points of focus include considering insurance to offset the financial impact of loss events. CC9.2 addresses risks associated with vendors and business partners specifically.

questions.q: A service organization obtains SOC 2 reports from its critical subprocessors, reviews them annually, and includes security requirements in vendor contracts. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC2.3
CC9.1
CC9.2
CC4.2
questions.exp: CC9.2 requires the entity to assess and manage risks associated with vendors and business partners. CC2.3 addresses communication with external parties, which is part of vendor management but not its core risk assessment and monitoring.

questions.q: Under the privacy category, a company provides individuals with a notice describing what personal information it collects, how it is used, and how long it is retained. Which privacy criterion does this support?
choices: P5.1, access
P8.1, monitoring and enforcement
P1.1, notice
P7.1, quality
questions.exp: P1.1 requires the entity to provide notice to data subjects about its privacy practices. P5.1 addresses giving individuals access to their personal information, which is a separate commitment.

questions.q: A customer asks an online retailer to correct an inaccurate shipping address and to show what personal information the retailer holds about her. Which privacy criteria are most directly involved?
choices: P4.2 and P4.3
P2.1 and P3.1
P6.1 and P6.2
P5.1 and P5.2
questions.exp: P5.1 addresses granting data subjects access to their personal information and P5.2 addresses correcting, amending or appending it. P4.2 and P4.3 concern retention and disposal, not individual access.

questions.q: A company collects health information from customers only after obtaining their explicit consent, because the information is considered sensitive. Which privacy criterion does this most directly address?
questions.exp: P3.2 requires explicit consent for the collection of personal information when explicit consent is required, such as for sensitive information. P1.1 concerns notice, which differs from obtaining explicit consent.

questions.q: After a breach of customer personal information, a company notifies affected individuals and regulators as required by its commitments and applicable laws. Which privacy criterion does this most directly support?
choices: P8.1, handling inquiries and complaints
P2.1, choice and consent
P4.1, use of personal information
P6.6, notifying affected data subjects, regulators and others of breaches and incidents
questions.exp: P6.6 addresses providing notification of breaches and incidents to affected data subjects, regulators and others. P8.1 concerns handling privacy inquiries, complaints and disputes, not breach notification.

questions.q: A company's policy states that personal information will be deleted 24 months after an account is closed, and an automated job purges such records. Which privacy criteria are most directly addressed?
choices: P6.1 and P6.4
P1.1 and P2.1
P4.2 and P4.3
P5.1 and P5.2
questions.exp: P4.2 addresses retention of personal information and P4.3 addresses its secure disposal. Access and correction (P5) concern individuals' rights to view and fix data, not retention schedules.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes availability from processing integrity under the trust services criteria?
choices: Both categories address only physical security
Availability addresses data accuracy; processing integrity addresses uptime
Availability sets minimum acceptable performance levels that all entities must meet
Availability addresses whether systems are accessible for operation and use as committed; processing integrity addresses whether processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely and authorized
questions.exp: Availability concerns accessibility for operation and use as committed or agreed, while processing integrity concerns the quality of processing. The TSC explicitly state that availability does not itself set a minimum acceptable performance level.

questions.q: In SOC 2 reporting, the trust services criteria are applied in relation to the service organization's:
choices: Service commitments and system requirements
Control objectives selected by the user auditor
Industry benchmarks set by the AICPA
Financial statement assertions
questions.exp: The SOC 2 opinion addresses whether controls provide reasonable assurance that the service organization's service commitments and system requirements were achieved based on the applicable TSC. Financial statement assertions relate to SOC 1 and financial audits.

questions.q: A company identifies all confidential client information it holds, labels it by classification, and restricts its storage to approved repositories. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: PI1.5
questions.exp: C1.1 requires the entity to identify and maintain confidential information to meet confidentiality objectives. C1.2 addresses disposing of confidential information, which is a later stage in its lifecycle.

questions.q: A payroll processor compares control totals of input batches to totals of processed output and investigates differences before releasing pay files. Which criteria are most directly addressed?
choices: CC6.1 and CC6.2
PI1.3 and PI1.4
C1.1 and C1.2
A1.1 and A1.2
questions.exp: PI1.3 addresses complete and accurate system processing and PI1.4 addresses complete, accurate and timely outputs; control total reconciliations support both. Availability criteria (A1) do not address the accuracy of processing.

questions.q: A company documents definitions of the data it processes and the specifications of its services, and communicates them to users. Which processing integrity criterion is most directly supported?
choices: CC8.1
PI1.5
PI1.2
PI1.1
questions.exp: PI1.1 requires the entity to obtain or generate, use and communicate relevant, quality information about processing objectives, including data definitions and product and service specifications. PI1.2 addresses controls over system inputs.

questions.q: A board of directors oversees the development and performance of internal control and includes members independent of management. Which common criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC4.1
CC6.1
CC3.2
CC1.2
questions.exp: CC1.2 (COSO Principle 2) states that the board demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of internal control. CC4.1 concerns performing ongoing and separate evaluations, which is a monitoring activity.

questions.q: A service organization identifies risks to achieving its service commitments, including threats from vendors and new technologies, and analyzes their likelihood and impact. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC5.2, selecting general controls over technology
CC7.4, responding to incidents
CC2.2, internal communication
CC3.2, identifying and analyzing risk to the achievement of objectives
questions.exp: CC3.2 (COSO Principle 7) addresses identifying and analyzing risks, and its points of focus include threats from vendors and technology. CC5.2 concerns selecting technology general controls once risks are known.

questions.q: Management considers the potential for fraud, including unauthorized access to systems by employees attempting to manipulate customer data, when assessing risks. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC2.1
CC1.1
CC3.3
CC4.2
questions.exp: CC3.3 (COSO Principle 8) requires the entity to consider the potential for fraud in assessing risks. CC1.1 addresses commitment to integrity and ethical values, which is part of the control environment, not risk assessment.

questions.q: Internal audit periodically tests the operating effectiveness of security controls and reports deficiencies to management and the board, which track remediation. Which criteria are most directly addressed?
choices: CC4.1 and CC4.2
CC6.4 and CC6.5
CC1.3 and CC1.4
CC8.1 and CC9.1
questions.exp: CC4.1 addresses ongoing and separate evaluations, and CC4.2 addresses evaluating and communicating internal control deficiencies timely. These are the monitoring activities criteria derived from COSO Principles 16 and 17.

questions.q: A company publishes a customer-facing portal that describes its security commitments and provides a way for customers to report suspected security incidents. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC2.2, communicating internally
CC2.3, communicating with external parties
CC7.1, detecting vulnerabilities
CC5.3, deploying policies and procedures
questions.exp: CC2.3 addresses communication with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control, including commitments and channels to report incidents. CC2.2 is limited to internal communication with personnel.

questions.q: Which situation best illustrates a SOC 2 privacy category commitment rather than a confidentiality commitment?
choices: Protecting a client's proprietary source code from disclosure
Encrypting a client's unreleased financial forecasts
Limiting use of customers' names and email addresses to the purposes disclosed in the privacy notice
Destroying a client's trade secrets at contract termination
questions.exp: Privacy criteria address the collection, use, retention, disclosure and disposal of personal information in line with the entity's notice and commitments. Source code, forecasts and trade secrets are confidential business information covered by the confidentiality category.

questions.q: A service organization maintains UPS units, fire suppression and climate controls in its data center to keep systems running. These controls are most directly relevant to which criterion?
choices: PI1.4
CC6.2
questions.exp: A1.2 addresses environmental protections, software, data backup and recovery infrastructure needed to meet availability commitments. CC6.2 addresses registering and authorizing users, not environmental safeguards.

questions.q: A company shares customer personal information with a marketing partner only after obtaining consent and requires the partner contractually to protect the information consistent with the company's privacy commitments. Which privacy criteria are most directly addressed?
choices: P3.1 and P3.2
P7.1 and P8.1
P6.1 and P6.4
P5.1 and P5.2
questions.exp: P6.1 addresses disclosing personal information to third parties with consent, and P6.4 addresses obtaining privacy commitments from vendors and other third parties. P3 criteria concern collection, not onward disclosure.

questions.q: A company's code of conduct requires employees to annually acknowledge standards of integrity and ethical behavior, and violations are addressed through a disciplinary process. Which criterion is most directly addressed?
choices: CC5.1, selecting control activities
CC3.1, specifying objectives
CC1.5, holding individuals accountable
CC1.1, demonstrating commitment to integrity and ethical values
questions.exp: CC1.1 (COSO Principle 1) is about commitment to integrity and ethical values, including standards of conduct and addressing deviations. CC1.5 concerns accountability for internal control responsibilities more broadly, such as performance measures and incentives.
